title: Comments must not assert facts that live outside their file unless the assertion is executable
description:
## The failure mode

Agent-authored comments routinely assert things about code, state, or issues OUTSIDE the file
they live in. Nothing checks those claims, so they decay silently and are then read as
authoritative by the next agent or operator. This is not hypothetical: five instances were
found in a single session (2026-08-17), and one of them caused a wrong diagnosis to be
reported to the operator before the code was checked.

Comments that explain WHY a local line is the way it is do not rot this way — their subject is
in the same file, so a change that invalidates them is in the same diff.

## Evidence (all verified 2026-08-17)

1. `vinlab-gitops` `clusters/vinlab/base/vantageex-app/configmap.yaml` header: "no epic/workflow
   dispatch reaches a real Runex worker from this cluster." FALSE. `RunexUrlResolver.resolve/1`
   (`vantageex lib/vantageex/execution/runex_url_resolver.ex`) consults `:runex_url_overrides`
   as arm 0, before every other arm, for any healthy registered node — `RUNEX_URL` is never read
   on that path. The comment was true when written and outlived the override arm (VIN-478 /
   infra-150). An agent (and the operator) were misled by it in-session.

2. `vantageex config/runtime.exs:399-409`: "See vantageex-733 — fix that before any soak."
   `vantageex-733` was closed 2026-07-30 (PR #655). This is the WORST class: not merely stale,
   it actively instructs an operator not to enable `REAPER_USE_CHANNEL_LIVENESS`, citing a
   resolved issue. A comment causing inaction today.

3. `vantageex lib/vantageex/workers/epic_picker_worker.ex`, pre-#677: "FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
   prevents TOCTOU race conditions." Ceased to be true when the wrapping transaction was
   removed. (Correctly rewritten in #677 — cited as the good case.)

4. `vantage_ex` ADR-062, ADR-102 (x2), ADR-109, flow-epic-dispatch-full-chain.jsx,
   flow-node-clustering.jsx (x2): all describe `SingletonLock` protecting cron workers it has
   not guarded since #677. Already filed as `vantage_ex-78`.

5. `vantageex-824`'s own issue text asserted prod ran `1cb42a54` and that Mini's liveness
   producer was absent. Both wrong — corrected in a comment 2026-08-17. Tracker prose rots
   identically to code comments.

## The rule to codify

A comment may not assert a fact that lives outside its own file unless that assertion is
executable. If the fact is load-bearing, express it as a test, a boot-time assertion, or a
`@moduledoc` on the module the fact is actually about — not as prose in a distant file.

Corollaries:
- **No issue IDs in code comments — not as constraints, not as provenance.** Provenance already lives in the commit message and PR, which `git blame` surfaces losslessly and which cannot drift from the line they describe. An ID in a comment is a second, unverifiable copy: it means nothing to a reader without tracker access, it cannot be checked from the file it sits in, and it survives the tracker itself (the beads→bees migration would have orphaned every `bd-NNN` reference had any been in code). It is the same outside-file-assertion class as the rest of this rule, not an exception to it.
- Do not describe another module's guarantees. Describe your own call site's assumptions, or
  assert them.
- Environment/deployment claims in manifests ("nothing reaches Z from this cluster") are the
  highest-risk shape: they summarize emergent behavior across many files and no single change
  invalidates them visibly.

## Scale of the habit (measured 2026-08-17, vantageex origin/main, lib/ + config/ only)

| Pattern | Hits |
|---|---|
| `vantageex-NNN` | 262 |
| `VIN-NNN` | 156 |
| `github-NNN` | 40 |
| `runex-NNN` | 14 |
| `bd-NNN` (retired tracker) | 0 |

472 references total. `bd-NNN` at zero is the tell that this is survivable to clean: the
beads→bees migration did not leave orphans in code, so the cleanup precedent exists.

These are NOT all equal and a sweep must not treat them as one bucket. Triage by what the
reference is doing in the sentence:

- An ID that is the ONLY explanation ("vantageex-562: rollback-safety fix only") — the comment
  is a pointer, not an explanation. Replace with the actual reason, in words. This is the
  common case and the whole problem: the ID stands in for knowledge that was never written down.
- An ID decorating a real explanation ("host-targeted liveness probe. host defaults to
  localhost (vantageex-572)") — the sentence survives deletion of the parenthetical. Drop the
  parenthetical, keep the sentence.
- An ID naming a live constraint ("fix vantageex-733 before any soak") — highest priority.
  Delete, and if the constraint is real, make it executable.

Related operator rule already on record: private refs (VIN/ADR/github-NNN) must not appear in
public artifacts. Keeping them out of code comments entirely satisfies that by construction
rather than by remembering to strip them per-repo.

## Three dispositions, not one

A blind deletion pass would destroy real knowledge. Classify each finding:

- DELETE — restates what the code plainly does, or asserts something now false and worthless.
- CORRECT — still broadly true, wrong in detail.
- PROMOTE — load-bearing and outside-file. Make it executable (test / assertion), then delete
  the prose.

Explicit counter-example that must SURVIVE any sweep: the `restraint:` comment at
`vantageex lib/vantageex/workers/epic_picker_worker.ex:1344-1354`, documenting that
`WorkerRegistry` is keyed on the raw JWT `sub` while `agent_label` is a canonicalised hostname,
so a case or `.local` mismatch silently disables the reaper's liveness veto. Nobody would
rediscover that without reading both sides. It is worth more than the code near it. A sweep
that deletes comments like this one is a net loss.

## Acceptance criteria

- The rule above lands in the appropriate core skill (candidates: `/core:documentation`,
  `/core:anti-fabrication`, `/core:code-review`) — pick one home, cross-reference from the
  others rather than duplicating.
- `/core:code-review`'s checklist gains an item: does any comment in this diff assert an
  outside-file fact? If yes, is it executable or provably current?
- Investigate a cheap detection pass. Two mechanically checkable shapes to start:
  (a) comments citing an issue ID whose tracker state is closed;
  (b) comments citing `file:line` or a module name, where the cited target no longer exists.
  Both are greppable and cross-checkable without judgement. Semantic claims ("nothing reaches Z")
  are NOT mechanically detectable — do not pretend otherwise; those need review-time attention,
  which is why the checklist item above matters.
- Prioritize remediation by blast radius, not by count. Comments that instruct an operator
  (item 2) outrank comments that merely describe (item 3).

## Not in scope

A sweep of the 472-reference cleanup across vantageex `lib/` and `config/`, plus whatever the
same measurement finds in `test/`, `runex`, and the bundle repos (runex-workflows, vantageex
bundles). That is separate, needs operator sign-off on scope, and must apply the three
dispositions above rather than deleting indiscriminately.

title: A negative or empty command result is unverified until you confirm the command's context
description:
FOUR wrong statements in one session, all the same shape: a command returned empty or "not found",
that result was read as a fact about the world, and it was actually a fact about the command's
CONTEXT.

The instances:
1. Lead ran `git fetch origin <branch>` and `git log origin/main` with a stale shell cwd left over
   from an earlier `cd`, and reported to the operator that a feature branch had been DELETED from
   the remote. It had not — the commands were querying a different repository entirely.
2. Lead ran a compound `... && echo "attribution: $(git log ... | grep -c ...)"` where the `git log`
   failed on an unfetched ref. The `grep -c` returned 0, which printed as "0 attribution hits" — a
   clean bill of health produced by a command that never ran.
3. A bees-manager ran `bees show <id>` from the wrong repo (vantageex vs vantage_ex — different
   DBs, different issue prefixes) and got "issue not found" for an issue that exists.
4. Lead ran a `for spec in "repo num"` loop under zsh, which does NOT word-split unquoted variables
   the way bash does, so the whole string was passed as one argument and every call errored.

WHY THIS CLASS IS DANGEROUS SPECIFICALLY: we act on negatives. "No attribution found", "no leaks
found", "the branch is gone", "that issue doesn't exist", "no callers of this function", "the guard
isn't set anywhere" — these are the results that authorize a merge, close an issue, or justify a
deletion. A false positive gets caught by the next step; a false negative closes the question.

THE RULE, for the anti-fabrication and agent-loop skills:

  Before reporting or acting on an EMPTY or NEGATIVE result, verify the command actually ran in the
  context you assumed. Concretely: confirm the working directory, confirm the ref was fetched,
  confirm the exit code was 0 rather than an error whose output happened to look like a clean
  result, and confirm the shell split arguments the way you expected.

  A command that errors and a command that finds nothing frequently produce identical-looking
  output — especially through a pipe to `grep -c`, `wc -l`, or `|| echo`, all of which convert an
  error into a plausible zero.

PRACTICAL FORMS:
- Prefer absolute paths (`git -C <path>`) over relying on cwd. The Bash tool's working directory
  persists between calls, so a `cd` three calls ago is still in effect.
- Never let an error path silently become a count. `cmd | grep -c x` prints 0 whether cmd found
  nothing or failed to run; check the exit code separately or print the raw output.
- zsh is not bash: unquoted `$var` is NOT word-split. Loops written from bash habit fail silently
  or pass whole strings as single arguments.
- When a negative is load-bearing, run a positive control — a query you KNOW should return
  something. If the control also returns empty, your context is wrong, not the world.

Related: claude-skills-280 covers claims relayed FROM others without provenance. This is the
inverse and arguably more insidious — your OWN tool output misleading you, with no intermediary
to blame.

title: Verify pre-packaged facts before relaying them into a brief
description:
On 2026-08-16 a single multi-agent session produced FOUR wrong claims that each cost a downstream
cycle. Every one shared a signature, and it is not the signature you would guess.

The four:
1. Lead relayed "worker_channel_client_test.exs:496-507 pins the old ?token= URL shape" into a work
   brief. It does not — those lines are the open_terminal test, and the only ?token= in the entire
   suite is an unrelated fixture. No test needed rework. Came from a research pass.
2. Lead relayed "auth_token: true works nested under websocket: or at the top level" into a work
   brief. Only top-level works; Phoenix's put_auth_token/2 unconditionally overwrites the nested
   value with nil, making the feature compile-time dead. Came from the same research pass. Cost:
   an implementation, a test that pinned the broken form, and two independent Gate 2 dev-verifies
   to rediscover.
3. A sub-team leader relayed "Phoenix 1.7.21" from its verifier's report. Both trees pin 1.8.5.
4. Lead filed a tracker issue calling for an audit of `eyJ`-keyed redaction across a repo whose
   shipped code contains zero instances of the pattern — the pattern existed only in the lead's own
   agent brief. The audit would have returned empty and read as a clean bill of health.

THE TELL IS NOT "THE CLAIM WAS SMALL." It is that the claim arrived ALREADY FORMATTED AS A FACT —
a file:line, a version string, a config spelling — from a prior agent or research pass. Stated by
the sub-team leader who diagnosed it: "A claim I derive myself I naturally check; a claim handed to
me in a brief reads as settled." In case 2 the relaying agent independently verified the HARD claim
(the macro mechanism) in the same message where it passed through the EASY one unchecked. Checking
the hard claim and trusting the easy one is exactly backwards, because the easy one is the one that
looks like it needs no checking.

THE RULE, for the agent-loop and anti-fabrication skills:

  Anything entering an Agent brief as a file:line citation, a version string, or an exact config
  spelling gets ONE confirming tool call before it is passed on — regardless of how authoritative
  the source agent seemed, and especially when it seems too small to be worth checking. A citation
  relayed unverified becomes an instruction, and downstream agents will implement against it.

Cheap to apply: a single Read or grep per relayed citation. Compare against the cost above.

Related: claude-skills-279 covers the adjacent rule that review gates cannot validate config
semantics — only execution can. These two compound: an unverified config spelling entering a brief,
which no review layer can refute by reading, is how case 2 reached production-shaped code.

comments.text:
SHARPER FRAMING, from the sub-team leader who diagnosed the failure mode in itself. Better than the
wording in this issue's description; prefer it when the rule reaches a skill.

  "A claim's weight comes from who VERIFIED it, not who SENT it — and passing through a senior
   intermediary strips the provenance while adding false authority."

That is more precise than "already formatted as a fact," and it explains the mechanism the original
framing only described. A claim arrives with two properties that are easy to conflate: how well
evidenced it is, and how authoritative its sender seems. Relaying preserves the second and destroys
the first. Each hop makes a claim sound MORE settled while making it LESS traceable.

A concrete instance from the same session, involving the agent that authored the framing:
it had personally verified that POST /admin/api/worker-tokens/request has zero callers across runex
lib/, config/, and bundles/ — so a per-worker-token objective was out of scope for its PR. Later,
"team-lead flagged this gap" reached it RELAYED THROUGH a third agent, and it dispatched a
verification cycle without checking the relayed claim against its own prior finding. The claim was
weaker evidence than what it already held, and the relay made it feel stronger.

Practical form of the rule, extending the description's one-tool-call requirement:
- When relaying a citation, carry HOW it was verified, not just the citation. "file:line, confirmed
  by Read" and "file:line, per an earlier agent" are different claims and must not look identical.
- When RECEIVING a relayed claim, check it against what you already verified yourself before acting.
  Your own prior finding outranks a relayed one, whatever the sender's position.
- Seniority of the sender is not evidence. A lead relaying an unverified claim is transmitting an
  unverified claim.

title: Review gates cannot validate config semantics — require execution proof
description:
On 2026-08-16 a change whose ENTIRE mechanism was a framework config option shipped through
three review layers dead, and only a real-transport dev-verify caught it.

The defect: `socket "/path", Sock, websocket: [auth_token: true]` in Phoenix. auth_token must be
a TOP-LEVEL socket/3 option. Phoenix does `websocket = put_auth_token(websocket, opts[:auth_token])`
and put_auth_token/2 is `Keyword.put(opts, :auth_token, enabled)` — so with the nested spelling
opts[:auth_token] is nil and the correctly-nested `true` is UNCONDITIONALLY OVERWRITTEN with nil.
:auth_token is in Phoenix's common_config allow-list, so nesting raises nothing. It just silently
does nothing. (deps/phoenix/lib/phoenix/endpoint.ex:745,770 — Phoenix 1.8.5)

What each layer did:
- The fable PLAN gate explicitly considered the two spellings, rated them "functionally
  equivalent", and waved it through as MINOR.
- The fable TEST gate approved a test (T11) that asserted `opts[:websocket][:auth_token] == true`
  — which PASSES against the broken spelling and FAILS against the correct one. A regression guard
  defending the regression.
- The unit suite was fully green because Phoenix.ChannelTest hand-supplies connect_info and never
  exercises socket_paths/4, where the overwrite happens.
- Two independent dev-verifies caught it within minutes of each other, by different methods
  (raw :gen_tcp + curl; :beam_lib decompilation + live :dbg trace after rm -rf _build).

The generalizable rule for the agent-loop / tdd / code-review skills:

  Reading a config option cannot tell you what a framework DOES with it. When a change's core
  mechanism IS a config value, a shape assertion is not coverage — it asserts what we typed, not
  what the framework parsed. The test gate must require at least one test that exercises the real
  code path the option controls, and the plan gate must not rate two spellings equivalent without
  reading the framework's parsing code.

This is a RECURRING class, not a one-off. CLAUDE.md's adversarial-TDD section already records the
same shape: test-configure-runex-plist.nu Test 23 asserted the wrong URL as EXPECTED, pinning a
regression as correct. T11 is that pattern recurring after it was documented — so documentation
alone has not been sufficient, and the gate checklist itself needs the rule.

Suggested change: add to the test-gate four questions a fifth — "if this change's mechanism is a
config value, does any test exercise the path that config controls, or do we only assert the
literal we wrote?"

title: elixir:ports — verify Windows env-name case-insensitivity vs allowlist helper
description:
Gate 3 review of PR #250 flagged, but could not verify (no Windows host): Windows environment variable names are case-insensitive, while the allowlist helper in plugins/languages/elixir/skills/ports/references/erlang-ports.md compares names case-sensitively via Enum.reject(&(&1 in @allowed)).

If Windows env names are case-insensitive, a variable set as 'Path' would not match an allowlist entry of 'PATH', and would be denied — or worse, a secret named differently by case could slip past the deny list.

Needs verification on a Windows host before either adding a caveat to the helper or normalizing case. Do NOT guess — this is explicitly unverified, which is why it is filed rather than documented.

title: fix(elixir): ports skill says {:env, list} replaces the OS environment; it extends it
description:
OTP documents that Port.open/2's {env, Env} EXTENDS the spawned process's environment, it does not replace it. Verified in erts erlang.erl (OTP 27 and 28 agree): 'The environment of the started process is extended using the environment specifications in Env.' Setting a value to false, "" or [] unsets that variable.

The /elixir:ports skill states the opposite in 6 places (SKILL.md lines 68, 73, 336, 338, 415 and references/erlang-ports.md line 57). This inverts the security posture the skill teaches: a reader believes a small env: list isolates the child, when in fact the child inherits every variable the BEAM holds.

The Security section's merge example (System.get_env |> Map.to_list) is built on the inverted premise and is removed. Fix: correct all 6 occurrences, state the mechanism as prose in SKILL.md, and put the deny example plus a minimal allowlist helper in references/erlang-ports.md.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #250 (squash 38fbcca): {:env, list} corrected to extend, not replace, across 6 occurrences; Security section rewritten; deny example + allowlist helper added to references

title: ADR forward-risk warnings are not routed to the PR they name
description:
## The gap
ADR-107's amendment named VIN-448 / PR #662 specifically and stated in writing what a reviewer should check before merge. That warning was written three weeks before the PR opened, and the PR still passed Gate 4, a frozen-test review, and its task briefing carrying the exact defect the ADR predicted.

Nothing surfaces a merged ADR's named warning to the PR, branch, or issue it is about. The mechanism that eventually caught it was an agent reading an unrelated research document while investigating something else.

## Why this belongs in the skills repo, not an app repo
It is a gate defect, cross-repo. Conventions already require reading ADRs from origin/main (a branched ADR is a draft) — but they assume a reviewer knows WHICH ADR applies. When an ADR names its own forward risk, that assumption is exactly what fails.

## Proposed shape (not prescriptive)
A lightweight step in the adversarial-review gate: grep `vantage_ex/architecture/decisions/*.md` on origin/main for the current branch name, PR number, or VIN identifier; if any ADR names it, surface that ADR's content to the reviewer explicitly rather than relying on independent recall.

Cheap, mechanical, and it turns a written warning from something a reviewer must happen to have read into something the gate hands them.

## Acceptance criteria
- A reviewer working a PR that a merged ADR names is shown that ADR's relevant text
- Verified against the real case: a review of a branch matching ADR-107's "Forward risk: VIN-448" surfaces the amendment
- Belongs in whichever of core:git / core:agent-loop owns the review gate — decide which rather than adding it to both

title: Agent shallow-clone isolation fails — scratchpad is session-scoped, so parallel agents share one clone
description:
Repo convention forbids git worktrees and prescribes shallow clones per worker for isolation, precisely to avoid the working-tree contention documented in `feedback_workspace_race_concurrent_workers`. On 2026-08-08 that convention was followed and did not isolate anything.

Two agents in an adversarial-TDD pair — a test author and an implementer, working on VIN-162 across `runex` and `runex-workflows` — were each told to "clone into your scratchpad." Both landed in the **same directory**, because the scratchpad path is **session-scoped, not agent-scoped**. They spent the task editing one shared clone without either being aware.

Discovered when the test author found uncommitted changes it had not made (`workflow.toml`, `codesign-binary.nu`, `place-binaries.nu`, plus untracked `sign.nu`, `sign-helpers.nu`, `codesign-verify-helpers.nu`) and watched two `BUNDLE_VERSION` bumps appear mid-session.

No damage occurred, and only because both agents happened to stage narrowly — `git add <path>` throughout, never `-A`, and a single-path stash that was popped immediately. A `git checkout`, `git reset`, blanket `git stash`, or `git clean` by either would have destroyed the other's uncommitted work with no warning. That is a coin-flip we won.

Two distinct problems:

**1. Isolation that reports success while providing none.** The instruction was followed exactly. The failure is that "your scratchpad" resolves identically for every agent in a session, so per-worker isolation silently degrades to a shared tree — the very thing the convention forbids. An agent has no way to detect this short of noticing files it did not create.

**2. It quietly erodes the adversarial-TDD boundary.** The split exists so a test author cannot shape tests to fit an implementation. Sharing a clone puts the implementation in front of the test author by construction. In this instance no harm resulted — every test predated the implementation, and the freeze check (`git diff <test-sha>..HEAD -- 'test/*'` empty) remains the real guard — but the pair was structurally able to see each other's work, which the separation is designed to prevent.

Fix directions:
- Make agent clone paths agent-scoped, e.g. `<scratchpad>/<agent-name>/<repo>`, either by convention in the prompts or by the harness providing a per-agent directory.
- Have agents assert isolation on arrival: if `git status --short` in a freshly-made clone is non-empty, someone else is already there — stop and report rather than proceeding.
- Consider whether adversarial-TDD pairs should be explicitly required to use distinct clone roots, since for them isolation is a correctness property and not merely hygiene.

P2 — no damage this time, but the mitigation depended entirely on both agents independently choosing narrow staging, and one ordinary `git checkout` would have caused silent data loss.

title: check-secrets-before-commit.sh: 'git add -f <gitignored> && git commit' goes unscanned
description:
Found by Gate 3 on PR #248 (claude-skills-271 review), independently confirmed by the lead. Out of scope for that PR — the gap predates it and nothing in the code or docs claims coverage — but it should be tracked rather than rediscovered.

The untracked export pass uses 'git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z'. That flag is CORRECT for the default staging set: 'git add .' will not stage a gitignored file, and dropping it would reintroduce the .env false-positive that claude-skills-268 explicitly decided against. But 'git add -f' means 'commit this DESPITE gitignore', and that is the one moment a gitignored secret genuinely enters history. The gate is blind exactly then.

VERIFIED, live token in each file:
  git add . && git commit -m x           (untracked, normal)  -> exit 2, blocked
  git add -f .env && git commit -m x                          -> exit 0, UNSCANNED
  git add -f private.txt && git commit -m x  (.git/info/exclude) -> exit 0, UNSCANNED

Lead confirmed the mechanism:
  git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -> []        (.env hidden, correctly)
  git ls-files --others                    -> [.env]
  after 'git add -f .env':
  git diff --cached --name-only            -> [.env]    (it IS in the index)

THE FIX IS NARROW. Because a force-added file lands in the index, the existing staged pass already catches it on any SEPARATE commit — 'git add -f .env' then 'git commit' as two commands is scanned today. The gap exists only when add -f and commit share one compound command, so the hook fires before the add has run.

Options: detect '-f'/'--force' in the intercepted command and widen that run's untracked set to drop --exclude-standard; or re-read the index after the fact. Note the first option reintroduces command-string matching for a coverage decision, which PR #248 removed for good reason — 'git stage' defeated exactly that shape. Prefer a mechanism that does not depend on parsing the command string, or accept the narrower scope deliberately and document it.

Do NOT fix by dropping --exclude-standard unconditionally: that scans every gitignored file on every commit, which is the false-positive behavior claude-skills-268 rejected and the reason a security gate gets disabled.

AC: a secret force-added to a gitignored path in the same compound command as the commit is detected and blocked. Controls: a gitignored file at rest is still NOT scanned (claude-skills-268), and a clean commit still succeeds.
close_reason: Merged PR #249 (docs+revert). Operator decision: document the gap, do not chase it. Two predicates each blocked legitimate commits (-f substring vs --fixup/--file; token-boundary vs rm -f/grep -f/docker build -f/tar -x -f). Gap is narrow: separate 'git add -f' then 'git commit' is still caught by the staged pass. Pinned by Parts 15-17, guarded by Parts 22/23, documented in /core:security, and both defeated predicates recorded in-code at the removal site.

title: gitleaks.nu scans git history only — uncommitted working-tree secrets are never examined
description:
Split from claude-skills-267 Gate 3 round 2 finding R2, deferred by operator decision to keep PR #246 scoped.

VERIFIED: a repo with one commit (a README) plus an uncommitted file containing a live slack-bot-token scans 20 bytes of history, satisfies the scanned-bytes>0 invariant added in PR #246, and prints 'No secrets detected'. The live secret is never examined.

This is gitleaks' documented behaviour, not a defect in gitleaks: 'git' mode walks history, 'dir' mode walks files. It is a gap in how scripts/gitleaks.nu uses it. The practical consequence is that the pre-push gate an agent runs before committing cannot see the very changes it is about to commit unless they are already committed.

The bytes invariant added in PR #246 closes the zero-scan and unparseable-summary cases only. Its code comment was corrected in that PR to stop claiming generality.

DESIGN QUESTION for whoever takes this: should gitleaks.nu run dir mode alongside git mode when the target is a work tree? That catches uncommitted secrets but changes what a 'clean' result means and needs its own test design. Note the shipped PreToolUse hook already covers the staged case correctly by exporting staged content to a temp dir and scanning it with --no-git.

AC: scanning a work tree containing an uncommitted secret reports it. Verify with the fixture above — one commit, one uncommitted token file.
close_reason: Merged PR #247 (docs). Operator decision: document the limit, do not change scanning behavior. Original AC superseded and recorded on the issue. Gate 3 approved after 4 rounds; review surfaced 4 distinct hook bypass classes, all routed to claude-skills-271.

comments.text:
Operator decision 2026-08-07: leave the scanning behavior as-is, document the limitation. Scope changes from a behavior fix to documentation.

The original AC ('scanning a work tree containing an uncommitted secret reports it') is SUPERSEDED and will NOT be met. Recording that explicitly so no future reader treats it as an outstanding requirement.

Measured evidence behind the decision, on a fixture with one committed file, one uncommitted file containing a live token, and a gitignored .env also containing one:
- git mode (current behavior): 0 findings. Misses both.
- dir mode over the whole tree: 2 findings — the uncommitted file (true positive) AND .env (a file intentionally gitignored, which normally holds real secrets by design).
- Cost is not the constraint: git 0.54s / 4.91 MB, dir 0.31s on this repo.

The rejected option was dir-mode-alongside-git. It meets the original AC but introduces false positives on gitignored files, and a security gate that cries wolf gets baselined or ignored — which is worse than one with a documented blind spot.

Note gitleaks dir takes exactly one [path] argument, so a per-file scan of 'git ls-files -co --exclude-standard' would need N invocations rather than one call.

REVISED AC: /core:security states plainly that gitleaks.nu's git-mode scan walks committed history and does not examine uncommitted working-tree changes; names the PreToolUse hook as what covers the staged case; and makes clear what a clean result does and does not establish. No behavior change to any of the three implementations.

title: gitleaks shell wrapper discards all arguments — every targeted scan silently becomes a full-history scan
description:
Found by impl-264 during claude-skills-264, after ci-runner-3 flagged that its scan counts matched no scope it had asked for. Independently verified by the lead before filing. This is the highest-value finding of the session because it silently degrades a security gate that /core:git and /core:security both mandate.

The shell environment defines gitleaks as a function (from ~/.claude/shell-snapshots/snapshot-zsh-*.sh):

  gitleaks () {
      container run -v $(PWD):/code zricethezav/gitleaks detect --source="/code" -v
  }

It never references $@. Verified: grep for '$@' in the definition returns 0. So EVERY argument any caller passes is silently discarded, and the function always runs one fixed full-history scan of the mounted cwd.

Consequences, all confirmed:
- 'gitleaks protect --staged' does NOT scan the index. It runs detect over history. A pre-commit staged scan — exactly what /core:git prescribes between commit and push — is therefore structurally incapable of seeing the work being committed.
- 'gitleaks detect --log-opts <range>' ignores the range and scans everything, which is why a scan reported 406 commits when the range held 1.
- Even 'gitleaks version' prints '407 commits scanned / no leaks found' — a command that is not a scan at all produces a scan report. That is the cleanest proof available that arguments never arrive.

The failure mode is worse than breakage: a full-history scan reports MORE commits and MORE bytes than the targeted scan it replaced, so it reads as stronger evidence while covering none of the requested scope. A reviewer seeing '407 commits, 6.44 MB, no leaks' reasonably concludes more was verified than with '1 commit, 10.49 KB'.

The absolute path is unaffected — ~/.local/share/mise/installs/gitleaks/latest/gitleaks (8.30.1) honours flags normally. Every scan this session that used it was real.

Note the wrapper also contradicts a decision this repo already recorded: root mise.toml line 11 declares gitleaks = "latest" with the comment 'Native binary preferred by scripts/gitleaks.nu over container runtimes (claude-skills-209)'. The wrapper reintroduces the container path that bee chose against. It also invokes 'container run', which this workspace restricts.

Two halves to the fix, and they are separable:
- Operator side (not repo content): remove or repair the shadowing function so the native binary resolves. Repairing means adding "$@" — but given 209 already chose native, removal is likelier correct than repair.
- Repo side: /core:git and /core:security tell agents to run gitleaks without specifying how to invoke it. Any agent following them literally gets a meaningless result on this machine. They should mandate the absolute path or the mise task, and say WHY — a bare invocation may be silently inert.

AC: agents following the documented gitleaks step get a scan whose scope matches what they asked for; the skills name the safe invocation. Verify by asserting a targeted scan reports a commit count matching the range — a scan that reports more than it was asked to cover has not been fixed. 'gitleaks version' must not print a scan report.
close_reason: Merged PR #246 (0f1cfe8). Operator half: shadowing gitleaks() removed from ~/.zshrc, verified against a control. Repo half: --no-git for non-git paths and a zero-bytes verification invariant across gitleaks.nu, gitleaks.sh and templates/mise.toml; docs name the shadow-proof invocation at point of use. 6 Gate 3 rounds. Follow-ups: claude-skills-268 (working-tree scanning), 269 (unpinned gitleaks + log-format coupling), 270 (arg-loop nit).

comments.text:
Framing correction from impl-264, adopted: **the defect is the missing $@ passthrough, not the container path.**

The original description leads with the passthrough, but its 'two halves to the fix' section risks misdirecting a reader toward the container-vs-native question. That is a consequence, not the defect. Someone could replace 'container run ... zricethezav/gitleaks' with the pinned native binary, satisfy the claude-skills-209 preference, remove the container invocation entirely — and still have a function that silently ignores --staged, --log-opts, and --redact, because it still would not reference $@.

Order of severity for whoever takes this:
1. Arguments are discarded. Any caller's flags vanish. This is the defect.
2. It hardcodes a full-history 'detect --source=/code', so the discarded flags are replaced by the broadest possible scan — which reports MORE commits and bytes than the targeted scan it replaced, and therefore reads as stronger evidence.
3. It uses a container runtime, contradicting claude-skills-209's recorded native-binary preference, and invokes 'container run', which this workspace restricts.

Fixing 3 alone leaves 1 and 2 intact and the gate still meaningless.

The AC as written is outcome-based ('a scan whose scope matches what they asked for', 'a commit count matching the range') so it already fails a fix that only addresses 3 — but the reasoning should be explicit rather than relying on the AC to catch it.

Confirmed working bypass, for anyone who needs a scan before this is fixed: call ~/.local/share/mise/installs/gitleaks/latest/gitleaks by absolute path. Verified 8.30.1, honours flags normally. Two independent scoped scans through it this session: 1 commit / 882 bytes on vantage_ex PR #166, and 1 commit / 10.49 KB on claude-skills PR #245.

Lead pre-flight, 2026-08-07. Premise correction plus new findings.

STALE PREMISE: the repo-side ask ('the skills name the safe invocation') was already satisfied before this bee was filed. plugins/core/skills/security/SKILL.md:247 has a '#### Shell-function shadowing trap' section naming 'nu scripts/gitleaks.nu' or the mise-resolved absolute path. It landed in af0f8af (PR #204, claude-skills-209).

WHY IT WAS MISSED: the installed plugin cache is core 0.2.41; the repo and marketplace are at 0.2.57. The skill body an agent loads at runtime lacks the section entirely. Anyone reasoning from the loaded skill concludes the mitigation is absent. This is a general hazard for every bee filed against skill content — verify against the repo tree, not the loaded skill.

OPERATOR HALF: DONE. The function was defined at ~/.zshrc:26-29, immediately after 'eval $(mise activate zsh)' on line 24. Removed (backup at ~/.zshrc.bak-pre-gitleaks-fix), replaced with a comment explaining why no wrapper belongs there. Verified against a positive control — sourcing the backup still yields 'gitleaks is a shell function'; sourcing the fixed rc yields the binary path. AC checks both pass: 'gitleaks version' prints '8.30.1' with no scan report; 'gitleaks git --log-opts=-1' reports '1 commits scanned' against 774 for full history.

CORRECTION TO THE BEE'S VERSION CLAIMS: gitleaks 8.30.1 --help lists only completion/dir/git/help/stdin/version. 'detect' and 'protect' survive as unlisted deprecated aliases and both were verified working, so the shipped hook and scripts/gitleaks.nu are NOT broken.

NEW DEFECT FOUND (fail-open, more severe than the filed issue): 'gitleaks detect --source=<non-git-dir>' without --no-git logs a git fatal, scans 0 bytes, prints 'no leaks found' and EXITS 0. scripts/gitleaks.nu:466 builds exactly that form and treats exit 0 as success — a green gate that scanned nothing. Safe today only because it happens to be pointed at a git repo. In scope for this bee per operator direction.

ALSO IN SCOPE: templates/mise.toml [tasks.gitleaks] invokes 'container run' unconditionally with no native path, contradicting root mise.toml:11 and claude-skills-209.

title: validate-plugin.nu self-test cannot detect always-true or reject-neutered mutations in most of its checks
description:
PR #217 enabled --strict in CI, which makes every check in validate-plugin.nu load-bearing. Gate 3 then probed the self-test suite by mutation and found most checks are not covered at all.

Proven by mutation against the 30-case suite, each probe run individually:
- validate-skill-md: body replaced with an unconditional error return, 30/30 cases still pass. No fixture carries a skills entry.
- is-kebab-case: replaced with return true, 30/30 pass. Only valid names appear in fixtures; the reject direction is untested.
- is-semver (the top-level version field, distinct from the dependency range check): replaced with return true, 30/30 pass. No malformed-version fixture exists.
- validate-agent-md non-model checks (name mismatch, tools given as a YAML list instead of a string, missing description): no reject-direction fixtures. The block added in #217 varies only the model field.
- main, validate-plugin-file, validate-from-marketplace, setup-external-plugin, cleanup-temp: not reached by self-test at all, which calls validate-plugin-content directly.

Partial mitigation, and the reason this is not catastrophic today: mise run test:plugins exercises the marketplace path against 30 real plugins, so a mutation that makes a check always FAIL is caught immediately. What is invisible to the entire CI is the opposite direction - a check neutered to always PASS, or with its reject branch removed.

That is exactly the shape that let the agent model allowlist ship untested and then become a CI blocker the moment --strict landed: reverting the allowlist passed the self-test with zero failures, because nothing reached the function.

AC: add reject-direction fixtures for each function listed above, sufficient that an always-true mutation fails at least one case. Verify by mutation per function rather than by counting cases - a suite that grows without closing this gap has not fixed it. Consider whether a mutation-probe harness belongs in the repo so this is checkable rather than periodically rediscovered.
close_reason: Closed by PRs #221 and #223 together. #221 covered is-kebab-case, is-semver, validate-skill-md, validate-agent-md's non-model checks and the marketplace description/keywords agreement check; #223 covered the remaining 11 array-type and path-existence checks. Self-test 30 to 80 cases, but the measure was per-function mutation verification, not case count. Remaining related work is tracked separately: claude-skills-243 (lenient-JSON5 scalar crash), 245 (unreachable null branches to delete), and a new bee for the commands/agents string-form doc divergence

comments.text:
PR #221 merged — closed the always-pass coverage gap for is-kebab-case, is-semver, validate-skill-md, validate-agent-md's non-model checks, and the description/keywords marketplace-agreement check (that last one was found by review INSIDE this PR: it could be neutered to 'if false' with the suite still green, against a genuinely drifted marketplace.json — the bee's own failure mode surviving in the PR closing the bee).

Suite 34 to 68 cases, but the case count is not the measure. Every function was verified by mutation: neuter to always-pass, confirm a case fails, restore, confirm green.

Two mutations survived the first 66-case round and were killed by two fixtures. Both had the same design flaw, recorded now in each fixture's why: comment. The kebab reject fixtures were all 'My_Plugin' style, carrying BOTH an uppercase letter and an underscore, so a mutant accepting pure snake_case stayed caught via the uppercase and was never distinguished. The semver reject fixtures all started with non-digits, so a mutant reduced to 'starts with a digit' passed everything. A reject fixture must differ from the accepted case in exactly ONE dimension.

Also diagnosed rather than papered over: a fixture using 'not valid json {{{' never reached the invalid-JSON path, because nushell parses that leniently as a bare string - so the production guard had been untested. Filed as claude-skills-243.

NOT closed: 11 further always-pass-neuterable checks remain in the skills/commands/agents array-type and path-existence surface, filed as claude-skills-244. This bee stays open until those have reject-direction fixtures. Network paths in setup-external-plugin are explicitly scoped out (self-test stays network-free, matching repo convention).

title: check-secrets-before-commit.sh allows the commit on any gitleaks exit code other than 1
description:
The pre-commit hook at plugins/core/skills/security/hooks/check-secrets-before-commit.sh treats exit code 1 as secrets-found (blocks, exit 2) and everything else as a soft failure - it prints a warning and allows the commit.

Confirmed empirically during Gate 3 of PR 204: a stubbed gitleaks forced to exit 42 produced 'Gitleaks scan failed (exit code: 42) / Allowing commit' and a hook exit of 0.

Why this matters more than a normal fail-open: it is a STANDING bypass, not an occasional one. A single committed broken .gitleaks.toml makes every subsequent scan exit non-1, so every commit thereafter is allowed with only a warning, indefinitely and silently. Nobody gets a signal that scanning stopped working.

PR 204 added a deliberate, documented fail-open for the separate 'no runtime available' branch, with a stated rationale (fail-closed would brick commits on any host without a scanner) and a revisit condition. That reasoning was accepted. It does NOT cover this branch, and the new comment does not mention it.

Also relevant context verified during that review: grep -rni gitleaks .github/ returns zero hits, so this hook is currently the only automated secret scan in this repo. CI's test:disclosure checks infrastructure identifiers, not credentials.

AC: either fail closed (exit 2) on unexpected gitleaks exit codes, or extend the documented fail-open rationale to cover them explicitly with its own revisit condition. Silence is the thing to fix either way. Pre-existing; not introduced by PR 204.
close_reason: PR #214 merged — check-secrets-before-commit.sh now fails closed (exit 2) on any gitleaks exit code other than 0/1, with a message distinct from secrets-detected. The documented no-scanner-available fail-open is untouched. Regression test covers 0/1/42/127 plus the no-runtime branch

title: Broken symlink in references/ hard-crashes validate-skills-quality.nu, masking every finding
description:
test/validate-skills-quality.nu around line 2928 calls 'open --raw' on each reference file. A broken symlink under any skill's references/ directory aborts the entire run: zero tables are printed and every other finding in the corpus is masked.

This is the failure mode the house rule warns about - a rule that crashes instead of reporting hides everything else. The operator cannot tell a crash from a clean run except by noticing the absent output.

Found during Gate 3 review of PR 207. Pre-existing; the line was not touched by that diff (grep of the diff for 'open --raw' returned zero matches).

AC: guard the read so an unreadable reference is REPORTED as a finding against that skill rather than aborting the run. Cover broken symlinks, unreadable permissions, and a symlink pointing outside the repo. Add a self-test fixture for each - a green run on a corpus with no broken symlinks proves nothing.
close_reason: PR #215 merged — unreadable references now report as a ref_unsafe finding instead of aborting the run (original crash printed zero score rows; fixed validator prints all 106). Hardened during review: every reference path is canonicalized, so a symlinked ANCESTOR directory cannot bypass the external-content quarantine — verified by planting one and confirming ref_unsafe fires where content was previously read and scanned

title: claude-plugins skill and validate-plugin.nu both treat 'dependencies' as invalid, but upstream documents it
description:
Upstream (code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference, fetched 2026-08-04) documents dependencies as a valid plugin.json field: 'Other plugins this plugin requires, optionally with semver version constraints', shape array, example [{ name: secrets-vault, version: ~2.1.0 }].

Two places contradict that:
1. plugins/tools/claude-code/skills/claude-plugins/SKILL.md has a 'Fields that must NOT appear in plugin.json' section listing dependencies as marketplace-only.
2. validate-plugin.nu invalid_fields denylist (around line 237) is [dependencies, category, strict, source, tags] - so the validator REJECTS a field upstream documents as legitimate.

Surfaced during PR 205 (claude-skills-215) and deliberately left out of that PRs AC, which named only outputStyles, lspServers and experimental.

The same upstream fetch also shows five further manifest fields the skill does not model at all: displayName, defaultEnabled, workflows, userConfig, channels.

AC: reconcile the skill and the denylist with current upstream. Decide whether the five unmodelled fields are one slice or several. Verify against upstream docs, not against the existing skill text.
close_reason: PR #213 merged — dependencies confirmed a plugin-manifest field (plugins-reference 'Component path fields' table + the Complete schema example); removed from the denylist and documented, along with displayName, defaultEnabled, workflows, userConfig, channels. relevance confirmed marketplace-only and deliberately left out

title: twelve-factor SKILL.md:263 blockquote is not verbatim from 12factor.net
description:
The blockquote at plugins/core/skills/twelve-factor/SKILL.md:263 reads 'A twelve-factor app never relies on implicit existence of state on the filesystem. Even if a process has written something to disk, it must assume that file wont be available on the next request.' It is presented as a direct quotation but does not appear on 12factor.net.

It is a mashup of two different factors. 12factor.net/dependencies says 'A twelve-factor app never relies on implicit existence of system-wide packages.' 12factor.net/processes says 'The twelve-factor app never assumes that anything cached in memory or on disk will be available on a future request or job.' An exact-phrase search for the committed text returns zero hits.

Found during Gate 3 review of PR 205, which proposed citing this line as the canonical worked example for a new boundary-test category named quoted source material. Enshrining it would have taught readers to protect a fabricated quote.

The adjacent blockquote at line 261 IS verbatim, confirmed against the 12factor.net front page.

AC: either replace 263 with the real text of whichever factor was intended and attribute it to that factor, or drop it. Verify against 12factor.net rather than inferring.
close_reason: PR #214 merged — twelve-factor SKILL.md:263 now carries the full verbatim Processes sentence including the U+2013 en-dash, replacing a truncation that had invented a terminal period. :261 untouched and byte-exact; the context-engineering-claude-5.md:88 cross-reference still resolves

title: test:version-bumps cannot see the aggregating all-skills plugin
description:
The check validates the diff direction on the branch (new > old) and never independently compares against origin/main's current value for a plugin whose content did not diff. all-skills aggregates skill paths, so its version line changes without its content changing — it therefore never appears in the modified-plugins set the check reports on.

Consequence: an all-skills version equal to OR BELOW main passes green. Observed repeatedly during this session's serialized merge queue — PRs #194, #197, #198, #200 and #201 each carried an equal-or-downward all-skills value at some point with a green check. Two further ways this hides: git raises no conflict when both branches set the same line to the same value, and gh pr view's mergeStateStatus goes stale against a moving main.

Only a manual 'git show origin/main:.claude-plugin/plugin.json | jq -r .version' plus 'git merge-base --is-ancestor origin/main HEAD' catches it today.

AC: compare every plugin's branch version against origin/main's current value, not just the diff direction, and include plugins whose version changed even when their content did not.

title: nushell: document the self-write truncation gotcha (open | ... | save same path zeroes the file)
description:
## Objective

Add a Critical gotcha to /core:nushell for the read-and-rewrite-same-path footgun, alongside the existing "No 2>&1", "bare main runs twice", and "external commands need ^" entries.

## The bug

    open --raw $f | lines | each {|l| ... } | str join "\n" | save --force --raw $f

`open --raw` returns a STREAM. `save` opens the same path for writing while that stream is still being read, so the file is truncated. Verified during claude-skills-182 batch 2: this zeroed .claude-plugin/plugin.json from 142 lines to 0 bytes.

Fix - force the read to complete before any save touches the path:

    let content = (open --raw $f | lines | each {|l| ... })
    ($content | str join "\n") + "\n" | save --force --raw $f

Diagnostic tell: sibling files processed by the same logic survive if their read was bound to a variable first. In the incident, ten plugin.json files written via `let lines = (open --raw $path | lines)` were fine and only the one written as a single pipeline died. A partial blast radius is the signature.

## Second, related gotcha worth the same entry

`lines` drops the trailing newline and `str join` does not restore it, so a rewrite silently strips the final byte (eleven files at once in the incident, surfacing as spurious -}/+} diff hunks). Append + "\n" explicitly - but check the target file convention first with `xxd <file> | tail -1`, since not every file has one and normalizing creates churn.

Also worth a line: do NOT verify a rewrite with `tail -c1`. On a zero-byte file it returns empty, which reads as "ends with a newline" - the check reported the file healthy at the moment it had been destroyed. Verify against `git show HEAD:<path>` or a line count.

## Acceptance criteria

- The gotcha appears in /core:nushell SKILL.md under Critical gotchas with the broken form, the fixed form, and the partial-blast-radius diagnostic.
- The trailing-newline behaviour and the tail -c1 anti-check are covered in the same entry or an adjacent one.
- If a detection grep is practical (a pipeline whose `open` and `save` name the same variable), state it; if not, say why.
- core + all-skills versions bumped, mise test green.

## Load skills

/core:anti-fabrication, /core:nushell, /claude-code:claude-skills
close_reason: PR #185 merged — read-and-rewrite-same-path truncation documented in /core:nushell with the partial-blast-radius tell, the trailing-newline and tail -c1 traps, and two grep forms scoped to which grep each needs.

title: sources: document that current_version and last_checked accept "unknown" in the skill-update field table
description:
## Objective

The sources.toml field table in plugins/tools/claude-code/skills/skill-update/SKILL.md does not document that entry-level current_version and last_checked accept the literal string "unknown", though the validator accepts it and 20 entries in the corpus already depend on it.

## Context

Found during claude-skills-182 batch 2 (PR #176) while resolving a Gate 3 finding.

The [meta] paragraph above the table correctly documents "unknown" for reviewed_at_plugin_version and last_full_check. The per-entry table below it does not: last_checked is listed as "YYYY-MM-DD", required, with no mention of the escape hatch, and current_version is listed as "string, yes unless none".

This matters for anti-fabrication specifically. "unknown" is the mechanism that lets an author record "I could not establish this" instead of guessing. An author reading only the field table sees a required date field and no permitted way to say they do not know it - which is exactly the pressure that produces a fabricated date. Batch 2 authors used "unknown" correctly only because the dispatch prompt told them it was permitted; the skill itself does not.

Corpus evidence at the time of filing: 20 entries use last_checked = "unknown" and validation passes.

## Non-finding, recorded so it is not re-investigated

Gate 3 on PR #176 also reported that this skill says current_version/last_checked are unconditionally required and that the schema uses a scalar "skill" field. Both are FALSE against the repo - the current file says skills as a list, current_version "yes unless none", and documents the none forbidden-fields rule. The reviewer was reading the version loaded from its plugin cache (0.2.34), which lags the working tree. Anyone verifying skill content must read the repo file, not the loaded skill body.

## Acceptance criteria

- The field table states that current_version and last_checked accept "unknown", with one line on when to use it (value could not be established from sources.md, git history, or a live check) rather than guessing.
- claude-code plugin + marketplace versions bumped, mise test green.

## Load skills

/core:anti-fabrication, /claude-code:claude-skills, /claude-code:skill-update
close_reason: PR #178 merged — field table now shows unknown for current_version and last_checked, with the enforcement asymmetry stated (last_checked checked by b3_date; current_version has no format check). Follow-up for the missing check filed as claude-skills-189.

title: sources: document the sources.md Entries-line convention required by c2_md_no_mention
description:
## Objective

Make the "every sources.toml entry name must appear in sources.md" requirement (rule c2_md_no_mention in test/validate-sources.nu) a documented, uniform convention before wave B (claude-skills-183) migrates 8 more plugins.

## Context

During claude-skills-182 batch 2, four independent authoring agents hit c2_md_no_mention and each invented a DIFFERENT workaround:

1. core - added an explicit sentence listing all 21 entry names in backticks after the index-pointer line.
2. design / pm / graphify - added an "Entries: ..." line, citing plugins/tools/qa/skills/sources.md as precedent.
3. elixir - renamed an entry from erlang-otp to erlang/otp so it would match text inside a URL.
4. rust / wasm - named entries after URL fragments already present in the prose (doc.rust-lang.org/stable, design/wit.html), degrading the name field, whose schema meaning is "Human-readable source identifier". Fixed in the same PR by renaming plus adding the Entries line.

The check itself is reasonable - sources.md is meant to be the index for sources.toml, so naming its entries is what an index does. The problem is that it is undocumented, so each author rediscovers it at validation time and solves it differently. Batch 1 left the corpus with two shapes; batch 2 without this fix would have left four.

Note the check passes on substring containment against the whole file including URLs, so an entry can satisfy it accidentally - rig/lemonade-server passes only because lemonade-server.ai appears in its own url field, not because any prose names it. That makes the rule weaker than it looks.

## Acceptance criteria

- The Entries-line convention (placement immediately after the Structured tracking pointer, backticked names, one line) is written down where a wave-B author will read it before authoring - the claude-code:skill-update skill sources.toml section and/or templates/sources.toml.
- Decide and record whether c2 should match prose only rather than the whole file including URL fields; if yes, file the follow-up, if no, record why accidental URL matches are acceptable.
- Existing migrated plugins are consistent with whatever is decided, or a follow-up bee names the ones left inconsistent.

## Load skills

/core:anti-fabrication, /core:nushell, /core:restraint, /claude-code:claude-skills, /claude-code:skill-update
close_reason: PR #177 merged — c2_md_no_mention now matches sources.md prose only (scheme-prefixed URLs stripped); 7 URL-only entries normalized across 5 plugins; convention documented in skill-update SKILL.md + templates/sources.toml. Residual gap accepted per restraint: schemeless www., scheme-relative //, and ftp:// are not stripped — zero such forms in the corpus.

title: validate-sources.nu crashes on wrong-TYPE top-level values instead of reporting
description:
## Objective

Close two input-domain gaps in test/validate-sources.nu before claude-skills-182 and 183 land 26 hand-authored sources.toml files, since that is exactly when malformed input becomes likely.

## The defect

Wrong-TYPE values at the two table roots abort the validator with a raw nushell error rather than emitting a finding. Both confirmed by construction during the Gate 3 review of PR 173:

- meta = "awman" (a scalar where the [meta] table belongs) aborts at line 70, only_supports_this_input_type, because  | columns is called on a string.
- A top-level sources = ["not-a-table"] (array of strings instead of [[sources]] tables) aborts at line 150, incompatible_path_access, because the .skills? cell path is applied to a string.

Both fail RED, never green, so CI cannot silently pass and this is not a correctness hole. The cost is diagnosis: the abort names the validator's own line rather than which of 28 plugins' files is bad, and the remainder of the scan is skipped, so an author fixing one file cannot see the others' findings in the same run. Across 26 hand-authored files that is a real tax.

This is the same describe/cell-path family as amendments A-F2 and A-F4 on the PR 181 plan. The implementer guarded null, missing, and wrong-SHAPE at both table roots; wrong-TYPE was the case nobody named. Note the repo has now been bitten four times in three days by this family: describe returning table<...> for a list of records, a dead == "record" branch that made every object source unchecked, the heterogeneous-table column-intersection trap caught in review, and now this. A type check before any columns or cell-path access should be the default posture in this file, not an exception.

## Also in scope, recorded as a decision rather than an oversight

Duplicate [[sources]] entries covering the same skill are silently accepted - a planted awman-dup entry exits 0. No rule exists in the design, the plan, or claude-skills-181, so this is currently accepted behaviour. Decide deliberately whether a duplicate is an error, a warning, or legal (a skill can legitimately have several upstreams, so legality is defensible; two entries with the same name for the same skill is more suspicious than two different sources).

## Acceptance criteria

- meta as a scalar, sources as an array of non-tables, and any other wrong-type value at either root produce a normal finding naming the plugin and the offending key, and the scan continues to the remaining plugins.
- Self-test cases added for both, in the file's existing embedded style.
- Verify by making it fail, then confirm the same input reports rather than aborts. Paste verbatim output both ways.
- A decision recorded on duplicate entries, implemented if the decision is that it is a finding.
- mise test exit 0; waiver count same or lower, never higher.

## Load skills

/core:anti-fabrication, /core:nushell, /core:git, /core:restraint, /core:security

## Reference

Gate 3 record on PR 173: https://github.com/vinnie357/claude-skills/pull/173#issuecomment-5132507890
close_reason: Fixed in PR #174 (0b8d438). Wrong-TYPE values at both sources.toml roots now report instead of aborting the scan, and the duplicate question is decided: entries may share a SKILL (a skill can genuinely have several upstreams) but not a NAME, which is the copy-paste error - rule b6_duplicate_name, with a self-test asserting the same-skill-different-name case stays clean. Self-tests 34 to 43. Two rounds were needed and the second is the one worth recording. My first fix aborted on exactly the inputs it was written to report, because 'any' itself throws on non-list input, so sources as a scalar, a record, or the single-bracket [sources] typo all died AT the new guard line. Gate 3 caught it and confirmed on the corpus that one bad file still killed the whole 28-plugin scan. Fixing that surfaced the fifth instance in three days of the same describe trap: my replacement used describe piped to str starts-with list, and my own self-tests immediately failed it because [[sources]] with entries renders as table<...>, not list<...>. The repo had already solved this in validate-marketplace.nu with describe --detailed | get type, which returns list for both; all seven describe sites in validate-sources.nu now use that form and a grep for the fragile spelling returns zero. Then six field-level abort inputs turned up, one of them - name = 123 hitting str downcase - sitting one line below a comment lecturing about fixing one site and leaving the sibling. Those route through a new scalar-str helper. A third site of the same root cause followed: the C-group's 'if sources != null' let a string root reach 'where'. All caught by self-tests, all guarded. Also fixed a latent bug in the self-test harness itself: the a4_review_pending failure message had unescaped parens, so it crashed instead of printing - invisible until that case failed. Verification was run by a haiku agent: eight negative cases all report rather than abort, and breaking awman and zig simultaneously yields findings for both in one run, proving the scan continues. Waivers unchanged at 65.

title: sources PR3: migration wave B - by-source-organised plugins and the oddballs
description:
## Objective

Author sources.toml for the remaining roughly 13 plugins: those whose sources.md is organised BY SOURCE rather than by skill (the claude-code pattern), plus the known oddballs. Third of four under claude-skills-180.

## CRITICAL - these plugins are the hard ones

- claude-code organises by source, not by skill: 35 URL entries across 12 skills, with multi-skill Used-In lines. Attribution requires reading each entry to decide which skills it covers. This is exactly where a heading-slugging migrator gets it wrong.
- plugins/tools/runex/skills/sources.md contains NO URL AT ALL across 47 lines. There is nothing to convert mechanically. Decide honestly what its entries are, and if the sources genuinely were never recorded, say so via unknown rather than inventing them. Note runex is a PRIVATE GitHub repo, so github-releases may not work from CI without a token - default its check_method to manual until tested.
- whamm writes the bullet as - **Version:** with the colon INSIDE the bold, which is why naive extraction misses it. Its URLs are affected by the same quirk.
- agent-sandboxing carries - **Version verified against**: lines - an upstream TOOL version, a different semantic from the plugin version. These map onto current_version per the PR1 schema, not onto meta.reviewed_at_plugin_version.

## CRITICAL - general

- Do NOT fabricate dates or versions; the literal string unknown is schema-legal.
- Every skill directory must appear in some entry's skills list; no-upstream skills get an explicit check_method = none entry with notes.

## Acceptance criteria

- All 28 plugins now have a conforming skills/sources.toml.
- mise test exit 0; mise run test:sources reports zero invariant violations corpus-wide.
- Union of skills arrays equals the skill directory set per plugin, verified by set difference.
- Waiver count same or lower. gitleaks clean. Conventional commits, no attribution.

comments.text:
Measured wave membership, 2026-07-30. Wave B is 8 plugins, not the roughly 13 the design estimated: agent-sandboxing, allium, altana, claude-code, github, slidev, runex, whamm.

Per-plugin facts - skills / sources.md lines / URLs / organising convention:

Why each is hard, beyond what the bee already records:

- altana: 1 URL; the rest are local filesystem paths under a home directory. Internal project. Note the repo is PUBLIC - do not carry a real home path into a tracked file. Use the check_method = none case or a generic placeholder.

title: sources PR4: flip enforcement on and retire the substring source check
description:
## Objective

Turn the reporting checks into enforcement, now that all 28 plugins have a conforming sources.toml. Final item under claude-skills-180.

## Scope

- test/validate-sources.nu: missing sources.toml changes from REPORT to FAILURE.
- Remove check 11 (the substring source check) from test/validate-skills-quality.nu, and shrink the baseline by the source keys it was carrying - 8 at filing time. These two changes MUST land atomically: removing the check without the shrink leaves stale passing keys, which is a hard failure, and shrinking without removing leaves the check firing.
- version_pin: drop the sources.md acceptance path added in PR1, making it toml-only. Delete the 9 remaining (current) annotation lines across 3 core SKILL.md files.
- Plugin and marketplace version bumps for every touched plugin per repo convention, plus all-skills, then mise update-all-skills.

## Why check 11 goes

It is a whole-file substring test, so it cannot distinguish real coverage from an incidental name match. Its 8 waivers today INCLUDE zig skills whose coverage genuinely exists but is invisible to a substring scan - that debt partly measures the check's blind spot rather than missing sources. The exact set-difference check that replaces it makes those waivers correct to retire rather than merely waived.

## Acceptance criteria

- mise test exit 0 with the baseline shrunk by exactly the retired source keys, and no other baseline entry altered.
- Verify by making it fail: temporarily remove one plugin's sources.toml and confirm test:sources now FAILS naming that plugin; restore it. Paste verbatim output.
- Confirm no version_pin finding appears after the (current) lines are deleted.
- gitleaks clean. Conventional commits, no attribution.

/core:anti-fabrication, /core:nushell, /core:git, /core:restraint, /core:security, /claude-code:claude-skills, /claude-code:claude-plugins

title: sources PR2: migration wave A - by-skill-organised and single-skill plugins
description:
## Objective

Author sources.toml for roughly 13 plugins whose sources.md is organised BY SKILL (the core pattern) plus the single-skill plugins. Second of four items under claude-skills-180.

## CRITICAL

- This is AUTHORING work requiring judgment per plugin, not scripting. There is deliberately no trusted auto-migrator: sources-init.nu misattributes skills via heading slugging and silently misses colon-inside-bold URL formatting. Use it for a draft only, then verify every entry by reading the plugin's actual sources.md and skill directories.
- Do NOT fabricate dates or versions. Where a plugin's sources were last reviewed at an unknown version on an unknown date, the schema permits the literal string unknown. A guessed date is fabrication.
- Every skill directory in the plugin must appear in some entry's skills list. A skill with no external upstream gets an explicit check_method = none entry with notes explaining why - not omission.

## Scope per plugin

Author skills/sources.toml; delete the Version and Plugin Information bullets from sources.md; add the index pointer line making sources.md an index for sources.toml.

Where a wave's sources.md edits make a previously-waived source key pass, run nu test/validate-skills-quality.nu --update-baseline in this PR. Baseline shrink is permitted AND required - a stale passing key is a hard failure.

## Acceptance criteria

- mise test exit 0, mise run test:sources reports no invariant violations for the migrated plugins.
- Waiver count same or lower, never higher.
- For each migrated plugin, the union of its entries' skills arrays exactly equals its skill directory set - verify with a set difference, not a substring match.
- gitleaks clean. Conventional commits, no attribution.

## Load skills

/core:anti-fabrication, /core:nushell, /core:git, /core:restraint, /core:security, /claude-code:claude-skills, /claude-code:skill-update

comments.text:
Measured wave membership, 2026-07-30. The design estimated roughly 13 plugins per wave; the actual split is 18 in wave A and 8 in wave B, summing to the 26 unmigrated plugins (awman and zig already have sources.toml).

WAVE A (18): core, design, elixir, rust, pm, ui, wasm, ansible, beads, dagu, graphify, linear, playwright, proxmox, qa, rig, sbx, tweag.

Per-plugin facts to work from - skills / sources.md lines / URL count:
core 13/298/37, elixir 9/306/40, rust 8/141/26, ansible 5/76/13, dagu 3/83/6, design 2/42/7, pm 2/40/6, wasm 2/98/16, graphify 2/54/4, tweag 2/91/14, ui 1/63/5, beads 1/31/4, linear 1/54/2, playwright 1/26/3, proxmox 1/84/26, qa 1/27/1, rig 1/84/9, sbx 1/40/8.

Judgment flags found in the sweep, so nobody hits them cold:
- Seven wave-A plugins have NO - **Version** bullet at all: design, ansible, beads, linear, proxmox, sbx, tweag. Nothing to delete there; meta.reviewed_at_plugin_version starts as unknown unless git archaeology finds the review commit.
- design has no plugin-metadata block whatsoever, not just a missing Version line.
- elixir's headings do not map 1:1 to skill directories: the tidewave skill has no heading of its own and sits nested under Phoenix Skill. Attribution needs reading, not slugging.
- pm is explicitly doctrine-only in its own text - 'Internal sources - this skill is composed of conventions from other skills'. That is the check_method = none case the schema added; it is not a gap to fill with a URL.
- qa has 1 URL across 27 lines and proxmox has 26 URLs across 84 lines; the density range means no single conversion shape fits all 18.

Reminder from claude-skills-185: sources-init.nu is a DRAFT generator only. Its to-slug misattributes every heading it touches (17 core headings produced 0 matches against 13 real skill directories), so its output must be verified per entry, never trusted.

Batch 1 of 2 merged as PR #175 (79eb10c). Eight single-skill plugins now have a conforming sources.toml: ui, beads, linear, playwright, proxmox, qa, rig, sbx. Corpus is at 10 validated, 18 pending. Waivers unchanged at 65.

Remaining for batch 2, the ten multi-skill wave-A plugins: core (13 skills), elixir (9), rust (8), ansible (5), dagu (3), design (2), pm (2), wasm (2), graphify (2), tweag (2).

Three things batch 1 established that batch 2 should reuse:

The data survived an adversarial fabrication audit. 21 of 24 url values appear verbatim in their plugin's sources.md, checked by set difference rather than by eye; the three exceptions each traced to a live API response or a base repo already in the file. Every current_version and last_checked traced to text already in sources.md, and reviewed_at_plugin_version = 0.1.0 was confirmed by git archaeology - each of beads, linear, proxmox and sbx has exactly one sources.md commit, with plugin.json at 0.1.0 at that commit. That standard of provenance is the bar for batch 2.

The migration found a real upstream rename. beads sources.md says steveyegge/beads; the toml records gastownhall/beads after confirming the old path 301-redirects to repo id 1074561042. Expect more of these - prose sources go stale silently, and this is the first mechanism that catches it.

Pinned-but-behind is recorded honestly rather than silently advanced. rig pins 0.40.0 while upstream is at 0.41.0, and sbx pins 0.30.0 against 0.37.1. Both stay pinned with a note. Do not bump a version during migration - that is a separate decision from recording what the skill was actually written against.

One process note: the PR body quoted a disclosure-lint file count from before the new files existed (588 versus 596 at head). Re-verified clean at head. Paste evidence AFTER the final commit, not from a mid-run state.

Batch 2 complete — PR #176 (10 multi-skill wave-A plugins: core, elixir, rust, ansible, dagu, design, pm, wasm, graphify, tweag). Corpus 10 -> 20 sources.toml, 18 -> 8 pending. Waivers unchanged at 65.
