title: core:nushell — document the version-bounded caught-error record shape (.json vs .details)

comments.text:
Verified 2026-08-15 against two nu versions directly.

/core:nushell should document the caught-error record shape AND that it is version-bounded, because getting it wrong is silent:

- nu 0.113.1: columns [msg, debug, raw, rendered, json]. '.details' DOES NOT EXIST (raises "Cannot find column 'details'"). '.json' is a JSON STRING; the discriminating code is at ($err.json | from json).code — e.g. nu::shell::io::connection_refused.
- nu 0.114.1: columns [msg, debug, raw, rendered, details]. '.json' is gone; the code is at $err.details.code.
- In BOTH versions $err.msg (and 0.114's $err.details.msg) is the generic 'I/O error'. nu::shell::io::* collapses timeout / refused / reset / unreachable into that one string, which is why reading the code at all matters.

WHY THIS NEEDS TO BE IN THE SKILL, not just a repo memory: an agent naturally verifies against whatever nu is ambient on the machine, which is NOT necessarily the version mise pins for the project. On 2026-08-15 an agent authoring a frozen test contract verified against ambient 0.114.1, concluded the recorded '.json' convention was wrong, and built fixtures to the 0.114 shape. All 44 tests passed. An implementer coding faithfully to those fixtures would have read a nonexistent '.details' field under the pinned 0.113.1, fallen back to $err.msg, and shipped the exact illegible 'I/O error' the convention exists to prevent. Caught only because the reviewer was explicitly told to verify against the pin rather than ambient.

SUGGESTED SKILL TEXT: a short subsection under the existing error-handling material giving both shapes, the version boundary, the instruction to check the project's mise.toml nu pin before writing any $err access, and the recommendation to note the boundary in any test asserting on error shape so a future pin bump fails loudly instead of silently.

Also worth a general note the incident generalises to: when a skill documents runtime behavior of a pinned tool, verifying against an ambient install is not verification. The pin is the runtime.

Source incident: brew-ops bundle test contract, runex-workflows branch test/brew-ops-bundle.

title: validate-security-hook.nu: ~30 of 35 cases never mutation-tested for passing-for-the-wrong-reason
description:
Raised by Gate 3 across PRs #248 and #249. Not a known defect — a known blind spot, in a suite that has already had two tests pass for the wrong reason.

The reviewer mutation-tested three points total: the untracked-pass mechanism and the --exclude-standard flag (PR #248), and the force-add predicate in both directions (PR #249). Each proved load-bearing. The remaining ~30 cases have never been probed.

WHY THIS MATTERS HERE SPECIFICALLY — this suite has a track record:
- Part 13 passed TRIVIALLY under the add-substring gate: the gate skipped the very pass the test was meant to exercise, so it proved nothing while showing green.
- Two stub fixtures modelled gitleaks output that real gitleaks never emits (silence), which forced a weaker invariant into the hook until the fixtures were fixed.
Both were caught by someone asking why a test was green, not by the suite.

The technique that works, already demonstrated in this repo: break the implementation deliberately and confirm the test goes red. The test author used it for the template-marker checks (four mutation shapes) and Gate 3 used it for the two mechanisms above. Neither found a false pass, but neither covered the bulk of the suite.

SCOPE: for each of the ~30 unprobed cases, mutate the specific hook behaviour it claims to exercise and confirm the case goes red. Where a case survives its mutation, either strengthen the assertion or document why the case is still worth keeping.

Prioritise: the four pre-existing exit-code cases, Parts 1-4 (the trigger-shape cases, which all share one stub methodology and could plausibly pass on a shared artifact), and Parts 11/12 (the allow-cases, where a fix that allows too much would pass).

AC: every case in test/validate-security-hook.nu has a recorded mutation that turns it red, or a documented reason it cannot be mutation-tested. Report any case that survives every mutation attempted — that is a case proving nothing.

title: Root mise.toml pins gitleaks = latest; bytes-verification parses an undocumented log string
description:
Split from claude-skills-267 Gate 3 round 2 finding R8.

PR #246 added a security invariant to scripts/gitleaks.nu that parses gitleaks' own 'scanned ~N bytes' stderr line to prove a scan covered something. That string is an undocumented log format, and root mise.toml:11 pins gitleaks = 'latest'.

VERIFIED by direct probe: dropping the tilde ('scanned 48 bytes') makes verified-clean false; a unit reword ('scanned ~48 KB') makes it false. Any upstream wording change therefore turns EVERY clean scan into a blocked scan repo-wide.

This fails closed, which is the safe direction, and the error text names the parse case — so it is survivable rather than dangerous. But it is an availability cliff sitting behind an unpinned dependency that auto-updates.

Options: pin gitleaks to a known-good version in root mise.toml and bump deliberately; or switch the invariant to a machine-readable signal (--report-format=json findings count plus an explicit scanned indicator) instead of scraping a human log line.

AC: an upstream gitleaks log-format change cannot silently break every scan in the repo.

title: Anti-fabrication pointers are now EARNED for the campaign-verified skills — 38 baseline debt entries can be reassessed
description:
Found by inspecting why 'mise test' reports 39 debt/bug entries after today's twelve merges. The number has not moved all session, and the reason is a premise that expired.

**The finding.** test/quality-baseline.json carries 38 anti_fab DEBT entries, all attributed to claude-skills-144 — which is CLOSED. Its close reason is the key text: the 4 genuine house-convention core skills got real per-skill pointers, and the remaining 40 were deliberately NOT swept, because 'a 44-file pointer sweep would have produced 44 green checks and zero examined claims'. That reasoning was correct at the time.

It is no longer correct for the campaign skills. Those 40 were then verified claim-by-claim across claude-skills-204 and 223 (PRs #219, #225, #233, #234) — both bees closed 2026-08-05. The claims HAVE now been examined, against live-installed toolchains for ansible, against slidevjs/slidev source for slidev, against the W3C and Material specs for tier 3, and against runex/beads/bees for tier 1. So a pointer added now is earned rather than a rubber stamp, which is precisely the distinction 144 was protecting.

Verified the entries are still live rather than stale: plugins/tools/slidev/skills/code/SKILL.md, plugins/tools/ansible/skills/ansible-inventory/SKILL.md and plugins/design/skills/accessibility/SKILL.md all contain ZERO occurrences of 'anti-fabrication' or 'anti_fab', and all three are named in the baseline.

**Scope rule, and it is the whole job.** Do NOT sweep all 38. Add a pointer ONLY where that skill's content was actually verified by the campaign, and determine that from each plugin's sources.toml — its last_full_check, its per-entry last_checked, and its unverified list, which several passes deliberately did not bump. Any skill the campaign did not cover keeps its DEBT entry and is left alone. Report the split rather than assuming the campaign covered everything: note that slidev's last_full_check was deliberately NOT bumped, and ansible's was not either because molecule-scenarios.md remains unverified — so 'the plugin was in the campaign' is not the same as 'this skill was fully verified'.

Each pointer must name that skill's actual claim area and what it was verified against, in the shape the 4 core skills already use. A generic paragraph is the rubber stamp 144 refused; if a skill has no checkable external claims, say that instead, as git's treatment did.

Then remove exactly the baseline entries that now pass. The ratchet is shrink-only, so removal is allowed and addition is not — if an entry cannot be removed, leave it and say why.

**Separate, smaller item in the same file.** One entry is duplicate_block attributed to claude-skills-148, which closed with an explicit assess-no-dedupe verdict: 21 shared normalised lines vs /core:git's 222, roughly 20:1 against, and cross-plugin self-containment rules out a pointer. Its close reason states 'dupe/28ccd32d stays in the baseline at 7 windows by design'. That is a permanent accepted exception, not debt to burn down, yet it is counted in the 'N debt/bug entries to burn down' total. Either give the baseline a class that distinguishes accepted-by-design from outstanding-debt, or exclude it from that message — a permanent entry inflating a burn-down number makes the number meaningless over time.

AC: pointers added only to campaign-verified skills, each naming its real claim area and verification source; the covered-vs-not split reported explicitly with sources.toml evidence; baseline entries removed only where the check now genuinely passes; the accepted-by-design duplicate_block entry distinguished from outstanding debt. mise test green.
close_reason:
PR #242 merged 1f71374. Debt 39 -> 21 (20 DEBT + 1 newly-classed ACCEPTED). 18 earned pointers added, 20 entries left as debt with per-skill reasons.

The premise this rested on: claude-skills-144 refused a pointer sweep because 'a 44-file pointer sweep would have produced 44 green checks and zero examined claims'. Correct then. The 40 skills were subsequently verified claim-by-claim under 204 and 223 (PRs #219, #225, #233, #234), so a pointer became earned rather than a stamp — for the skills actually covered.

The scoping was the job, and it discriminated rather than swept. Included where every backing source was campaign-dated with no live caveat: ansible x4, design x2, runex, wasm x2, zig x7, slidev code and export. Excluded with reasons: core/dagu/elixir/ui (never in 204/223 scope, sources predate it), six slidev skills each carrying at least one source explicitly marked not-re-verified, and ansible-testing.

ansible-testing is the judgement worth preserving. Its sources ARE verified with real corrections, but references/molecule-scenarios.md stays stale (pre-26.6.0 schema, removed --driver-name, dead 'molecule lint') and was only caveated. Since anti_fab is SKILL.md-scoped and presence-only, a pointer there WOULD have passed the check while asserting verification the skill's own sources deny. Gate 3 agreed the exclusion is right rather than over-cautious.

Note for anyone reading the check's output: anti_fab is PRESENCE-ONLY. Any of four substrings makes it pass, so the check cannot distinguish an earned pointer from a rubber stamp. A green run proves nothing about this class of work — the assurance is human judgement plus the sources trail, which is why the covered-vs-not split was the deliverable rather than the edits.

Gate 3 verified the zig 7 individually rather than as a block, since they share one upstream and one last_full_check. sources.md itemizes positive compile evidence for the four files that needed no corrections, and separately RETRACTS an earlier spot-check-as-full-pass claim — the record is honest about its own limits.

New ACCEPTED class: reclassifies claude-skills-148's permanent duplicate_block verdict so a by-design entry stops inflating a burn-down total it will never leave. Gate 3 proved it does not weaken the ratchet, testing four directions directly (count raised -> regression fires; count lowered -> stale_counts forces shrink; not-failing -> stale_keys; unrelated new key -> hard failure), and proved the new self-test fixture non-vacuous by mutation. Residual it flagged: an ACCEPTED relabel cannot silence a failure, but CAN misstate debt as by-design in the count, and only review catches that — the mandatory issue field is the audit trail.

Two small items recorded here rather than filed, because both are 'next time you touch this' conditions rather than ready work: zig/c-interop is the weakest evidentiary link of the seven (blanket 'all seven compiled' rather than an itemized per-claim entry — worth one line in sources.md at the next zig pass), and runex/SKILL.md's naming-drift note is now historical since claude-skills-239 was fixed upstream in runex PR #297, so it should be refreshed when that version pin next moves.

title: Nested-list entries crash the skills, commands and agents loops
description:
The type checks for skills, commands and agents test only 'str starts-with "list"', so a nested list such as skills: [["a"]] passes the check and enters the per-entry loop, where 'path join' raises an uncaught nu::shell::cant_convert. Identical for commands: [["a"]] and agents: [["a"]].

Pre-existing on main - verified by running main's validator against the same input, which crashes the same way. Not introduced by PR #229, which added the skills string form.

The shape is worth noting because it is the inverse of the shapes fixed so far. Every previous crash in this file came from a value that was the WRONG top-level type. This one is the right top-level type - it really is a list - carrying elements of the wrong type. A check that validates the container and not the elements admits it.

AC: guard each entry inside all three loops, rejecting a non-string entry with a clean error naming the field and the offending value's type. One shared helper is likely right rather than three copies. Reject fixtures per field for a nested list and for a list containing a number; verify by mutation per field - neuter the guard, confirm a case fails by clean stdout assertion rather than by crash, restore.

Note when fixturing: direct-call fixtures in this file have no subprocess isolation, so a reverted guard crashes the whole self-test instead of failing one case. Use the CLI-subprocess pattern.
close_reason: PR #230 merged as part of a class sweep — the bee understated itself: those sites crashed on ANY non-string entry, not only nested lists (skills: [42] crashes identically). Guarded via an is-string predicate matching the file's existing is-kebab-case/is-semver family, using 'continue' in the loops so a bad entry REPORTS and later valid entries still validate — verified, not assumed

title: Five documented plugin.json fields have no type validation at all
description:
validate-plugin.nu has type checks for only five fields: dependencies, keywords, skills, commands, agents. Upstream documents non-array forms for several more, and those have NO validation whatsoever - they accept literal garbage.

Verified empirically during the plan review for claude-skills-248, on main at 04d2866: a manifest with lspServers set to 42, or workflows set to true, validates with 0 errors, 0 warnings, exit 0. Inline hooks and mcpServers objects and a string outputStyles also pass, which is correct per upstream - but they pass because nothing checks them, not because anything permits them.

The fields upstream documents as flexible: skills, commands, agents, workflows (string | array); hooks, mcpServers, lspServers (string | array | object); outputStyles (string | array); experimental.themes and experimental.monitors (string | array). Of these, only skills currently REJECTS its documented form (that is claude-skills-248); commands and agents were fixed in PR #228; the remaining five are unchecked.

Worth noting how this was found, because the framing was backwards. The question asked was whether 248 was mis-scoped - whether other fields also reject a documented form, repeating the fix-one-instance mistake that made claude-skills-247 take six rounds. The answer was no: the adjacent defect is the opposite shape. Not too strict in more places, but no checking at all.

Note also that zero manifests in this repo use a non-array or object form for any of these fields, so mise run test:plugins passes without exercising any of them. Any fix here needs self-test fixtures; a repo manifest will not pin it.

AC: add type validation for workflows, hooks, mcpServers, lspServers and outputStyles matching what upstream documents for each, accepting every documented shape and rejecting others with a clean error. Reject fixtures per field for a value invalid under all documented shapes (a number or bool), plus accept fixtures per documented shape. Verify by mutation per field: neuter the check, confirm a case fails by clean stdout assertion rather than by crash.
close_reason:
PR #231 merged 28b4fd7. Closed the whole component-path-fields class, not just the five in the AC: workflows, hooks, mcpServers, outputStyles, lspServers (AC scope) plus experimental.themes, experimental.monitors, userConfig, channels, and a record-type guard on experimental itself. Self-test 122 -> 151 cases.

Gate 3 finding worth recording: nushell describes an array of records as table<...>, NOT list<...>, so this file's existing 'str starts-with list' idiom false-rejected upstream's own documented channels shape ([{server, userConfig}]). Caught empirically before merge, fixed with a shared is-array-type helper accepting both prefixes, applied to all 8 array-accepting checks. Gate 3 independently reproduced the table describe against real opened JSON (not nushell literals, which behave differently) and grep-verified all 8 call sites.

Fixture placement held under adversarial test: only 'experimental' has crash-capable get -o drilling, so only its wrong-type fixture needed cli_cases subprocess isolation; the other 28 went in-process correctly. Five independent mutations by Gate 3, all failing by clean stdout assertion rather than crash.

title: skills field: validator rejects the bare string form that upstream documents
description:
Upstream's plugin manifest table (code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference) documents skills as 'string | array', the same as commands and agents, and describes the string form as replacing the default directory. validate-plugin.nu rejects a bare string for skills.

This is the identical defect claude-skills-246 covered for commands and agents, in a third field. It surfaced while reversing 246: the fix there restored commands/agents to accept a string, and the same upstream table row shows skills has always been in the same position.

Worth recording how 246 went, because it applies here directly. The first attempt narrowed OUR docs to array-only to match the validator. That was wrong - plugin-schema.md describes itself as the schema for Claude Code plugin.json files, so its subject is upstream's schema, not this validator's subset. Narrowing turned an honestly-recorded divergence into a codified falsehood while the validator kept rejecting manifests upstream loads. The correct direction was to make the validator accept what upstream accepts.

Also carry forward the implementation note from 246: do NOT coerce the string into the array-entry loop. That loop enforces must-be-a-file and calls into per-entry content validation, so coercion would flag a legitimate directory as an invalid file entry. Existence-check the string as a single path instead.

AC: accept a bare string for skills, existence-checked as a single path, without routing it through the array-entry loop. Add accept fixtures proving the string form genuinely resolves rather than merely type-checking, plus a reject fixture for a value invalid under both shapes (a number). Verify by mutation - neuter the accept path and confirm a case fails by clean stdout assertion rather than by crash.
close_reason: PR #229 merged — validator accepts a bare string for skills, existence-checked as a single path, mirroring the commands/agents fix from #228 but with the correct skills-specific reasoning: the array loop treats each entry as its own skill dir and looks for <entry>/SKILL.md, so coercing a parent-of-skill-dirs would wrongly report 'missing SKILL.md file' (verified by execution, not assumed). Docs now state the ADD-vs-REPLACE distinction — a skills string adds to the default scan while commands/agents replace theirs — including upstream's marketplace-root exception, which this repo's own all-skills plugin (source: './') is an instance of. Two adjacent crash shapes found during review were pre-existing and are tracked as claude-skills-251 and 252

title: validate-plugin.nu: unguarded 'from yaml' crashes on malformed frontmatter
description:
validate-skill-md (around line 664) and validate-agent-md (around line 734) call 'from yaml' on frontmatter content with no try/catch. A real SKILL.md whose frontmatter is malformed - for example '---\nname: [unclosed\n---' - crashes uncaught with 'Could not load YAML: did not find expected , or ]', exit 1. Zero mutation required, plain on-disk file.

This is the fourth instance of one defect class in this file, and the pattern of how they were found matters more than any single crash. Three earlier ones were unguarded 'open' calls: the agents path (fixed in PR #223), the skills path (PR #224), and the marketplace path (folded into #224). Each was found one review round at a time. A sweep for 'open' calls found the third; this one is a parse step one line after an open, carrying the identical trust assumption, and was missed by that sweep because it is a different function name.

Related, same PR's review: the new marketplace guard catches a directory but not malformed CONTENT. A non-JSON marketplace file crashes at the '.plugins' access with incompatible_path_access. The try/catch pattern already used at lines 149 and 237 is the shape that prevents this.

The harm in every case is the same and is why these matter beyond tidiness: failures accumulate and print only at the end of a run, so an uncaught crash mid-suite suppresses every finding recorded before it plus the final report.

AC: guard both 'from yaml' calls and the marketplace content parse, reporting a clean error rather than crashing. Add reject-direction fixtures for malformed YAML frontmatter and a malformed marketplace file, each verified by mutation - revert the guard and confirm a case fails BY ASSERTION rather than by crash. Then sweep once for the class rather than the function name: any operation that assumes well-formed content, not just 'open' and 'from yaml'.
close_reason: PR #228 merged — six crash shapes fixed, not the one the bee named. Both 'from yaml' calls guarded against two shapes each: content that raises, and content that parses to a non-record WITHOUT raising, which try/catch cannot catch (the claude-skills-243 defect in YAML). Plus the marketplace open, the bare .plugins cell-path access, a wrong-typed plugins value, and an entry that is a record but lacks a name key — that last one because nushell's 'where name == x' RAISES on such a record rather than skipping it, so a record-only pre-filter did not protect the name access. Four direct-call fixtures were replaced with CLI-subprocess equivalents after discovering they had no isolation, so a reverted guard crashed the whole self-test instead of failing one case. Remaining in this class: claude-skills-249

title: commands and agents string form is documented but rejected by the validator
description:
plugin-schema.md:21-22 documents "commands": "string | array" and "agents": "string | array", and SKILL.md:50/52 agrees, describing the string form as a directory to scan. validate-plugin.nu rejects a string value for both fields with an error.

The validator's behaviour predates PR #223. That PR added self-test fixtures (commands_not_array_errors, agents_not_array_errors) asserting the current reject behaviour, which means the divergence is now pinned by tests - fixing it later is a test-flipping change. Both fixtures carry why: comments recording this explicitly so nobody reads them as endorsing the behaviour.

The resolve path was investigated during #223 and deliberately not taken, for a reason worth preserving: the documented string form means directory-SCANNING semantics - find and validate every file under that directory - which this validator does not implement for commands or agents today, though it does for skills. A naive fix that coerced the string into a one-element list and reused the per-entry loop would flag a genuinely valid directory as an invalid single file entry. That is the same defect class #223 had just fixed elsewhere, so shipping it would have traded one bug for another.

AC: pick one and implement it. Either (a) implement the documented directory-scan semantics for the string form, mirroring how skills already handles scanning, and re-point the two fixtures; or (b) narrow plugin-schema.md and SKILL.md to array-only if directory scanning is not wanted, and keep the fixtures as-is. Do not coerce string to a single-element list - that satisfies the type check while producing a wrong result.
close_reason: PR #228 merged — resolved by making the VALIDATOR accept the string form, not by narrowing the docs. The first attempt narrowed plugin-schema.md and SKILL.md to array-only; Gate 3 fetched upstream and found code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference documents commands and agents as 'string | array' with bare-string examples. Since plugin-schema.md describes itself as the schema for Claude Code plugin.json files, narrowing it would have documented this validator's limitation as the specification — turning an honestly-recorded divergence into a codified falsehood while still rejecting manifests upstream loads. The string is existence-checked as a single path, deliberately NOT coerced into the array-entry loop, which enforces must-be-a-file and would flag a legitimate directory. Same defect exists for the skills field: claude-skills-248

title: validate-plugin-file crashes on JSON that nu parses leniently as a bare scalar
description:
validate-plugin.nu's invalid-JSON guard assumes 'from json' either yields a record or raises. Nushell parses JSON5-style bare scalars leniently, so content like 'not valid json {{{' comes back as a plain string rather than raising - verified: "not valid json {{{" | from json | describe returns string.

The try/catch therefore never fires, and the downstream code that expects a record crashes with nu::shell::only_supports_this_input_type instead of printing the documented 'Invalid JSON syntax' message.

Found during claude-skills-238 (PR #221). It surfaced because a test fixture intended to be invalid JSON was silently parsing as valid, which is also worth noting on its own: 'obviously malformed' input may not be malformed to nushell.

The SKILL.md claim that the script 'checks JSON syntax' and references/validation-and-troubleshooting.md both need updating once the guard is fixed, since today the guard covers less than they describe.

AC: reject non-record results from 'from json' (bare string, number, bool, list) with the documented Invalid JSON syntax error rather than letting them reach code that assumes a record. Add reject-direction fixtures for each scalar shape, using content verified to actually parse leniently rather than content assumed to be malformed.
close_reason: PR #227 merged — both guard holes fixed (validate-plugin-file and validate-plugin-content), not just the one the bee named. Gate 3 constructed 14 non-record shapes and ran each against pre- and post-fix validators: bare scalars, arrays, empty array, top-level null, empty file, invalid UTF-8, and 500-deep nesting all crashed before and are cleanly rejected now. A record with no keys was already handled. Only SKILL.md:144 needed the doc correction — the bee's claim that validation-and-troubleshooting.md also overstates was wrong and is corrected on that bee

comments.text:
Correction: this bee was closed in error during the PR #224 merge and immediately reopened. PR #224 did NOT address it — that PR fixed the validate-skill-md directory crash, the symlink false-positive in both content guards, and the unguarded marketplace open. The lenient-JSON5 scalar crash described here is untouched and still reproduces.

Scope note added from the plan review of this bee's brief: there are TWO instances of this guard hole, not one. validate-plugin-file has it, and validate-plugin-content has an identical one with its own try/catch and a different message ('Failed to parse plugin.json'). A fix patching only the first leaves the marketplace and self-test call paths crashing on the same input.

Compatibility constraint for whoever takes it: the existing self-test fixture cli_invalid_json_exit_1 pins exit 1 plus the exact 'Invalid JSON syntax' message for the properly-raising shape. Route scalars into that same message or add a separate fixture - do not restructure the catch.

One correction to this bee's own text: it says references/validation-and-troubleshooting.md carries a similar overstating claim. It does not. The only related line there sits under a heading stating 'No script detects these', describing Claude Code's loader rather than the validator, and overstates nothing. SKILL.md:144 is the only site that needs correcting.

title: 11 more always-pass-neuterable checks in validate-plugin.nu's skills/commands/agents surface
description:
PR #221 closed the always-pass coverage gap for is-kebab-case, is-semver, validate-skill-md, validate-agent-md's non-model checks, and the description/keywords marketplace-agreement check. A mutation sweep during that PR's review found 11 further checks with the same property.

The remaining surface is the skills/commands/agents array-type and path-existence checks - for example the 'keywords must be an array' type assertion and the 'Skill directory ... missing SKILL.md file' existence check. Each can be neutered to always-pass with the suite staying green.

The asymmetry that makes this matter is unchanged from claude-skills-238: mise run test:plugins runs the marketplace path against 30 real plugins, so a check mutated to always FAIL is caught immediately, while a check neutered to always PASS is invisible to the entire CI. --strict is now wired into test:plugins, which makes every one of these load-bearing.

claude-skills-238 stays open until these have reject-direction fixtures.

AC: add reject-direction fixtures for each of the 11, and verify per check by mutation - neuter to always-pass, confirm at least one case fails, restore, confirm green. Report the exact stub and exact case count per check. Case count alone is not evidence: a suite can grow substantially without closing any of these.
close_reason: PR #223 merged — all 11 array-type and path-existence checks now have reject-direction fixtures, each verified by TWO mutations (obvious always-pass plus a non-equivalent one). Two survivors were found and fixed during the work: a dirname mutation that survived because the fixture's parent directory was also missing, and a 'right check, wrong report' mutation that survived because every fixture asserted counts only — closed by adding message-substring assertions to all 11. Also fixed a crash reachable with NO mutation: a documented-valid 'agents: ["agents"]' directory form hit an unguarded open. The guard is 'path type != file' rather than '== dir', because path type returns empty for a path a broken existence check wrongly claims exists

title: runex: execution_class/1 guard uses 'runex_sub' but the registered driver name is 'runex'
description:
Discovered while verifying the runex skill's driver documentation for claude-skills-223 (PR #219).

Runex.Driver.execution_class/1 guards its workflow class with ~w[workflow runex_sub federation]. The @drivers map registers the driver under the name 'runex', not 'runex_sub'. So execution_class("runex") returns "other" rather than "workflow".

The module's own doc comment describes the grouping the guard was evidently meant to produce, so the doc and the code disagree - which is how this surfaced: the skill documented the class table from the doc comment, and the table does not match what the function returns for a real registered driver name.

Verified read-only against ~/github/runex origin/main (commit 627f284f) via git show, no checkout. This is an upstream runex defect, not a claude-skills one - the skill text was corrected in PR #219 to attribute class labels to the @drivers map's own groupings rather than to execution_class/1, so nothing in this repo now asserts the wrong behaviour.

Filed here because the runex tracker is not in scope for this session. Someone with runex write access should decide whether the guard should read 'runex' or the driver should register as 'runex_sub', and check whether anything downstream depends on the current 'other' classification.

AC: reconcile the guard clause with the registered driver name upstream, or confirm the current behaviour is intended and fix the module doc comment instead.
close_reason:
Fixed upstream in runex PR #297, merged as 2b51c61.

The defect was larger than filed: TWO dead names in the execution_class/1 workflow guard, not one. @drivers registers 'runex' => Runex.Drivers.RunexSub — module named RunexSub, driver string 'runex' — so the guard's 'runex_sub' matched nothing and execution_class('runex') returned 'other'. Guard fixed to read 'runex'; renaming the driver was ruled out because it would break every workflow TOML, doc and persisted step row.

'federation' is the second unregistered name but was deliberately KEPT: Runex.Drivers.Federation exists with dispatch logic written, and README.md:208-210 states it is not yet wired into the registry and is roadmap work. Gate 3 disagreed on this and said so rather than smoothing it over — under strict YAGNI it would have dropped the entry, since a guard entry for an unregistered name is the same SHAPE as the defect being fixed. It did not block, on the reasoning that the bug misclassified real reachable data while the federation entry is unreachable through Step.changeset's validate_inclusion gate and can misclassify nothing. Now carries an explanatory comment so the next reader does not file it again.

The durable artifact is a property test driven by names/0: every registered driver must classify to something other than 'other'. Gate 3 mutation-tested it by reverting the guard — it fails, and names the offending driver in its message rather than asserting a bare boolean. That is what makes this drift class unreproducible.

A test asserting execution_class('runex_sub') == 'workflow' had pinned the defect — a test for a driver name that could never exist. Replaced with the 'runex' case that was missing and would have caught this.

No backfill needed: execution_class is not persisted anywhere in runex (verified across priv/ migrations, schemas and lib/). It is computed per-payload in run_metrics_worker.ex:158 and POSTed to the external RUNEX_METRICS_SINK_URL sink. Impact is historical: every metrics event for a 'runex' step reported execution_class 'other' to that sink. Anyone consuming it for grouping should know the series changes from here.

Not deployed — merging to runex main is separate from a Mini deploy, which is the operator's call.

title: validate-plugin.nu has no strict mode; an invented plugin.json field keeps CI green
description:
PR #213 (claude-skills-219) made validate-plugin.nu WARN on unrecognized plugin.json fields instead of silently accepting them. That matches upstream's documented default: 'claude plugin validate reports unrecognized fields as warnings, not errors... A plugin with only unrecognized-field warnings still passes validation and loads at runtime.'

Upstream also documents 'Pass --strict to treat warnings as errors' and recommends it for CI. This repo wired no equivalent, so an invented or typo'd field in a repo plugin keeps mise test green with only log visibility. Verified during Gate 3: injecting notARealField into a real plugin produced a visible warning and exit 0.

That is claude-skills-219's original complaint in attenuated form — the field is no longer invisible, but nothing fails.

Two facts that make this cheap: all 30 repo plugins are currently warning-free, so promoting warnings to errors in test:plugins would be safe today, and this repo is deliberately stricter than upstream elsewhere (it rejects allowed-tools on skills, which upstream permits).

AC: add a strict mode mirroring upstream's --strict and decide whether CI uses it. If CI stays permissive, record why, since the warn-only posture is the thing a future reader will question.
close_reason: PR #217 merged — --strict mode added mirroring upstream's documented flag, wired into test:plugins. Two plugins that warned on main (core's model casing, all-skills' unreachable sources.md path) were fixed first, so all 30 pass under strict. The bee's premise that all plugins were warning-free was false and is corrected on the record

title: MISE_VERSION ARG in Dockerfile.claude-code is declared but never consumed
description:
templates/Dockerfile.claude-code (and the copy embedded in its SKILL.md) declares ARG MISE_VERSION=2026.5.0, but the image installs mise via 'curl -fsSL https://mise.run | sh', which always fetches the latest release at build time. The ARG is never referenced by the install step.

Consequence: the pin is decorative. A reader reasonably concludes the image is pinned to a known mise version; two builds a month apart will silently contain different mise versions. It also means bumping the ARG - the obvious maintenance action - changes nothing.

Found during claude-skills-176 while registering fenced version literals. It was recorded in the registry entry's notes rather than fixed, because this is a correctness bug in the Dockerfile, not a freshness question, and 176 asked only for a detection signal.

AC: either consume the ARG in the install step so the pin is real (mise.run supports version selection - verify the exact mechanism against mise's install docs rather than inferring a flag), or delete the ARG so nothing claims a pin that does not exist. Whichever is chosen, apply it to BOTH the template and the copy inside SKILL.md, which must not drift from each other.
close_reason: PR #212 merged 61debb5 — MISE_VERSION ARG now consumed via mise.run's own env-var contract (verified by fetching the install script: version=${MISE_VERSION:-v...} then ${version#v}); ARG confirmed in scope (single-stage Dockerfile); both copies byte-identical

title: version-check-methods.md worked examples use a def signature that does not parse on nu 0.113.1
description:
Every worked nushell example in plugins/tools/claude-code/skills/skill-update/references/version-check-methods.md declares its command as:

    def f [args] -> string { ... }

That return-type form does not parse on nushell 0.113.1. The accepted syntax is a full signature with an input type, e.g.

    def f [args]: nothing -> string { ... }

Consequence: a reader copying any of these examples gets a parse error, not a version lookup. The file is the reference SKILL.md points at for parsing examples, so it is the surface most likely to be copied verbatim.

Scope: all six sections. Three are pre-existing (present since the original github-releases/hex-pm/crates-io sections landed); the three added in PR #208 for npm/docker-hub/endoflife-date copied the same shape. Found during Gate 3 of PR #208 and left out of scope there as inherited rather than introduced.

AC: correct the signature in all six sections and run each example to confirm it parses and returns the documented output. Sweep the repo for the same form elsewhere - it is likely copied into other skills' examples. Verify against nu 0.113.1 specifically rather than assuming, since nushell is pre-1.0 and syntax has shifted between minor versions.
close_reason: PR #216 merged — all six version-check-methods.md signatures corrected to ': nothing ->'; each example executed live on nu 0.113.1 and returns its documented value; repo-wide sweep found no remaining instances

title: endoflife-date check_method reports an EOL version as latest; no eol sentinel
description:
The endoflife-date check_method added in PR #208 returns the newest release cycle's latest patch unconditionally. For a fully end-of-life product this means confidently reporting an EOL version as 'latest' - verified live: centos returns '8 (2111)'.

The decision to ship it this way was deliberate and the rationale is internally consistent: github-releases, hex-pm and crates-io do not filter for 'still supported' either, and the question a staleness check asks is only 'is something newer available to pin'. It is documented in a comment on check-endoflife-date and in references/version-check-methods.md.

Two reasons it still deserves a follow-up:
- claude-skills-176, the issue that motivated adding this method at all, is explicitly about detecting EOL pins. A method named after endoflife.date that cannot report end-of-life is a surprising shape for its primary consumer.
- The data is already in hand. The API response carries each cycle's eol field, so a sentinel costs zero additional network calls.

AC: add an eol signal to the endoflife-date method (surface the cycle's eol field, and/or prefer the newest SUPPORTED cycle with the EOL state reported separately), or record a decision not to and note in claude-skills-176 that EOL detection must come from elsewhere.
close_reason: PR #216 merged — check-endoflife-status returns {latest, eol, cycle}, parsing the cycle's ISO eol date via into datetime rather than truthiness (centos eol=true, nodejs eol=false, verified live). Library-level per the AC's first alternative; report wiring tracked as claude-skills-237

title: docker-hub check_method returns a tag name, not a version - drift never transitions
description:
The docker-hub check_method added in PR #208 (claude-skills-210) queries the tag list with ordering=last_updated and returns the newest tag NAME. For library/node that is 'lts-trixie-slim'.

Gate 3 found the resulting signal is degenerate in both directions:
- Following the template's own prescribed usage (current_version = 'unknown' or a rolling marker) classifies as no-pin FOREVER. It can never flag staleness - including for its flagship worked example, node:16-buster-slim, which is the exact case claude-skills-176 wanted covered.
- Setting a version-shaped pin instead reads stale=yes forever, because the newest tag on a rolling alias is re-pushed daily and never equals the pin.

Neither state ever transitions, so the method cannot produce an actionable drift report as shipped.

The documentation is honest about what it does, which is why this was not treated as a merge blocker. The design is the gap.

Fix direction suggested by the reviewer: query Docker Hub's per-tag endpoint (/v2/repositories/{repo}/tags/{tag}) so a specific pinned tag can be compared, or add a tag-filter companion field so the method can select a comparable series rather than the newest tag overall.

AC: make the docker-hub method able to report a state transition for a realistically pinned image, or record why it cannot and adjust the schema documentation so nobody adopts it expecting drift detection.
close_reason: PR #216 merged — docker_tag field added; check-docker-hub-tag queries the per-tag endpoint and compares the content digest, so the signal now transitions in both directions. Verified end-to-end on a REAL adopted entry (agent-sandboxing's previously-untracked FROM debian:13-slim pin), not just a fixture

title: check-version-bumps self-test covers only pure functions; all-skills wiring is unguarded
description:
PR 203 (claude-skills-207) added semver-compare and classify-bump as pure functions with 18 self-test fixtures. Gate 3 confirmed the fix works end-to-end by reproducing the original regression shape, but noted the self-test asserts only at the pure-function layer.

The all-skills scope logic in main (around lines 166-174 of test/check-version-bumps.nu) is not covered. A future refactor that drops or breaks that block would leave every self-test green, because the fixtures never exercise the path that decides whether all-skills is in scope at all. That is the exact failure mode the original bug had - the logic was simply absent and nothing noticed.

AC: add a git-fixture integration test that constructs a real repo state (a plugin content change plus an unbumped all-skills) and asserts the script exits non-zero, so the wiring itself is guarded rather than only the helpers it calls.
close_reason: PR #215 merged — --integration-self-test builds a real git repo and invokes the script as a subprocess, guarding main's all-skills wiring. Proven load-bearing: deleting the wiring block leaves --self-test green at 22 cases while the integration test fails

title: sources:validate reports 22-23 errors; 9 are dead or unreachable non-crates URLs, not rate limiting
description:
Two separate PRs this session attributed the full sources:validate error count to pre-existing crates.io rate limiting. A Gate 3 reviewer reproduced the run (272 checked - 250 pass, 0 redirect, 0 fail, 22 error) and extracted the actual list: only 13 are crates.io (12 rust crates plus crates.io/policies under claude-code). The other 9 are different hosts entirely:

- 4 github.com blob/tree URLs (anthropics/skills x2, hexpm API.md, anthropics/claude-code tree)
- vinnie357/runex (private repo, anonymous HEAD fails - known and expected)
- molecule.readthedocs.io
- butunclebob.com (I/O error)
- m3.material.io

The error-classification work in claude-skills-212 covers github-releases, hex-pm and crates-io fetch paths. It does not address these: a github.com blob URL 404 is a dead documentation link, not a rate limit, and needs a different signal.

Two problems worth separating. First, the URLs themselves may be genuinely rotted and need repointing or removal. Second, an undifferentiated 'error' bucket is what let two independent agents mis-attribute the whole batch to one cause without anyone noticing - the tool made the wrong inference easy.

AC: triage each of the 9. Repoint or remove dead links. Consider whether sources:validate should distinguish a 404 on a documentation URL from a transient network error, so the summary line cannot be read as one homogeneous cause. The private-repo case is expected and should be reported as such rather than as an error.
close_reason: PR #220 merged — sources-validate-urls now classifies dead/blocked/rate-limited/private/error instead of one undifferentiated error bucket, by reusing classify-fetch-error from sources-lib rather than duplicating it. The 14 crates.io entries were NOT dead: the website 404s to automated clients while the API path returns 200 from the same egress with the same UA, so they now cross-check via crates.io/api/v1/crates/<name> and pass. Six genuinely dead links repointed (including a spec URL that had rotted twice), plus three duplicate references outside sources.toml. Follow-ups: claude-skills-241 (table truncation makes per-row detail unreadable), claude-skills-242 (a genuinely dead crate under-claims as blocked)

comments.text:
Root cause found during Gate 3 of PR #208, and the error set is worse than 'transient network noise'. A reviewer re-swept all 23 with curl: 14 persistent crates.io anti-bot 403s, 2 REAL 404s on anthropics/skills blob URLs (content moved), dead steveyegge.github.io/beads/, dead butunclebob.com, a private-repo 404 (vinnie357/runex, expected), and one HEAD-405 artifact (m3.material.io is alive via GET). None are transient.

Root cause: test/sources-validate-urls.nu classifies from $err.msg, which nushell sets to a generic 'Network failure' for 404s. That is the SAME bug class claude-skills-212 fixed in sources-lib.nu — the fix was applied to the check/report/stale path but not to the URL validator.

Concrete follow-up work, beyond the triage this bee already asks for:
- Port catch-http-error from sources-lib.nu into sources-validate-urls.nu so a 404 is reported as dead rather than as generic network failure.
- Add a HEAD to GET fallback: m3.material.io returns 405 to HEAD and is reported as an error despite being alive.
- Fix or remove the 2 dead anthropics/skills blob URLs and the dead butunclebob.com link.
- Report the known-private repo as such rather than as an error.

This also explains why two independent agents mis-attributed the batch in one session: the tool renders every failure identically, so 'pre-existing rate limiting' was the available guess rather than a checkable claim.

title: validate-plugin.nu accepts any unknown plugin.json field - denylist has no allowlist counterpart
description:
validate-plugin.nu checks unknown fields against a fixed denylist (invalid_fields = [dependencies, category, strict, source, tags]). Anything not on that list passes.

Demonstrated during Gate 3 of PR 205: a plugin.json containing {"notARealField":"garbage"} validates with 0 errors and 0 warnings.

Consequence: the validator cannot catch a typo'd or invented field name, and 'the validator accepts field X' is not evidence that X is legitimate. That mattered concretely in PR 205, where the correct conclusion (no validator change needed for outputStyles/lspServers/experimental) happened to be right for the wrong reason.

AC: decide whether an allowlist of upstream-documented fields is warranted, or whether unknown fields should warn rather than pass silently. Note the denylist itself is separately wrong about dependencies - see the sibling bee. Prefer warn-on-unknown over hard-fail so a new upstream field does not break every plugin overnight.
close_reason: PR #213 merged — allowlist of 23 documented fields with warn-on-unrecognized, matching upstream's documented default (warnings, not errors). notARealField now produces a visible warning where it previously passed silently. Strict mode tracked as claude-skills-234

title: Apple Container --rm does not reliably remove the container on 1.0.0
description:
Observed directly: 'container run --rm --network default alpine:latest sh -c ...' left a stopped container behind despite --rm. This is very likely the accumulation mechanism behind roughly 300 stopped containers found on a dev host, a large share of them anonymous gitleaks-image containers — consistent with repeated gitleaks scans never being reaped, since this repo's gitleaks task also relies on --rm.

AC: reproduce on a disposable test; document the real behaviour in the container skill's Container Lifecycle or Troubleshooting section; consider whether the gitleaks script should add an explicit cleanup rather than relying on --rm.

Context worth preserving: an agent deleting 'its own' leftover container ran 'container rm -f $(container ls -aq)', which has no filter and removed every container on the host including several k8s control planes. Images and named volumes survived; container state did not. Two lessons — inspect the target list before a destructive command, and never splat an unfiltered ls into rm.
close_reason: PR #204 merged af0f8af — --rm unreliability documented at 1.0.0 as an operator observation, named-container cleanup added to both container paths

title: gitleaks task has no non-container runtime path
description:
plugins/core/skills/security/scripts/gitleaks.nu detects a container runtime and shells out to 'container run --rm' (or docker/colima). On a host where docker and colima are both absent, the mandated pre-commit gitleaks gate is unavailable entirely — confirmed during this session.

A native gitleaks binary IS available via mise at ~/.local/share/mise/installs/gitleaks/latest/gitleaks and was used successfully as a fallback.

Second, related trap found the same session: a shell function named 'gitleaks' can shadow the mise binary and silently route a bare 'gitleaks ...' invocation through 'container run'. Anyone expecting the native binary gets a container instead.

AC: add a native-binary path (prefer 'mise exec gitleaks@latest -- gitleaks ...' or the resolved binary) with the container path as fallback, or at minimum detect 'no runtime available' and say so explicitly rather than failing opaquely. Document the shadowing trap in the security skill.
close_reason: PR #204 merged af0f8af — native-first runtime selection in gitleaks.nu and the pre-commit hook, explicit error when nothing available, shadowing trap documented

title: sources.toml check_method has no npm, Docker Hub, or endoflife.date method
description:
test/validate-sources.nu restricts check_method to github-releases | hex-pm | crates-io | manual | none. claude-skills-176 asked for a freshness signal for version literals inside code fences and explicitly named npm, GitHub releases, endoflife.date and Docker Hub as the sources to query.

Consequence: the bee's own worked example — node:16-buster-slim in github/skills/act/references/setup-and-config.md — is not merely untracked, it is UNEXPRESSIBLE under the current schema. PR #197 hardened the existing sources:check/stale/report tooling and fixed a false-positive bug that had made it unusable (152 unknown-pin entries reported as drift), but the fenced-literal half of 176 cannot be delivered without this.

claude-skills-176 stays OPEN against this.

AC: extend CHECK_METHODS with at least a Docker Hub tag method and an npm method; keep the intentionally-pinned rationale in the entry's notes field rather than reserving a new schema field.
close_reason: PR #208 merged 9d03c65 — npm, docker-hub and endoflife-date check_methods added with parse functions tested against captured live responses. Known limitations tracked as claude-skills-225 (docker-hub drift never transitions) and 226 (no EOL sentinel)

title: Add a lint for braced CLAUDE_* in SKILL.md and commands/*.md bodies
description:
The braced form of CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT / CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR expands at load time when it appears in a skill or command BODY, substituting one machine's absolute cache path pinned to an installed plugin version. Hand-fixed three times with no check guarding it: claude-skills-169, 172, 178.

Allowed and must NOT be flagged: the braced form inside YAML frontmatter (the harness expands it at hook runtime, e.g. core/skills/security/SKILL.md), inside references/ (Read returns raw bytes), inside templates/, and in manifests.

The Gate 3 reviewer on PR #190 hand-classified exactly this rule across 614 files with zero false positives, so the rule is known-clean and ready to encode.

AC: error on braced CLAUDE_* in SKILL.md and commands/*.md bodies; no finding for frontmatter, references/, templates/, or manifests; self-test covering one of each.
close_reason: PR #207 merged 03f3cad — braced CLAUDE_* lint added for SKILL.md and commands/*.md bodies, exempting frontmatter/references/templates; regex widened to catch the shell-default form

title: anti_fab flags core/bees despite six explicit 'verified against 0.4.0' citations
description:
core/bees SKILL.md contains six 'Verified against bees 0.4.0' citations and zero fabricated claims — it does exactly what core:anti-fabrication asks. It still fails anti_fab, because the check only matches the literal substring 'fabricat' or a core:anti-fabrication reference, neither of which appears.

This is the same check that let claude-skills-126 (a skill documenting syntax that does not exist) pass while carrying no verification at all. The check is wrong in BOTH directions: false-negative on verified content missing the keyword, false-positive-pass on unverified content that happens to mention the topic.

AC (pick one or propose better):
- Recognize an explicit verification pattern (e.g. 'verified against X <version>') as satisfying anti_fab, alongside the current substring match.
- Or reclassify cases like this in the baseline as CHECK_DEFECT rather than DEBT, since the content is not debt — the check is.
Either way, note in the check's comment that presence-only detection cannot distinguish verified-content-missing-the-keyword from unverified-content-missing-the-keyword, which is the root cause of both directions.
close_reason: PR #207 merged 03f3cad — anti_fab now recognizes 'verified against X <version>'; core/bees passes on its six citations

title: anti_fab check only reads SKILL.md — real claims can sit unscanned in references/
description:
validate-skills-quality.nu:2237 loads reference files only for the examples/ref_depth checks; anti_fab (~2251) tests $content, which is SKILL.md body only. A thin pointer-style SKILL.md can carry zero fabrication risk while its references/*.md carries dense version-gated API claims the check cannot see.

Evidence: zig/build has a 19-line SKILL.md whose references/build.md (158 lines) asserts Zig 0.14/0.15 API removals (root_source_file removed from ExecutableOptions, .fingerprint required in build.zig.zon since 0.14) — none of it anti_fab-scanned. Same shape across zig's other 6 skills and both wasm skills. Note wasm/wit is 496/500 lines, so 'pointer file' does not describe all of them; what they share is routing real claims through references/.

Proof of impact (Gate 3, PR #201): replacing a skill's entire anti-fabrication paragraph with a bare '## Anti-fabrication' header and nothing else still scores 17/17.

AC: either extend anti_fab to scan the same refs the examples/ref_depth checks already load, or document in the check comment and benchmark docs that anti_fab is SKILL.md-only and reference-file risk is out of scope until claude-skills-141 covers it.
close_reason: PR #207 merged 03f3cad — resolved as AC option (b): anti_fab is SKILL.md-only by design, documented in the check comment and benchmark-skills.md with the Gate 3 fixture as rationale; reference-file risk tracked by claude-skills-141. The ref-scan was implemented, proven strictly weakening, and reverted

title: claude-code: benchmark-skills still restates validator-owned numbers and a divergent check list
description:
## Objective

Finish applying the single-source-of-truth principle in plugins/tools/claude-code/commands/benchmark-skills.md. PR #189 removed the hardcoded score denominator; three related instances survive, all found by its Gate 3 review.

## 1. The 500 denominator survives the argument that removed 11

The example scorecard still shows 120/500 and 380/500. 500 is validator-owned in exactly the way check_count is: test/validate-skills-quality.nu:2221 gates on > 500 and :2360 hardcodes the display string. If the drift argument was strong enough to remove one denominator it applies here. Currently correct, so nothing is broken - the fix is just internally inconsistent about its own principle.

## 2. The surviving bullets carry hard numbers

Step 3 lists <=1024 chars, <=64 chars, <=500 lines. All three match the validator today (verified at :2194, :2215, :2221). The sibling skill claude-skills-benchmark/SKILL.md:23 deliberately states intent WITHOUT figures - "length caps", "bounded body size" - which is what makes SKILL.md:21 "do not restate its checks here" survivable. The command restates the figures, one screen above the line PR #189 removed for the same reason.

## 3. The bullet list and the score now measure different sets

This became load-bearing only after #189 made the printed score authoritative; previously the agent hand-computed both from the same bullets, so they could not disagree.

The validator emits 17 keys: desc, use_when, third_person, kebab, name_len, reserved, lines, fm_schema, examples, ref_depth, anti_fab, allowed_tools, name_dir, links, orphans, invocations, version_pin.

Step 3 names two things the validator does not check - "imperative language", and "Has references/" (ref_depth tests nesting only; orphan detection is a separate key) - and omits seven it does: fm_schema, allowed_tools, name_dir, links, orphans, invocations, version_pin. Bullet 6 "Source coverage" belongs to test/validate-sources.nu, not this validator, as SKILL.md:23 itself says.

So the agent narrates one check set and reports a score computed from another.

## Acceptance criteria

- The command no longer embeds validator-owned numbers it does not own, or states explicitly why any that remain are safe.
- The narrated categories either match what the validator actually checks, or say plainly that they are a reading aid and not the check list.
- Decide whether the score column example should show a literal number at all.
- claude-code plugin + marketplace versions bumped, mise test exit 0, waivers not higher.

## Load skills

/core:anti-fabrication, /core:restraint, /claude-code:claude-skills
close_reason: Merged PR #195

title: sources: the sources.toml template documents current_version values the validator now rejects
description:
## Objective

Bring plugins/tools/claude-code/skills/skill-update/templates/sources.toml in line with rule b3_version_shape, merged in PR #187.

## The mismatch (found by a post-merge Gate 3 pass, verified)

skill-update SKILL.md line 24 points authors at this template as the annotated reference. The template says current_version may be:

    Exact version string (e.g. "0.10.0"), or "stable"/"rolling" for
    those constraints, or "unknown" when nobody has measured it yet.

and ships current_version = "" as its default. Measured against the merged regex:

    "stable"  -> REJECTED
    "rolling" -> REJECTED
    ""        -> REJECTED   (this is literally a frozen reject-case in the PR test suite)
    "unknown" -> accepted
    "0.10.0"  -> accepted

So an author who copies the template as instructed gets a file that fails validation on its first run, and two of the three documented alternatives to a version string are not accepted.

The template is also internally inconsistent: its last_checked = "unknown" IS accepted by b3_date, so the two adjacent fields behave differently than the comments imply.

## Why nothing caught it

validate-sources.nu globs plugins/**/skills/sources.toml. The template lives under .../skill-update/templates/, so it is not among the 28 validated files. Corpus impact today is zero and CI is green - the mismatch is invisible to every check.

## Note on stable/rolling

Those two strings are a sanctioned convention elsewhere - they are values of version_constraint. Deciding whether current_version may ALSO carry them is a real design question, not just a doc fix: if yes, b3_version_shape needs to accept them; if no, the template is simply wrong and should say so.

## Acceptance criteria

- The template documents only values the validator accepts, and its default is one of them.
- Decide and record whether "stable"/"rolling" are legal current_version values; make doc and check agree either way.
- Consider whether the template should be validated - a doc that ships an invalid example is the failure this epic keeps finding, and the glob currently cannot see it.
- claude-code plugin + marketplace versions bumped, mise test exit 0, corpus 28 validated / 0 pending.

## Load skills

/core:anti-fabrication, /core:nushell, /core:restraint, /claude-code:skill-update
close_reason: PR #188 merged — template no longer documents values the validator rejects, and new rule b6_template_drift reads the real template file. Guard hardened twice after review: it crashed and masked every other finding on 11 corruption shapes.

title: sources: an unquoted TOML float in current_version silently records a different version
description:
## Objective

Decide whether current_version (and the other version/date fields) should require a quoted string, so an unquoted numeric cannot silently record a value the author did not write.

## The finding (Gate 3 on PR #187, finding F5, verified by execution)

TOML parses an unquoted current_version = 1.10 as a FLOAT. scalar-str then coerces it, and nushell renders the float without its trailing zero:

    current_version = 1.10   ->  recorded as "1.1"
    current_version = 0.30   ->  recorded as "0.3"
    current_version = 1.0    ->  recorded as "1"

All three pass b3_version_shape, because "1.1" and "0.3" are perfectly valid shapes. The author wrote one version and the file records a different one, with no diagnostic.

## Why this matters more than it looks

The asymmetry with the sibling field is the point:

- An unquoted DATE (last_checked = 2026-01-01) parses as datetime, which scalar-str coerces to a long human string that fails the shape check - it FAILS LOUDLY.
- An unquoted FLOAT passes QUIETLY as a different value.

current_version exists to record the version the skill content was verified against. A silently altered pin is worse than a rejected one: it looks recorded, reads as intentional, and a later freshness check compares against something nobody chose. This is the same class as the stale-prose problem the whole sources epic was built to remove.

## Current exposure: latent, not active

Measured at filing: zero non-string current_version values in the corpus - every entry is a quoted string today. So nothing is corrupted now. The risk is a future author typing 1.10 without quotes.

## Why it was not fixed in PR #187

The fix is a type rule (must be a quoted string), not a regex change - out of scope for a PR whose contract was frozen around shape matching, and pinning the numeric-accepting behaviour was correct for consistency with every other field that routes through scalar-str.

## Acceptance criteria

- Decide: require a quoted string for current_version, or document the coercion as accepted with its lossiness stated.
- If a type rule is added, consider whether it should apply to the other scalar-str fields too - or state why current_version alone warrants it.
- Self-test cases covering unquoted 1.10, 1.0, and a quoted "1.10" that must still pass. Tests before implementation per the repo split.
- Corpus stays 28 validated / 0 pending, waivers not higher, mise test exit 0.

## Load skills

/core:anti-fabrication, /core:tdd, /core:nushell, /core:restraint
close_reason: PR #188 merged — current_version now requires a quoted string. An unquoted TOML numeric silently recorded a different version (1.10 -> 1.1); it is the only scalar-str consumer whose check lacked a natural type guard.

title: sources: b3_version_shape rejects PEP 440 pre-release forms without a separator
description:
## Objective

Decide whether b3_version_shape should accept PEP 440 style pre-release suffixes that carry no - or + separator, and either widen the regex or record the rejection as intended.

## The edge (found by Gate 3 on PR #187, recorded not fixed)

The suffix group in VERSION_SHAPE_RE requires a leading - or +:

    ^[A-Za-z]{0,10}[-.]?\d+(\.\d+){0,4}([-+][0-9A-Za-z.]+)?$

So these are accepted:  1.0.0-rc1
And these are rejected:  3.13.0rc1, 2.0b1, 1.0.post1, 1.0.0-rc.1+build.5

3.13.0rc1 is a genuine CPython release string. An author pinning a Python pre-release would be rejected, and the only difference from the accepted form is one hyphen - which is surprising rather than obviously wrong.

## Why it was not fixed in PR #187

- No corpus entry currently pins a pre-release, so nothing is broken today.
- The rule is severity fail, so it blocks loudly at authoring time rather than silently recording a corrupted value.
- The skill-update field table now publishes the regex verbatim, so a rejected author can read the rule instead of reverse-engineering it.

Widening was not done blind: the same PR established that a rule fitted to present data overfits, and that widening a check without measuring can convert a false positive into a false negative. That reasoning applies here too - a looser suffix group admits more junk.

## Acceptance criteria

- Decide: widen the suffix group to accept PEP 440 separator-less forms, or document the rejection as intentional in the skill-update field table so the edge is stated rather than discovered.
- If widened: self-test cases for 3.13.0rc1, 2.0b1, 1.0.post1, and 1.0.0-rc.1+build.5, plus a re-measure proving 0 of the corpus values are newly rejected AND that the previously-rejected junk set is still rejected. Tests before implementation per the repo split.
- Corpus stays 28 validated / 0 pending, waivers not higher, mise test exit 0.

## Load skills

/core:anti-fabrication, /core:tdd, /core:nushell, /core:restraint, /claude-code:skill-update
close_reason: PR #188 merged — suffix class aligned with SEMVER_RE (hyphenated prerelease accepted). PEP 440 separator-less and dual -pre+build recorded as deliberate won't-fix with measured reasoning. A first attempt admitted bare calendar dates; corrected so a hyphenated suffix requires a dotted base.

comments.text:
Second, distinct cause found by a post-merge Gate 3 pass — verified.

The suffix character class in VERSION_SHAPE_RE is [0-9A-Za-z.], which omits the hyphen. So hyphens INSIDE a prerelease are rejected:

    1.0.0-alpha-1  -> rejected by VERSION_SHAPE_RE, ACCEPTED by SEMVER_RE
    1.0.0-rc-2     -> rejected by VERSION_SHAPE_RE, ACCEPTED by SEMVER_RE

Both measured. The sharp part: SEMVER_RE is declared four lines above VERSION_SHAPE_RE in the same file and its suffix class IS [0-9A-Za-z.-], hyphen included. So the rule documented as deliberately wider than semver is in fact NARROWER than the strict-semver constant sitting directly above it. Changing the suffix class to ([-+][0-9A-Za-z.-]+)? closes this and would bring the two constants into agreement.

Correction to the reporting reviewer on one example: it cited 2.0.0-rc.1+exp.sha.5114f85 as a valid strict-SemVer form also rejected. It IS valid per the semver.org spec, but our own SEMVER_RE rejects it too, because SEMVER_RE permits only one suffix group rather than both a -prerelease and a +build. So that example does not demonstrate the shape-vs-semver contradiction - the two hyphen-in-prerelease cases above do.

This is separate from the PEP 440 cause already in this bee (a suffix with no separator at all). Both widen the same group; decide them together.

title: skills-quality: ref_depth cross-skill exemption is word-order sensitive and undocumented
description:
## Objective

Make the cross-skill exemption in has-unqualified-references-token either order-insensitive, or document the order requirement as a third accepted residual.

## The trap

test/validate-skills-quality.nu:270-271 computes the prefix as the text BEFORE the references/ token and passes only that to cross-skill-qualified:

    let idx = ($line | str index-of "references/")
    let prefix = ($line | str substring 0..<$idx)

So the exemption only fires when the qualifier precedes the path. A legitimate cross-skill pointer written the other way round is flagged as a same-skill nesting violation:

- Flagged:   Per `references/ci-discipline.md` in `/core:tdd`:
- Exempt:    Per `/core:tdd`s `references/ci-discipline.md`:

Both mean the same thing, and the target core/tdd/references/ci-discipline.md exists on disk in each case. Found during claude-skills-145: the brief handed to the fixing agent asserted the first form was exempt, the agent tested has-unqualified-references-token directly rather than trusting it, and found the opposite. That line was fixed by reordering the sentence, which is fine prose - but the next author has no way to know the order matters.

## Why it is worth addressing

The function header already documents two accepted residuals (heading lines, bare directory mentions without a filename). This is a third, and it differs in kind: the other two silently PASS things that should fail, while this one silently FAILS something legitimate. A false positive pushes an author to reword correct content, or to waive a check that was right to be quiet.

## Acceptance criteria

- Either the exemption considers the whole line rather than only the prefix, with self-test cases covering qualifier-before-path and qualifier-after-path, or the header comment gains a third accepted-residual bullet naming the order requirement.
- If the check is widened, verify it does not start exempting genuine same-skill links that merely mention another plugin elsewhere on the line - add a self-test case for that.
- Corpus stays clean, waivers not higher, mise test exit 0.

## Load skills

/core:anti-fabrication, /core:tdd, /core:nushell, /core:restraint
close_reason: PR #186 merged — order requirement documented as a third accepted residual, four load-bearing regression guards pin it against silent widening, and ref_depth now reports the nested filename. Widening was measured and rejected: it breaks the $-anchored repo-path qualifier form and converts a false positive into two false-negative shapes.

title: tweag: stale tree-sitter query-docs anchor in topiary/references/query-syntax.md
description:
