title: claude-code: benchmark-skills command says X/11 checks, matching neither its own list nor the validator
description:
## Objective

Reconcile the score denominator in plugins/tools/claude-code/commands/benchmark-skills.md with a real number.

## The discrepancy (found by Gate 3 on PR #182)

Line 46 instructs "Calculate score (X/11 checks passing)". Eleven matches nothing:

- the commands own bullet list immediately above it has 6 grouped bullets covering roughly 14 named sub-checks
- test/validate-skills-quality.nu scores each skill out of check_count, which is 17 as of claude-skills-191

So an agent following this command produces a denominator that disagrees with the validator the rest of the document points at. Pre-existing, not introduced by PR #182 - that PR corrected the adjacent Source coverage bullet, which is how this surfaced.

## Why it matters

Same species as claude-skills-191: a count in prose that no longer tracks the thing it counts. A benchmark command that reports X/11 while the validator reports X/17 will make two runs of the same skill look like different results.

## Acceptance criteria

- The denominator either matches the validators check_count, or the command stops printing a fixed denominator and reads it from the validator output.
- The bullet list and the denominator agree with each other.
- claude-code plugin + marketplace versions bumped, mise update-all-skills run, mise test exit 0.

## Load skills

/core:anti-fabrication, /core:restraint, /claude-code:claude-skills
close_reason: PR #189 merged — the hardcoded X/11 denominator is gone; the command now reads the score from the validator, which is the single source of truth its sibling skill already declared. Remaining validator-owned numbers filed as claude-skills-199.

title: skills-quality: check_count is off by one against the failure keys the loop can emit
description:
## Objective

Reconcile check_count in test/validate-skills-quality.nu with the number of distinct per-skill failure keys the loop can actually append.

## The discrepancy (pre-existing, surfaced by Gate 3 on PR #180)

The per-skill loop appends 17 distinct failure keys, while check_count is 16. Before claude-skills-184 removed the source check the same gap existed one higher: 18 keys against check_count 17. The cause is fm_schema - it is a real check that can fail and can land in the baseline, but it is not counted.

test/README.md heading tracks check_count rather than the table row count, so the README table has always listed one more row than its own heading claims (18 rows under a heading of 17 at main; 17 rows under 16 after PR #180). PR #180 preserved that convention deliberately rather than changing it mid-flip.

## Why it matters

check_count feeds the detail_count ratchet. A number that does not match the checks that can actually fire is a latent source of confusion for anyone reasoning about coverage, and the README inherits the error.

## Acceptance criteria

- Decide and record which number is canonical: either count fm_schema and make check_count 17, or state explicitly why fm_schema is excluded and rename the constant to say what it counts.
- test/README.md heading and table agree with each other and with whatever is decided.
- No change to baseline contents. mise test exit 0, waiver count unchanged.

## Load skills

/core:anti-fabrication, /core:nushell, /core:restraint, /claude-code:claude-skills
close_reason: PR #182 merged — check_count 16 -> 17. Measurement dissolved the bee's open question: the loop's 17 keys and the README's 17 table rows are the same set, so fm_schema was uncounted rather than deliberately excluded.

title: sources: extract pure functions from main so the enforcement checks are unit-testable
description:
## Objective

Extract the inline check logic in test/validate-sources.nu and test/validate-skills-quality.nu into pure functions so the behaviours flipped in claude-skills-184 can be unit-tested.

## Context

During PR #180 the test author found that none of the three changed behaviours was reachable from the existing case-table harnesses, because all three live inline inside def main rather than in callable functions:

- the missing sources.toml guard (validate-sources.nu main plugin loop) - never reaches check-sources, which receives an already-parsed toml
- the stale_pins computation for version_pin (validate-skills-quality.nu, per-skill loop)
- the source_ok block that was check 11 (same loop)

The author reported this instead of writing tests that appear to cover the change while exercising something else, and wrote two data assertions on real artifacts instead. Gate 3 confirmed the gap is real: a wrong implementation that kept the sources.md acceptance path in version_pin would pass every gate silently. That is inert today because no annotation remains, but it reopens the moment a future plugin adds one.

## Acceptance criteria

- The missing-file guard and the stale_pins computation are pure functions taking their inputs as arguments, callable from a self-test.
- Self-test cases cover: missing sources.toml reports a failure naming the plugin; a pin present only in sources.md prose FAILS; a pin present in sources.toml current_version PASSES; a skill with no pin PASSES.
- Tests written before the refactor per the repo adversarial-TDD split, since this is runtime behaviour.
- No behaviour change: corpus stays at 28 validated / 0 pending, waivers unchanged, mise test exit 0.

## Load skills

/core:anti-fabrication, /core:tdd, /core:nushell, /core:restraint
close_reason: PR #181 merged — missing-sources-findings and find-stale-version-pins extracted as pure functions with 10 red-first cases; behaviour proved unchanged by an old-vs-new differential over the real corpus.

title: skills-quality: benchmark docs still describe the retired substring source check
description:
## Objective

Update the two plugin-content locations that still document the source check retired in claude-skills-184 (PR #180).

## Locations (measured by the Gate 3 reviewer on PR #180)

- plugins/tools/claude-code/commands/benchmark-skills.md:45 - says the check verifies a skill is documented in sources.md
- plugins/tools/claude-code/skills/claude-skills-benchmark/SKILL.md:23 - same

## Context

check 11 (source) was a whole-file substring test asking whether a skill directory name appeared anywhere in the plugin sources.md. It could not distinguish real coverage from an incidental name match, and it was replaced by the exact set-difference coverage check in test/validate-sources.nu, which compares the union of every sources.toml entry skills array against the plugin declared skill set.

test/README.md was corrected inside PR #180 because it needs no version bump. These two files live inside the claude-code plugin, so fixing them requires a plugin + marketplace version bump, which is why they were split out rather than folded in.

## Acceptance criteria

- Neither file describes a source check that no longer exists. Where the concept is still worth mentioning, describe the actual replacement (sources.toml skills coverage, verified by set difference).
- claude-code plugin.json + marketplace.json entry bumped, mise update-all-skills run, mise test exit 0.

## Load skills

/core:anti-fabrication, /core:restraint, /claude-code:claude-skills
close_reason: PR #182 merged — benchmark docs describe the sources.toml coverage check; two github registration checklists corrected too (found by review, outside the bee's named scope).

title: sources: current_version has no format validation — any string passes
description:
## Objective

Add format validation for entry-level current_version in test/validate-sources.nu. Today it accepts any string.

## Context

Found while implementing claude-skills-187 (PR documenting the "unknown" convention), verified by two independent readings of the validator.

current_version appears in test/validate-sources.nu only three times: the allowed-keys list, ENTRY_NETWORK_KEYS (required when check_method != none), and NONE_FORBIDDEN. There is no regex and no format check anywhere. current_version = "banana" passes validation silently, as would a typo, a stray space, or an accidentally-pasted URL.

Contrast last_checked, which IS checked by rule b3_date (YYYY-MM-DD or the literal "unknown", anything else fails). The asymmetry is now documented in the skill-update field table, but documenting a gap is not closing it.

## Why this is not trivial

64 of 109 entries in the current corpus use current_version = "unknown" - a majority. Any validation must special-case that literal before checking the rest, or it breaks the whole corpus at once.

Upstream version strings are also genuinely heterogeneous and NOT all semver. Measured examples already in the corpus: mise uses CalVer (v2026.7.17), OTP uses its own scheme (OTP-29.0.4), molecule and ansible-lint use calendar versioning (v26.6.0), and some entries legitimately carry a bare major.minor. A strict semver regex would produce false failures on real data. The check probably has to be shape-based (no whitespace, no scheme-prefixed URL, reasonable length, not obviously prose) rather than semver-conformant - or keyed off version_constraint, since "rolling"/"stable" entries have different expectations than "semver"/"pre-1.0" ones.

## Acceptance criteria

- A new rule (or an extension of an existing one) rejects clearly-invalid current_version values while accepting "unknown" and every version string currently in the corpus.
- Self-test cases cover: "unknown" passes, a valid semver passes, a CalVer/OTP-style string passes, and at least two clearly-invalid values fail. Tests written before the implementation per the repo adversarial-TDD split, since this is runtime behaviour.
- Corpus stays clean: 20 validated / 8 pending, zero new findings, waivers not higher.
- Whatever shape is chosen is documented in the skill-update field table so the doc and the check agree.

## Load skills

/core:anti-fabrication, /core:tdd, /core:nushell, /core:restraint, /claude-code:claude-skills, /claude-code:skill-update
close_reason: PR #187 merged — b3_version_shape validates current_version (shape-based, not semver: accepts unknown, CalVer, bare majors, v-prefixes, pre-release/build suffixes; rejects whitespace, URLs, prose). 0 of 39 corpus values rejected. Doc and check now agree. PEP 440 separator-less edge recorded as claude-skills-196.

title: Pass-2 check findings are not wired into failing_counts, so their waivers absorb unlimited later findings
description: Findings from Pass-2 surface checks on agent and command files are not added to the failing_counts map; only the per-skill loop populates it. The consequence is a ratchet hole. validate-baseline-entries requires an integer detail_count for any waiver whose key ends in a detail-producing check name, so a hand-added waiver for an agent or command finding must carry a count, but the ratchet never compares that count because the current-run side is empty and the comparison short-circuits. One waiver therefore absorbs an unlimited number of later findings on that same file, which is precisely what the shrink-only ratchet exists to prevent. This is pre-existing rather than new: the links check added for claude-skills-164 already had it, and the code carries a NOTE saying so. The frontmatter schema check added in PR 168 is the second Pass-2 check to inherit it. Corpus impact today is zero because no agent or command waiver exists, so nothing is being absorbed right now; the hole is latent and opens the first time one is added. Two possible resolutions: populate failing_counts from the Pass-2 loops so the ratchet compares real numbers, or make validate-baseline-entries reject detail_count on Pass-2 keys so the requirement matches what is actually enforced. Prefer the first, since the second documents the gap rather than closing it. Found during the Gate 3 review of PR 168.
close_reason: Merged PR #199

title: Stale library and tool versions in the github and security skills
description: Two version references outside the action-pin scope of claude-skills-161 are stale, both found during the Gate 3 review of PR 165 and both in files that PR already touched. First, plugins/tools/github/skills/actions/SKILL.md around line 302 instructs authors to install the actions toolkit core package at version 1.10.0; the current major is 3.x. Second, plugins/core/skills/security/SKILL.md pins the gitleaks pre-commit hook at rev v8.18.0 while the gitleaks binary is at v8.30.1. Neither is a GitHub Action pin, which is why they were deliberately left out of PR 165 rather than folded in — that PR bumped only action pins plus the node runtime recommendations, which were in the same currency class and in already-touched files. Resolve by checking both against their upstream releases and bumping, reading release notes for breaking changes rather than bumping blind, exactly as PR 165 did. The toolkit one matters more: a skill teaching action authoring that names a two-major-old library version will produce code against an outdated API. Note also that version references like these are invisible to the version_pin check, which covers action pins only, so nothing catches them drifting.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #169 (070ced7). The bee named two items; a corpus sweep found ten. The headline item was a breaking-change migration, not a bump: every current toolkit major the actions skill teaches (core 3.x, github 9.x, exec 3.x, cache 6.x, artifact 6.x) is ESM-only, so the skill's seven require() blocks were converted to import and the artifact example rewritten for the v2+ DefaultArtifactClient API. Verified empirically on node v24.18.0 rather than from docs, because the toolkit README still shows require() and contradicts its own release notes. Also bumped: gitleaks pre-commit rev v8.18.0 to v8.30.1, alpine 3.18 to 3.24, node:18 and node-version 20 defaults to 24 in three files, debian:12-slim to 13 (debian 12 went EOL 2026-07-11), and the ansible molecule matrix off ubuntu 20.04 and debian 12. Kept in-support pins (postgres 15, redis 7, ubuntu 22.04, rockylinux9, MISE_VERSION) under a stated rule: fix what is EOL or where following the doc produces code that cannot run. Six plugin versions bumped. The enforcement gap the bee notes is filed separately.

title: Manifest agreement check has a deletion escape hatch and is keyword-order sensitive
description: Two gaps in the description/keywords agreement check added in PR 161, both found by adversarial testing and both accepted at the time rather than fixed. First, drift by deletion is invisible: removing description or keywords entirely from a marketplace entry makes the check pass silently, because an omission on either side is deliberately not treated as a mismatch. A plugin.json-side omission still draws a Missing recommended field warning, but nothing requires the marketplace entry to carry either field, so an entry can lose its Level 1 discovery text without any check objecting. Decide whether marketplace entries should be required to carry both fields when the plugin.json defines them. Second, the comparison is order sensitive: two keyword lists with identical members in a different order fail with a message that says mismatch even though the sets are equal. Harmless today since all 30 pairs match in order, and defensible on the grounds that the entry is meant to be an exact copy, but the failure message would be confusing when it fires. Either compare as sets or say order matters in the message. Verified by constructing each case against the real validator and observing the exit code.
close_reason: Merged PR #200

title: core plugin description names 4 of its 13 skills
description: The core plugin description reads Essential development skills: Git, documentation, code review, security. It omits tdd, agent-loop, restraint, bees, mise, nushell, container, twelve-factor, and anti-fabrication. Both plugin.json and the marketplace entry carry the same text, so it was outside the mismatch scope of PR 161 and the new agreement check passes on it. This is the synced-but-wrong class the agreement check cannot catch by design: it enforces that the two copies match, not that either is accurate. Level 1 discovery text is the only thing a user sees when browsing the marketplace, and core is the most-loaded plugin in this repo, so underselling it by nine skills has real cost. A sweep of all 30 plugins during the PR 161 review found core to be the only gross underseller, so this is a single targeted fix rather than a program. Rewrite the description to cover what the plugin actually ships, update both files together, and bump the version.
close_reason: PR #167: description now names all 13 skills; two labels sharpened on review (gitleaks secret scanning, twelve-factor apps)

title: beads install commands name an anthropic package identity; upstream is steveyegge
description: plugins/tools/beads/skills/beads/references/installation.md gives 'npm install -g @anthropic/beads' and 'brew install anthropic/tap/beads', while the Go install line in the same file points at github.com/steveyegge/beads/cmd/bd@latest. The npm scope and Homebrew tap both claim an anthropic package identity for a project whose own source URL is steveyegge. At least one of these is wrong. UNVERIFIED and deliberately so: this workspace uses bees, not bd, so nothing here dogfoods the beads toolchain and no bd or npm or brew command was run to check. The content moved verbatim and unfixed in PR 159 under that PR's move-only rule, because silently correcting an untested claim would fabricate. To resolve: check the upstream repo's README and the actual npm and Homebrew registries for the real package identities, then correct all sites. Note the same claims may also appear in the git history of the pre-relocation path under plugins/core/skills/beads/. Discovered while planning the claude-skills-143 final batch and confirmed during the Gate 3 review of PR 159.

title: elixir plugin description drifts between plugin.json and marketplace.json, and no check compares them
description: plugins/languages/elixir/.claude-plugin/plugin.json describes the plugin as 'Elixir development skills: Phoenix, OTP, Ports, Ecto, Tidewave MCP, testing, configuration, style, and anti-patterns' while the elixir entry in .claude-plugin/marketplace.json ends '...configuration, style' — omitting anti-patterns. Verified pre-existing and untouched by PR 158 (git diff of the description lines against origin/main is empty). The interesting part is not the one-word drift but that nothing catches it: test/validate-plugin.nu and the marketplace validator check schema and path validity, and test:version-bumps compares the version fields between the two files, but no check compares descriptions. Marketplace descriptions are Level 1 discovery text, so drift there changes what a user sees when browsing versus what the installed plugin claims. Two parts to resolve: fix the elixir entry, and decide whether a plugin.json-vs-marketplace.json description equality check belongs in the validator, sweeping all 30 plugins for existing drift first. Found during Gate 3 review of PR 158.
close_reason: PR #161: 18 mismatches synced across 11 plugins, agreement check added to test:plugins, keyword union preserves all discovery terms

title: bees accepts invalid enum values silently across several commands
description:
Found during the claude-skills-157/158 audit and independently reproduced. bees 0.4.0 performs no enum validation on several documented value sets, so a typo is stored verbatim and fails silently later rather than at the point of error.

Measured in a throwaway repo:
- 'bees update <id> --status bogus' -> 'Updated <id>', exit 0; 'list --json' then shows status 'bogus'. The issue is silently excluded from 'bees ready' from that point on, with no indication why.
- 'bees dep add <id> <blocker> -t nonsense' -> exit 0, type stored verbatim.
- 'bees create x -t garbage' -> accepted and stored.

Also a naming inconsistency worth resolving while here: 'dep --help' spells the third dependency type 'parent-child' while our docs say 'parent' — BOTH are accepted, because nothing validates. And 'create --help' lists type 'story' while the 'bees prime' cheatsheet says 'chore'; both accepted.

This is upstream behaviour, not a docs defect, so it is deliberately NOT part of the #157/#158 truth-up. Two possible dispositions: (a) document the trap in the bees skill — a typo'd status silently removes an issue from the ready queue, which is exactly the 'not discoverable from --help' content the skill body is for; or (b) raise it upstream against bees. (a) is cheap and within our control; (b) is the real fix. They are not exclusive.

Valid values observed from --help: status open, in_progress, closed, deferred; dep types blocks, related, parent/parent-child; issue types task, bug, feature, epic, story.
close_reason: Merged PR #193

title: sources.md Version lines are stale repo-wide against plugin.json
description:
Found by Gate 3 on PR #149. Each plugin's skills/sources.md carries a 'Version: X' line that is not maintained when the plugin version bumps, so they drift silently. Measured at PR #149's head: slidev sources.md says 0.2.0 while plugin.json says 0.2.1; zig says 0.1.0 vs 0.1.4; core says 0.1.19 vs 0.2.32. Not created by #149 — the repo has never maintained them per bump, and #149 only made one of them one patch staler.

Decide one of three, then it is mechanical: (a) drop the Version line from sources.md entirely, since plugin.json is the source of truth and a second copy is exactly the duplication this repo keeps removing; (b) keep it and add a check that it matches plugin.json, which turns silent drift into a CI failure; (c) keep it and document that it means something else (e.g. the upstream tool version being tracked, not the plugin version) — check what it was originally for before assuming it mirrors plugin.json.

Note there is already a version_pin check that validates 'Current stable: X' claims against sources.md entries, so (b) would extend an existing mechanism rather than add a new one. Prefer (a) if the line has no consumer — restraint says delete the second copy rather than build a check to keep two copies equal.
close_reason: Superseded entirely by claude-skills-180. This bee asked to correct sources.md Version lines that were stale against plugin.json. Measurement on 2026-07-30 showed the premise was wrong: the field is not drifting, it was never maintained. 16 of 28 files carry it, 13 disagree, and seven still read 0.1.0 - the value from the day the file was created. claude-code reads 0.1.8 against plugin.json 0.2.34; core reads 0.1.19 against 0.2.41. Mechanically correcting those 13 values would have written 13 fresh falsehoods: it asserts sources were reviewed at 0.2.34 when the last review was 0.1.8. Two agents independently recommended deleting the field, having grepped only for machine readers; the operator overruled that, since sources.md is load-bearing for the skill-update process and undocumented claims violate anti-fabrication. Both this bee's option (a) delete-the-line and option (c) give-the-semantic-a-structured-home are answered by 180's schema: the plugin-version mirror goes away, and the surviving meaning becomes meta.reviewed_at_plugin_version in sources.toml, where a mismatch against plugin.json is reported as information (N bumps since the last sources review) rather than treated as a defect. Invariant C3 in the design prevents the prose field regrowing. Do not reopen to fix version numbers.

title: validate-skills-quality crashes when a git-tracked file is deleted from the working tree
description:
Found while running the historical replay for claude-skills-141. The duplicate_block corpus scan (validate-skills-quality.nu ~line 1731) builds its file list from 'git ls-files' and then does 'open --raw' on each path. If a tracked file has been deleted from the working tree but the deletion is not yet committed, the validator dies with a raw nushell 'File not found' stack trace pointing at the open call, exit 1.

Reproduced on MAIN, so it predates 141 and came in with the duplicate_block check in PR #144: clone the repo, 'rm plugins/tools/claude-code/skills/claude-commands/references/examples.md', run 'nu test/validate-skills-quality.nu' -> 2 'File not found' lines, exit 1.

Why it matters: deleting a file and running CI before committing the deletion is an ordinary mid-refactor state, and any removal PR hits it — claude-skills-136 deleted tracked files and would have hit this had the removals not been staged first. The failure is also misleading: it looks like validator corruption rather than 'you have an uncommitted deletion'.

Fix: filter the corpus to paths that exist on disk, or use 'git ls-files' intersected with a filesystem check, and report skipped-because-deleted paths explicitly rather than crashing. Do not silently ignore missing files without saying so — a silent skip in a corpus scan is how a check goes quiet.

Same class as the other duplicate_block hardening in claude-skills-151; could be fixed together.
close_reason:
Shipped as PR #148. The duplicate-block corpus scan built its list from 'git ls-files' then opened every path, so a tracked-but-deleted file — an uncommitted deletion, the ordinary mid-refactor state — aborted the validator with a raw nushell trace. Reproduced on main first; came in with #144 (git log -S on the corpus line -> commit 2739702).

Fixed in BOTH scripts. Gate 3 found the sibling I had missed: sweep-unregistered in validate-core-list.nu had the identical git-ls-files-then-open shape, so a removal PR's local CI still died one script later in the same mise test run. Closing only the reported instance while its sibling survived is the exact 'fixed one instance of a class' pattern this repo keeps hitting. Both now partition missing paths out and ANNOUNCE the skip with each path — a corpus that shrinks silently would be worse than one that crashes.

After the fix the original repro exits 1 for the right reason: the links check reports that the skill references a file no longer on disk.

Residual recorded, not hidden: deleting main's one-line print caller still passes every self-test. The warning CONTENT is now pinned in split-corpus-paths (the 'helper returns no warnings' mutation fails), but main's wiring is not unit-testable. That is the third instance of one root cause — see claude-skills-151, which now carries all three and the integration-harness fix shape that would close them together.

title: /core:setup bootstraps new projects with beads while our own convention is bees
description: Noticed during claude-skills-136's documentation sweep. plugins/core/agents/setup.md defaults a NEW project to beads (bd init, with --stealth -> bd init --local and --contributor -> bd init --pull), and the /core:setup skill description says 'Bootstrap a new project with beads task tracking'. Meanwhile this workspace's CLAUDE.md says 'bees for issue tracking (not beads - beads is removed from all repos)' and claude-skills itself just removed its beads installation in #146. Not a false claim about this repo, so it was correctly left alone by that PR - setup.md is about the project being created, not this one. But we now recommend to new users a tracker we removed from our own repos. Decide: make bees the /core:setup default with beads behind a flag, offer both explicitly, or leave as-is and document why. Both skills stay in the marketplace either way.
close_reason: Merged PR #193

comments.text: OPERATOR DECISION (2026-07-27): help users bootstrap BEES. Scope for whoever takes this: /core:setup and plugins/core/agents/setup.md should bootstrap bees as the default tracker for a new project. Do NOT rip out beads support — /core:beads remains a legitimate marketplace skill for users whose repos use beads (claude-skills-136 was explicit about this), so beads stays available, e.g. behind a flag, with bees as the default path. Today setup.md defaults to 'bd init' with --stealth -> 'bd init --local' and --contributor -> 'bd init --pull'; the bees equivalents need to be the primary flow and the skill description updated to match. Check whether this repo's own 17 bees:* mise tasks are the right template for what a new project gets.

title: Subset-aware SATELLITES shape: check what a subsetting tier omits, not just what it names
description: Gate 3 on PR #145 confirmed the subsetting exemption's floor has no teeth. In a scratchpad clone, deleting /core:anti-fabrication from references/validator.md — the one skill that PR's own text calls never-omissible — left both 'nu test/validate-core-list.nu' and 'nu test/validate-skills-quality.nu' at exit 0. The invocations check catches a name that does not RESOLVE (verified: bogus name fails; and simulating removal of ./skills/tdd from plugins/core/.claude-plugin/plugin.json makes every /core:tdd mention fail), so stale and misspelled names cannot survive a core-list change. What is unchecked is MEMBERSHIP: a tier silently dropping a skill it should carry passes CI. That is the exact class that produced claude-skills-125, which was invisible to CI for as long as it existed. Proposed shape: a subset-aware SATELLITES entry {path, expected: [names...]} so validate-core-list.nu asserts a declared subset exactly, rather than requiring the full canonical list or skipping the file. Two files would use it today: references/validator.md (2 names) and references/fix-agent.md (5 names). Deliberately not blocking #145 — the adjacent prose says anti-fabrication is never omissible, so a silent drop requires editing past an explicit warning, and the accidental case is now a documented decision instead.
close_reason: Merged PR #198

title: Self-test the duplicate-block count accumulation directly
description: Gate 3 on PR #144 found one mutation the 14 new self-tests do not catch: removing the failing_counts append in Pass 3 leaves both 'nu test/validate-skills-quality.nu --self-test' (14/14) and the full run green. Nothing pins that main actually feeds window counts into the ratchet, which is the absorption trap the validator warns about at its own line ~1010. Behaviour is correct today — verified live in a scratchpad clone: growing the waived beads/bees group 7->8 windows exits 1 with 'current 8 > baselined 7', and shrinking it to 3 exits 1 on stale count, with --update-baseline correctly ratcheting the entry down. The gap is architectural and shared with every pre-existing detail check, since counts are accumulated inline in main rather than in a testable function; it is NOT a regression introduced by #144. Fix: extract the {key, count} accumulation into a function and self-test it directly, which would cover the existing detail checks at the same time. Second, smaller item from the same review: exemption 3 parses validate-core-list.nu with a regex matching 'path: "' anywhere in the file, and self-test case 14 asserts only a lower bound (>=5 satellites). A future 'path: "' string in that script — a test fixture, say — would silently broaden the exemption. Bound the parse to the SATELLITES block and add an upper-bound assertion.
close_reason: Merged PR #199

comments.text:
Third instance of the same root cause, from Gate 3 on PR #148 — main's wiring is not unit-testable, so any single-line caller in main can be deleted with every self-test green.

Instances so far: (1) removing the failing_counts append in Pass 3 leaves 15 cases green (the original report); (2) unwiring the floor check from main leaves all vocab cases green (Gate 3 on #147, judged inherent); (3) deleting the skip-warning print line in the corpus scan produces zero skip lines and nothing fails (Gate 3 on #148). In #148 the warning CONTENT was moved into split-corpus-paths so a self-test pins it — the mutation 'helper returns no warnings' is now caught — but the one-line 'for w in ... print' caller in main remains unprotected.

The pattern: extracting the VALUE into a pure helper makes the value testable; it does not make the WIRING testable. Every pass has this shape.

Fix shape, unchanged: an integration harness that runs main against a small fixture repo and asserts on its output, rather than more per-value extraction. That would cover all three instances at once. Judged disproportionate at each individual finding; recording the third instance because the count is the argument — if a fourth shows up, the harness is cheaper than continuing to argue it down case by case.

title: dedupe cross-skill duplicate blocks flagged by duplicate_block check
description: Burn-down for five cross-file duplicate groups baselined when the duplicate-block check landed (claude-skills-124). Groups (key — shared 8-line windows — members): dupe/1182fd06 — 5 — elixir phoenix/references/tidewave.md vs tidewave/SKILL.md; dupe/abe3453c — 2 — claude-code claude-plugins/SKILL.md vs plugin-marketplace/SKILL.md; dupe/da5499df — 2 — claude-plugins/SKILL.md vs plugin-marketplace/references/schema-specification.md; dupe/ccc3a496 — 7 — root CLAUDE.md vs claude-code claude-skills/SKILL.md; dupe/639413bb — 1 — github dependabot-consolidator/references/registration.md vs pr-review/references/registration.md. For each: keep one canonical copy and point the other at it (or extract to a shared reference), then remove the baseline entry so the ratchet locks the fix in. Run nu test/validate-skills-quality.nu to see current members/counts.
close_reason: Merged PR #202 — dupe/1182fd06 (elixir phoenix/tidewave) and dupe/639413bb (github registration) both retired; baseline 4 groups -> 2, verified gone from the detected set rather than under-threshold

comments.text: Three of the five groups are retired; two remain. Retired: dupe/ccc3a496 (root CLAUDE.md vs claude-code claude-skills/SKILL.md, was 7 shared windows) by PR #170, because the duplicated best-practices prose WAS the shared text and the router trim deleted it. dupe/abe3453c (claude-plugins/SKILL.md vs plugin-marketplace/SKILL.md, was 2) and dupe/da5499df (claude-plugins/SKILL.md vs plugin-marketplace/references/schema-specification.md, was 2) by PR #171. All three are gone from the detected set, not merely under the 8-line window threshold, and the baseline shrank 68 to 65 accordingly. Still open: dupe/1182fd06 (elixir phoenix/references/tidewave.md vs tidewave/SKILL.md, 5 windows) and dupe/639413bb (github dependabot-consolidator/references/registration.md vs pr-review/references/registration.md, 1 window). Neither is in the claude-code plugin, so neither was reachable from the claude-skills-128 shape work. One transferable lesson for whoever finishes this: while moving the two validation-error catalogs into new per-skill reference files, the byte-identical kebab-case block would have minted a NEW cross-skill duplicate group, and because the baseline is shrink-only it cannot accept a new key at all - it would have been an unwaivable CI failure rather than something --update-baseline absorbs. The fix was to keep that example in one reference and have the other state the rule and quote the validator message instead. Measure the longest shared normalised run between candidate files before committing a dedupe that splits content into new files.

title: dedupe beads-worker/bees-worker shared git/PR block via skills: preloading assessment
description: Duplicate-block check group dupe/6365464e (7 shared windows) spans plugins/core/skills/beads/agents/beads-worker.md and plugins/core/skills/bees/agents/bees-worker.md. Corrected constraint from the claude-skills-124 plan (revision 2), quoted verbatim — do not act on the earlier false categorical version ('pointers do not work; both agents must carry the full workflow'): 'a markdown citation is not followed at spawn time, so the pointer shape used for references does not transfer; `skills:` preloading is the candidate mechanism. Two open questions for whoever takes it — whether preloading `/core:git` (220 lines) to remove ~21 duplicated lines is a favourable trade for an agent whose value is a tight prompt, and how to parameterise the `bd` vs `bees` commands that interleave with the shared block.' Also from the plan: the identical run begins at `git add <files>`, after the tracker-specific lines diverge, so what is shared is generic git/PR mechanics rather than policy — lower drift risk than the raw line count suggests. claude-skills-136 does not moot this: it explicitly preserves /core:beads as a marketplace skill.
close_reason: Assessed no-dedupe; verdict recorded on PR #202 and in the bee. Measured with the validator's own normalise-dupe-lines: 21 normalised shared lines vs /core:git's 222, and skills: preloading is eager — so deduping would add 222 lines of new cost per spawn to remove 21, roughly 20:1 against. Cross-plugin self-containment also rules out a pointer: bees-worker ships in core, beads-worker in beads, so a preload or citation dangles when only one plugin is installed, and this span is main-path rather than conditional. dupe/28ccd32d stays in the baseline at 7 windows by design

comments.text:
Assessed, no dedupe — recorded on PR #202 rather than acted on. Measured with the validator's own normalise-dupe-lines: the 7 windows collapse into an 11-line PR-mechanics span plus a 10-line Pattern/Action dispatch table = 21 normalised lines. /core:git is 222 lines.

Three reasons not to dedupe:
1. skills: preloading is EAGER (preloads full skill content at subagent startup), and neither bees-worker.md nor beads-worker.md declares skills: today — so 222 lines is entirely new cost, not redirected existing cost. ~20:1 against.
2. Cross-plugin self-containment: bees-worker ships in core, beads-worker in beads. Install only one plugin and a skills: [core:git] preload dangles — as does a prose pointer. For an agent's MAIN-PATH operating instructions that is unacceptable, which also rules out hoisting the span into one file and pointing the other at it.
3. Span 2 is not git content at all, so /core:git would not cover it, and inventing a skill for 10 lines fails the first restraint rung.

Note the distinction that makes this different from an ordinary pointer: bees-worker.md already cites /core:agent-loop successfully at lines 69/106/110, because those citations are CONDITIONAL — only the pipeline branch needs them. The PR-mechanics span is main-path, needed every run.

dupe/28ccd32d stays in the baseline at 7 windows. Leaving this open as DEBT with the verdict recorded; close as won't-fix if preferred.

title: rust-implementer's Gate 1/Gate 2 collide with the merge-policy gate numbers
description:
plugins/languages/rust/agents/rust-implementer.md:37-38 uses 'Gate 1 — frozen tests untouched' and 'Gate 2 — full CI green' as its own step names. Since PR #143 those numbers collide with /core:git's Three-Gate Merge Policy, where Gate 1 is local CI and Gate 2 is remote CI — so rust's 'Gate 2' is the policy's Gate 1.

Behaviour is unambiguous today: each rust step names its criterion inline and never cites /core:git's numbering, and Gate 3 review judged the non-change defensible. But two schemes sharing the word 'Gate' with different numbers is the kind of thing that reads fine to the author and confuses everyone else.

Cheap fix: rename rust's to 'Check 1 — frozen tests untouched' and 'Check 2 — full CI green', or fold them into the numbered list without gate language. Verify no other agent or skill cites rust's numbering before renaming.

Raised by the Gate 3 review of PR #143 as a non-blocking follow-up.
close_reason: Merged PR #191

title: Judgment-over-rules pass on the densest prescriptive skills
description:
Deferred from claude-skills-123, which reconciled the cap literals and applied rule 4 to the authoring skills. This is the other half: apply the judgment-over-rules practice to the skills carrying the most prohibition-shaped prose.

Bounded by a measured selection rule rather than 'the densest ones'. Prohibition-keyword density (grep -cEi 'never|do not|don.t|must not|no exceptions') ranks:
  agent-loop 19, twelve-factor 13, claude-agents 9, restraint 9, git 9

Apply the boundary test from plugins/tools/claude-code/skills/claude-skills/references/context-engineering-claude-5.md to EACH rule individually, not to the file: if removing the prescription would break a check, permit a fabrication, or rely on an agent recognising a need it does not yet have, it stays prescriptive.

Expect this to be small. The top two are exactly the skills that reference's boundary section protects as push-not-pull standing disciplines — agent-loop carries the mandatory-load doctrine and twelve-factor is mandatory precisely because its Use when trigger under-fires. Most of their prohibitions are likely facts. That is a finding to record, not a reason to skip the pass.

Do NOT soften anything backed by a validator check, mise test:disclosure, or the CI gates. Re-measure the density ranking before starting; it will have shifted.
close_reason:
Measured and closed as no-edit-warranted, per the boundary test applied rule-by-rule (not file-by-file) to the four densest skills. Re-measured on main: agent-loop 20 (was 19), twelve-factor 13 (unchanged), git 12 (was 9), restraint 9 (unchanged), claude-agents 4 (was 9) — claude-agents dropped out of the top 5 entirely because PR #195's SKILL.md/references split (441->156 lines) moved bulk content out of the scanned file. That is evidence the density metric partly measures body size rather than actual prescriptiveness, not evidence the methodology was wrong.

Of ~50 individual prohibitions across the four files, essentially all classify as stays-prescriptive:
- agent-loop: confirmed by reading test/validate-core-list.nu directly (not inferred) that line 19's anchor and its mandatory-load list are SATELLITES[0], drift-checked against 10 other sites — the concrete would-break-a-check case the boundary test exists for. Every other genuine rule (never-omissible anti-fabrication, agents-never-merge, never-hardcode-a-model-literal, validator-never-fixes, never-print-secrets) passes the same test. One genuinely debatable case, kept: the question-batching nudge at line 66 — procedural, with no self-correcting signal if violated.
- twelve-factor: 8 of 13 are the methodology's own core prescriptions (softening would misrepresent the cited source); one (0.0.0.0 bind) is corroborated by the operator's own production conventions with a cited incident; 4 are DON'T-labels inside paired code examples; 1 (line 252) is a verbatim blockquote from 12factor.net and is not eligible for rewording at all, since altering a direct quotation is a fabrication risk in the opposite direction. That category is missing from the boundary test — filed as claude-skills-213.
- restraint: every hit is the skill's own definitional boundary or the never-lazy-about carve-out. Softening any would be self-defeating by the skill's own logic; it is the standard this exercise appeals to.
- git: 11 of 12 stay, several corroborated by real incidents; 1 excluded as out of scope (the SSH-vs-OAuth-scope citation, handled in PR #201 as a citation-accuracy fix). #201 added 2 more prohibition-shaped lines after the count was taken, both self-evidently in the permits-a-fabrication category, not re-litigated.

5th-place tie noted but not pursued: anti-fabrication and dependabot-consolidator both at 8 after the shift. Left out per the bee's own bounded-selection-rule framing — taking newly-opened ranking slots is the scope creep that rule exists to prevent.

title: Six skills have sibling reference-to-reference links
description:
The ref_depth waivers that are genuine DEBT rather than check defects. Each is a reference file linking to a sibling reference in the same skill, which breaks the one-level-deep rule (SKILL.md to reference, never reference to reference) — an agent following the chain pays for two loads when the body should have pointed at both.

Six entries carrying nine findings:
- awman/awman (2): workflows.md, command-reference.md, api.md cross-link each other
- core/git (2): two sibling cross-links
- qa/qa (2): stack-detection.md and gherkin-format.md link each other
- claude-code/claude-teams (1): references/subagents.md:144 links sibling agent-sdk.md
- elixir/testing (1): tdd-discipline.md links os-subprocess-adapter.md
- slidev/styles (1): discovery-pipeline.md links theme-generation.md

Fix per link: either promote the pointer into the SKILL.md body so both references are reachable at one level, or merge the two references if the split was arbitrary. Reword rather than delete — the cross-reference exists because a reader needs both.

Filed by claude-skills-130's review: these waivers pointed at claude-skills-134 (Harden core-list check), which mentions ref_depth zero times. Second instance of pointer rot found since the class/issue requirement landed in PR #137 — that requirement catches a MISSING pointer, not a wrong one.
close_reason: PR #184 merged — nine ref_depth findings across six skills flattened to one-level disclosure; waivers 55 -> 49.

title: 14 non-always-loaded skills exceed the 500-line cap
description:
The lines waivers remaining after claude-skills-121 split the always-loaded ones (mise, nushell, twelve-factor). These 14 are over the cap but are NOT in the mandatory core set, so their bodies load only on activation and the cost is bounded:

core/beads 735, core/bees 581, core/code-review 611, core/container 793, core/documentation 676, dagu/workflows 833, elixir/anti-patterns 589, elixir/config 616, elixir/otp 719, elixir/phoenix 599, elixir/style 514, elixir/testing 853, github/act 653, github/workflows 887.

Line counts as of 2026-07-26; re-measure before acting. Same treatment as claude-skills-121: move detail into references/ (one level deep, every file linked from SKILL.md), keep the decision-shaped content and gotchas in the body, then let the ratchet's stale-count rule force each waiver's detail_count down or its removal.

Note core/bees at 581 is the closest to the cap and is a tracker skill agents load constantly — likely the highest value of the group despite not being mandatory.

Split out of claude-skills-121 (closed) so these waivers point at live work, per the class/issue requirement from claude-skills-132.
close_reason: All 14 skills under the 500-line cap across four batches; PRs 152, 156, 157, 158, 159. Zero :lines keys remain in the baseline; waivers 95 to 68. Final sweep: no SKILL.md exceeds 500 lines repo-wide.

comments.text:
PREMISE CORRECTION, found by plan review before any edit. This issue's description says the 14 'are NOT in the mandatory core set, so their bodies load only on activation and the cost is bounded.' That is FALSE for core/bees: /core:bees is item 10 of the canonical mandatory block in agent-loop/SKILL.md, so it loads on EVERY agent at EVERY tier — the same cost profile as the mise/nushell/twelve-factor cohort that claude-skills-121 split. Its 581 lines are paid on every spawn.

The other 13 genuinely are activation-only; the error is bees-specific. Consequence: bees deserves the LEAST conservative trim of the group, not the most, and any batch decision that leans on 'bounded cost' must exclude it.

Also recorded for the batch that follows — plan review measured which mechanics do NOT generalise from the bees slice:
- 7 of the 13 have no usable references/ dir (core/documentation, elixir/anti-patterns, elixir/config, elixir/otp, elixir/style, github/act, github/workflows; dagu/workflows' dir is empty). They need directory + orphan-link plumbing that bees did not.
- github/workflows (887, 387 over), elixir/testing (853), dagu/workflows (833) will need multiple reference files and likely body condensation closer to #121's more aggressive treatment. The bees slice's 'move, not trim, account for every line' constraint is BEES-SPECIFIC and should not be inherited as part of the rule.
- elixir/style (514, 14 over) is the opposite edge: apply the principle, and resist moving more than the lookup content just to reach a rounder number.

Coordination risk: core/bees:anti_fab is waived under claude-skills-144. If 144 edits bees SKILL.md, these line counts drift — re-measure bees at execution time.

FIRST SLICE SHIPPED — PR #150. core/bees 581 -> 356 lines, waivers 82 -> 81. Thirteen skills remain.

THE RULE, validated by contact and safe to inherit: the body answers 'should I, and what will bite me'; references answer 'how exactly'. A section stays if it is a decision, a gotcha, or the happy path; it moves if a reader would look it up rather than read it through. Gate 3 read the 356-line result cold and found nothing missing that you would need before opening a reference, and nothing left in the body that is pure lookup.

SIX MECHANICS NOTES FOR THE BATCH, five sound and one rewritten:
1. Classify SUBSECTIONS, not H2s. This slice moved three subsections out of parents that stayed — that is what let gotchas remain while lookup left.
2. 'Happy path' means the PROCEDURAL happy path. A workflow an agent adapts in-conversation stays; a script artifact you open to copy moves.
3. Keep each moved section's heading as a pointer anchor. MANDATORY where external citations exist — pm and qa sources.md cite bees/SKILL.md, and the anchors keep those resolving. Grep for citations before removing a heading.
4. Deliberate body/reference duplication is sometimes right (the dep-order gotcha lives in both). Cap it at single lines — never blocks, or the duplicate_block check fires.
5. REWRITTEN, and this is the highest-value lesson: byte-faithful moving plus a correction manufactures same-file contradictions. WHEN YOU CORRECT A CLAIM, GREP THE BODY AND EVERY REFERENCE FOR RESTATEMENTS BEFORE COMMITTING. This slice proved it twice — the corrected create examples left a flags list six lines below still documenting the removed flags, and a grep afterwards found the same broken flag in teams-integration.md, a file the PR never touched.
6. A 2-line install stub plus a template pointer is enough to actually install. Fine as the batch default.

DO NOT INHERIT: the 'account for every line' constraint was bees-specific. github/workflows is 387 over and needs real condensation; accounting for every line would block it.

UNEXPECTED FINDING WORTH EXPECTING AGAIN: this trim turned into a correctness fix. The bees Commands Reference documented four things the binary does not do (update --labels, create -l, create -p as parent, comma-separated labels) and the body claimed cycle detection that does not exist — bees 0.4.0 accepts a 2-cycle at exit 0 and both issues then vanish from bees ready. Budget for the possibility that moving content surfaces wrong content, and decide in advance whether to fix in-slice or file. Filed here: claude-skills-157 (audit the rest of commands.md against the binary) and claude-skills-158 (the mise.toml template forwards the broken flags).

REMAINING 13, re-measure before starting: github/workflows 887, elixir/testing 853, dagu/workflows 833, core/container 793, core/beads 735, elixir/otp 719, core/documentation 676, github/act 653, elixir/config 616, core/code-review 611, elixir/phoenix 599, elixir/anti-patterns 589, elixir/style 514. Seven have no usable references/ dir.

BATCH 2 of 4 SHIPPED — PR #152, github plugin. workflows 887 -> 210, act 653 -> 454. Waivers 81 -> 79. Eleven skills remain.

THE RULE HELD AT THE HARDEST CASE. workflows was the largest gap in the program (387 over) and the bees plan review predicted it would need body condensation beyond the move-only approach. It did not: 631 of its 887 lines were contiguous GitHub Actions YAML syntax reference, which is look-it-up content by definition, so a straight move handled it. Gate 3 read the resulting 210-line body cold as an author and found nothing missing before opening a reference. A 76% cut was a trim, not an evisceration, because the thing being cut was uniformly one kind of content.

FOUR MECHANICS FOR BATCHES 3 AND 4, all Gate-3 assessed as sound:
1. Name a destination file for EVERY moved item in the plan. Revision 2 left two moved patterns without a target and the implementer had to choose.
2. Budget ~4 lines per moved H2 for pointer anchors before promising a body size. 13 anchors cost ~50 lines here and put the result 10 over target.
3. Scan same-file windows BY HAND after a wholesale move. The duplicate_block check windows are CROSS-FILE only, so two overlapping sections landing in one reference file are invisible to CI. One instance was caught and fixed by hand this batch.
4. Body/reference near-duplication is fine where the two versions genuinely carry different things (a worked example including an invocation the raw payload lacks). Not a violation of the single-line duplication cap.

THIRD SLICE, THIRD TIME A TRIM SURFACED FALSE CONTENT — treat this as expected, not surprising. act documented three things that do not work, all verified against act 0.2.89: 'act --shell bash' (no such flag, zero occurrences in --help), 'if: github.event_name != \\'act\\'' (act passes the real event name; there is no act event, so the guard never fires and the local-only step never runs — found in THREE places, not the two the plan named), and '--container-daemon-socket -' described as host networking (it is the Docker socket URI; --network already defaults to host). Budget for this in batches 3 and 4.

ONE SCOPE DECISION WORTH INHERITING: every GitHub Action pin in the workflows skill is 2-4 majors stale (checkout v4 vs v7.0.1). NOT fixed here, deliberately — pins appear in both moving and kept sections, so a partial bump manufactures the body/reference contradiction that bit #150. Bump all or none; this bumped none, leaving the skill uniformly stale, which is self-consistent and wrong in one way rather than two. Filed as claude-skills-161 covering the skill, its new references, and our own validate.yml.

REMAINING 11, re-measure before starting: elixir/testing 853, dagu/workflows 833, core/container 793, core/beads 735, elixir/otp 719, core/documentation 676, elixir/config 616, core/code-review 611, elixir/phoenix 599, elixir/anti-patterns 589, elixir/style 514. Suggested next batch: core (4 skills), then elixir (6), then dagu (1).

title: 44 skills lack an anti-fabrication reference; 8 lack a sources.md entry
description:
The anti_fab and source waivers remaining after claude-skills-131 fixed the claude-code plugin's cases. Both checks are presence-only.

anti_fab (44 entries): the check greps for a core:anti-fabrication reference or the word 'fabricat'. Fix is a short pointer per skill — see plugins/languages/rust/skills/async for the shape. IMPORTANT: this check cannot detect actual fabrication, only its absence as a topic. A passing anti_fab check says nothing about whether a skill's content is sound — claude-skills-126 (a skill documenting a syntax that does not exist) sat behind one of these waivers. Detection of fabricated content is claude-skills-141.

source (8 entries): the plugin's skills/sources.md exists but has no section for that skill. Add one following the existing URL / Purpose / Date Accessed / Key Points / Used In convention.

Both are mechanical burn-down. Split out of claude-skills-131 (closed) so these waivers point at live work, per the class/issue requirement from claude-skills-132.
close_reason: Split per assessment + Gate 3 review (PR #201): the 4 genuinely house-convention core skills (git, documentation, code-review, twelve-factor) got real per-skill anti-fabrication pointers, each naming its actual claim area or stating honestly it has none. git turned out to be the one skill in the set making concrete checkable external claims (GitHub API behavior) and was treated accordingly. Gate 3 replaced git's paragraph with a bare '## Anti-fabrication' header and nothing else: still 17/17 — a 44-file pointer sweep would have produced 44 green checks and zero examined claims. The remaining 40 are NOT closed as a sweep; see claude-skills-202, 203, 204.

comments.text: Remeasured 2026-07-29. The sources.md half of this issue is DONE and should not be re-attempted: all 28 plugins now have skills/sources.md. Verified two independent ways rather than by the loop that produced the first count - 28 plugin.json files against 28 sources.md files, then a comm -23 set difference on the sorted directory lists, which came back empty. The anti-fabrication half has drifted the wrong way, from 44 to 45 skills with no mention of anti-fabrication in their SKILL.md, presumably because skills were added since this was filed. Retitle or split accordingly: what remains is one measurable task, not two. Note the anti_fab validator check only requires the words to be present, so a mechanical pass that appends a pointer to core:anti-fabrication would satisfy it in all 45 - which is exactly why the check is documented as presence-only with soundness left to the author. A batch that adds pointers without reading each skill for actual unverifiable claims would turn 45 green while changing nothing real. If this is worth doing, do it as a per-skill judgment pass, and treat the count as a progress indicator rather than the goal.

The source half of this bee is subsumed by claude-skills-180, specifically its PR4 item claude-skills-184. The 8 source waivers retire there when the substring check is replaced by an exact set-difference over sources.toml skills arrays. Worth knowing why that is a retirement and not a waiver-dodge: the current check is a whole-file substring test, so it cannot distinguish real coverage from an incidental name match, and its waivers today INCLUDE zig skills whose coverage genuinely exists but is invisible to a substring scan. Part of that debt measures the check's blind spot rather than missing sources. The anti_fab half of this bee - 45 skills with no anti-fabrication mention as remeasured 2026-07-30 - is untouched by 180 and stays open. Keep the caution recorded in the earlier comment: the anti_fab check is presence-only, so a mechanical pass appending pointers would turn 45 green while changing nothing real.

title: agent-substrate-overview has no examples anywhere
description:
plugins/tools/agent-sandboxing/skills/agent-substrate-overview: the examples check fails and, unlike the other 16 examples waivers, this one is genuine DEBT rather than a check defect. Verified: ref_count 0, no fenced code blocks and no example header in SKILL.md, and no references/ directory holding them elsewhere. The other 16 are hub skills whose fenced examples live in references/ that the check does not scan.

Fix: add a worked example, or convert the skill to point at one. If the skill is a pure prose overview by design and an example would be filler, reclassify the waiver as CHECK_DEFECT with that reasoning instead — but decide deliberately rather than leaving a DEBT entry pointing at the check-fix issue.

Split out of claude-skills-132: its waiver was initially pointed at claude-skills-130, which owns fixing misfiring CHECKS. A genuine skill-content debt needs its own target.
close_reason: Merged PR #200

title: Decide the name_dir convention: plugin-prefixed frontmatter name vs bare directory name
description:
19 of the 125 quality-baseline waivers are name_dir — the largest single group after anti_fab. All 19 are the same deliberate pattern: frontmatter uses a <plugin>-<skill> prefix (dagu-rest-api, github-workflows, slidev-*, zig-*) while the directory is the bare name, and the check requires name to match the directory exactly.

This needs ONE decision, then it is mechanical either way:
(a) Keep the prefixed frontmatter names and relax the check to accept <plugin>-<dir>, or
(b) Drop the prefixes so name matches the directory, per the Agent Skills spec rule this repo states ('Must exactly match the name property').

Note the interaction with command naming: for PLUGIN skills the frontmatter name sets the last segment of the invocation, so dropping a prefix changes how the skill is invoked. Verify that before choosing (b).

Needed by claude-skills-132, which requires every waiver to carry a linked issue — these 19 entries point here.
close_reason:
Shipped as PR #149. Option (b): dropped the <plugin>- prefixes from 19 skill frontmatter names so name matches the directory. Waivers 101 -> 82, the largest single reduction of this run; zero name_dir remaining, source unchanged at 8.

THE DECISION'S BLOCKER DID NOT EXIST. The issue hedged on whether the frontmatter name sets the invocation segment. It does not — invocation is directory-driven, verified three times independently: zig/skills/build had 'name: zig-build' and lists as 'zig:build'; the validator registry is built from plugin.json skill PATHS (line 1496); upstream docs describe name as a display field defaulting to the directory. Option (a) — relax the check — was rejected as weakening a spec check to accommodate redundant prefixes.

THIS FINISHED A MIGRATION RATHER THAN STARTING ONE. Closed issue claude-skills-90 records PRs #111/#112 doing the same rename for elixir; rust/testing, rust/troubleshooting and elixir/testing already carried bare names on main, so cross-plugin bare duplicates were already live and harmless.

MY CATALOG DESIGN WAS WRONG AND REVIEW REVERSED IT. I proposed converting README and skill-catalog entries to the invocation form (slidev:code) on the reasoning that bare names are ambiguous 'in a flat catalog'. The catalogs are not flat — they are sectioned by plugin, and every other section already used bare names (README:115-117 dagu, :135-138 github; skill-catalog's elixir and github rows). Invocation form would have introduced a third style. Reasoning confidently from an unchecked premise, same shape as generalising N=3 to N=8 in claude-skills-124.

FOUR TRAPS, ALL AVOIDED: slidev-exported (the exportFilename config default, where slidev-export is a PREFIX of it); a #slidev-export-configuration TOC anchor whose heading would go stale; four real docs.github.com/...-github-actions URLs — meaning github, zig and dagu sources.md needed ZERO edits, where my first plan said all per-plugin sources files needed updating; and .bees/issues.jsonl tracker history, left untouched. Gate 3 confirmed all three trap files byte-identical to main.

One plan claim was wrong and is corrected on the record: bees skill: labels are plugin-qualified (skill:claude-code:claude-workflows), not bare. The conclusion held anyway — workers consume labels via jq and use the catalog only as a sectioned keyword fallback, so nothing emits labels from catalog rows.

Follow-up filed: claude-skills-156 (sources.md Version lines stale repo-wide against plugin.json; prefers deleting the second copy over building a check to keep two copies equal).

comments.text: BLOCKER RESOLVED, evidence for whoever takes this. The issue asked to verify whether dropping the prefix changes invocation before choosing (b). It does not — invocation is DIRECTORY-driven, not frontmatter-name-driven. Measured: plugins/languages/zig/skills/build has frontmatter 'name: zig-build' and the live skill listing shows it as 'zig:build'; plugins/tools/github/skills/workflows has 'name: github-workflows' and lists as 'github:workflows'; plugins/tools/dagu/skills/rest-api has 'name: dagu-rest-api'. In every case the invocation segment matches the DIRECTORY, not the prefixed frontmatter name. So option (b) — drop the prefixes so name matches the directory — is safe and does not change how any skill is invoked. Recommendation: take (b). It deletes 19 waivers, matches the Agent Skills spec rule this repo already states ('Must exactly match the name property'), and avoids option (a)'s cost of weakening a spec check to accommodate redundant prefixes. Still needs an operator decision, but the risk that motivated the hedge is measured and absent.

title: Two follow-ups from the PR #132 and #134 reviews
description:
Non-blocking nits recorded by the fable reviewers; both merged PRs were approved as-is.

1. plugins/tools/agent-sandboxing/skills/sandbox/SKILL.md around lines 201-207: the scripts bullet now correctly uses ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/, but the adjacent templates/SandboxTemplate.*.yaml and mise.toml bullets in the same list are also plugin-root artifacts still written skill-relative. title: Remove dead beads tooling: 6 tracked files, a post-merge hook, and an untracked dolt dir
description:
This repo's CLAUDE.md states bees is the tracker and 'beads is removed from all repos', but beads is still wired in and firing on every merge.

Evidence:
- 6 tracked files under .beads/: .gitignore, README.md, config.yaml, interactions.jsonl, issues.jsonl, metadata.json.
- .beads/issues.jsonl holds 9 issues, latest activity 2026-02-21. The live tracker .bees/issues.jsonl holds 135.
- .git/hooks/post-merge is a beads hook that runs 'bd import' after every pull or merge. It printed 'Failed to import bd changes after merge' when PR #131 was squash-merged.
- An untracked .beads/embeddeddolt/ directory keeps reappearing in git status and has been noise in every status check this session.

Proposed cleanup, needs an operator decision because it deletes tracked data:
1. Confirm the 9 beads issues are genuinely dead or migrate anything still wanted into bees.
2. git rm -r .beads/ and remove the post-merge hook.
3. Add .beads/ to .gitignore so a stray local beads install cannot re-add it.

Do NOT do step 2 before step 1 — the file is tracked issue history, and deleting it is irreversible from the working tree alone.

Note /core:beads remains a legitimate SKILL in the marketplace for users whose repos use beads; this issue is only about this repo's own dead installation, not the skill.
close_reason:
Shipped as PR #146. Removed this repo's dead beads installation: .beads/ (6 tracked files + the untracked embeddeddolt dir), the .git/hooks/post-merge import hook, .gitattributes (deleted outright — its only content was the merge=beads driver, and bees uses none), and 221 lines from mise.toml (the beads tool install + all 20 beads:* tasks, an operator-approved scope extension since mise install was still pulling the binary). .beads/ added to .gitignore. 432 deletions, 10 insertions.

/core:beads is UNTOUCHED and remains in the marketplace. It does not depend on this repo's mise tasks — it tells users to add their own (beads/SKILL.md:53). This removed an installation, not a skill.

STEP 1 MATTERED AND I GOT IT HALF RIGHT. Of the 9 tracked issues, 8 were closed (outcomes spot-checked as shipped) and 1 was open: a P2 typescript plugin spec with no such plugin in the marketplace and nothing in bees covering it. Migrated to claude-skills-153 before deleting. But the migration copied only the DESCRIPTION — Gate 3 found the record also carried 2 comments and 4 labels, and both comments were titled CORRECTION and superseded the description (correct path is plugins/languages/typescript/, and the structure is 6 skills using the references pattern, not 4). An agent picking up 153 as first migrated would have built the wrong thing at the wrong path. Recovered verbatim from git history and re-added with provenance headers. Recoverable only because the data was still one commit back.

Documentation the change obligated: this repo's own PR workflow instructed bd close / git add .beads/ / bd ready — dead instructions, updated to bees. Two commit/PR format examples held up 'add beads tooling to mise.toml' as the model change. And AGENTS.md still told non-Claude harnesses 'This project uses bd (beads)... run bd onboard' — found by Gate 3, not by my sweep, because I grepped for the .beads DIRECTORY rather than the bd TOOL. Converted to a symlink to CLAUDE.md per the workspace convention, which is what stops it drifting again.

Follow-up filed: claude-skills-154 (/core:setup still bootstraps new projects with beads while our own convention is bees — not a false claim about this repo, so correctly out of scope here).

title: Harden core-list check: remaining follow-ups from PR #131 review
description:
Non-blocking hardening identified by the fable review of PR #131. The check is correct on the current corpus and negative-tested in both drift directions; these are edge cases that all fail LOUD rather than passing silently, which is why they were not blockers.

1. Fence info-string parsing: a fence opened as triple-backtick immediately followed by a skill name parses as a G1 names-only line, because backtick stripping runs before tokenising. Contrived (no current file does this) but the fix is to skip fence-delimiter lines explicitly before applying G1.

2. EXCLUDED_PARTIAL is documentation shaped as executable config: the const at test/validate-core-list.nu:71-74 is never referenced by code — exclusion is actually implicit in the SATELLITES allowlist. Wiring it buys nothing today, since validator.md's inline numbered form parses under neither grammar. Either annotate it 'documentation only — not referenced by code' or demote it to a comment block. Currently it implies enforcement that does not exist.

3. G1 strips a trailing comma but not a trailing period, while G2 strips both. A names-only line ending in a period fails G1. Safe direction (reports drift rather than passing), but the asymmetry is arbitrary — make both strip the same trailing punctuation set.

Already fixed pre-merge, recorded here so the reasoning is not lost: G2 now requires the remainder after the skill name to be empty or start with an open paren, so a prose bullet like '- /core:tdd — standing discipline' is no longer counted as a load-list entry. Without that, such a bullet could MASK a genuinely missing name, which is the same false-pass class the structural check was built to remove. Verified with a masking test: name removed from work.md's real list plus present as a prose bullet fails correctly. Also unified the canonical extractor and both grammars onto shared CORE_NAME and SKILL_NAME consts; they previously disagreed on case and digits, so /core:s3-tools would parse in a satellite but drop from the canonical block.
close_reason: Closed with PR #139 (a598efe): fence delimiters explicitly excluded from the grammar via a shared is-fence-delimiter predicate, EXCLUDED_PARTIAL demoted from documentation-shaped-as-config to a header comment naming claude-skills-125, and the G1/G2 punctuation asymmetry dissolved with G2's deletion.

comments.text:
CORRECTION to this issue's framing, and one item removed because it was fixed.

My original text said the remaining edges 'all fail LOUD rather than passing silently'. That was FALSE. An adversarial review found two SILENT false passes in the same class, both tool-verified by me independently:

- PoC A: with /core:tdd deleted from work.md's real list, appending '- `/core:tdd` (standing discipline)' anywhere in the file made the check print a green tick for that file.
- PoC B: same deletion, plus a fenced worked example containing bare /core:tdd on its own line. Also green.

Root cause: extract-load-list-names unioned every G1/G2 hit across the whole file and compared sets per FILE rather than per LIST, so any second occurrence anywhere restored a deleted name to the union. My earlier pre-merge G2 fix (requiring a paren rather than an em-dash after the name) closed ONE idiom and simultaneously blessed the more dangerous one — it documented paren-annotated bullets as legitimate list entries with nothing keeping authors from using that idiom in prose.

FIXED in PR #131 rather than deferred here, since a silent false pass in a check people trust is worse than a stale diff: lists are now compared per contiguous RUN of list lines. A run carrying fewer than 2 /core: names is ignored (so a lone prose mention still costs nothing), and more than one qualifying run in a satellite is reported as ambiguous rather than guessed at. Regression matrix now covers five cases — both PoCs FAIL, lone prose bullet PASSES, extra-name-in-list FAILS, missing-name FAILS.

The header comment was also overclaiming ('prose mentions are ignored by design' was untrue for paren bullets; 'both drift directions are checked' was maskable). Rewritten to state what the check guarantees and to list three things it still cannot see.

STILL OPEN in this issue: the fence info-string edge, the trailing-punctuation asymmetry between G1 and G2, and EXCLUDED_PARTIAL being unreferenced documentation shaped like executable config. Those three genuinely do fail loud or are cosmetic.

Refinement after attempting to break the per-run design myself. Three attacks run:

ATTACK 1 — delete a name from its position and re-add it as a paren bullet adjacent to the real list, so it joins the same run: FAILS correctly (the placeholder line splits the run). Note the genuine case — name deleted from position and re-added inside the same contiguous run with no gap — PASSES, and that is correct: the name really is in the list. Recorded in the header as behaviour, not a gap.

ATTACK 2 — blank line inside a single logical list: FAILS. A false fail, accepted because it is loud and names the parsed runs.

ATTACK 3 — a satellite carrying a SECOND complete example list: FAILED under the 'exactly one run' rule. That was a real usability defect, not an edge case: leader-spawn-example.md exists to hold worked examples, so adding a second one would have broken CI for legitimate content.

Fixed by replacing 'exactly one run' with 'EVERY run must match canonical'. Strictly better — both masking PoCs still fail (their partial run disagrees with canonical), while a second correct list now passes. Regression matrix is 7 cases: baseline PASS, PoC A FAIL, PoC B FAIL, lone prose bullet PASS, extra-name FAIL, missing-name FAIL, second-complete-list PASS.

Header comment corrected again — it had been rewritten to describe the single-run rule that no longer exists, and now also records the two accepted false-fail cases (blank-line split, deliberate partial list).

title: Skill-authoring hygiene: duplicate anti-fab blocks, missing sources entry, numeric drift
description:
Small verified fixes across the claude-code plugin, grouped because each is one to three lines.

1. Three verbatim copies of core:anti-fabrication content live in plugin bodies (claude-skills:397-433 is 37 lines, claude-skills-benchmark:109-128 is 20 lines, and plugin-marketplace / claude-plugins / claude-statusline have no mention at all). Validator check 10 accepts a single core:anti-fabrication reference. Replace copies with a pointer; add the pointer where missing. Clears plugin-marketplace:anti_fab, claude-plugins:anti_fab, and claude-statusline:anti_fab waivers.

2. skills/sources.md has no skill-update section (grep verified) — the skill about source tracking is itself untracked. Add it; clears the skill-update:source waiver.

3. skill-update:links is a FALSE POSITIVE with an honest fix: the flagged path templates/0.11.0/commands.md at :90 is illustrative, not a link. Reword to 'a templates/<version>/ snapshot' so the check regex (which requires a file extension) stops matching; waiver drops.

4. Numeric drift, three literals for two different quantities: the description cap appears as 1024 (validator check 1, claude-skills-benchmark:25) and 1,536 (claude-skills:90). These are genuinely different bounds — 1,536 is Claude Code's listing-truncation limit for description plus when_to_use, 1024 is our stricter enforced cap. Note both explicitly at claude-skills:90 so they stop reading as a contradiction.

5. Hedging-verb prohibition is stated three times (claude-skills:134, again at :366-376, and plugins/tools/claude-code/hooks/session-start.sh:20-21) with no validator check behind it. Collapse to one judgment line in claude-skills and drop the other two.

6. The multi-model targets (70/85/95 percent at claude-skills-benchmark:66-70, 90 percent and under-5-percent activation at :80) also appear at claude-skills:344. State them in references/evaluation-guide.md only; pointer elsewhere.

Numeric drift at claude-skills:90 disambiguated (1536 listing truncation vs 1024 enforced cap). Benchmark's stale 11-check table replaced with intent plus a pointer to test/validate-skills-quality.nu as the single source. skill-update illustrative path reworded.
