title: gitleaks.sh arg loop dereferences $2 with no presence check
description:
Split from claude-skills-267 Gate 3 round 6 finding W3. Deliberately not fixed in PR #246 — touching bash argument parsing at approval time was not worth the risk for a cosmetic issue.

VERIFIED: 'bash gitleaks.sh --runtime' (flag with no value) prints 'line 478: $2: unbound variable'.

NOT a defect — it fails closed. The reviewer measured the real exit codes for --runtime, --path, --config, --baseline, --report and --bogus across BOTH scripts: all exit 1, and none claims a scan. So a malformed invocation can never produce a false clean result. This is an ugly message, not a security gap.

Fix: presence-check $2 before dereferencing in the argument-parsing while loop, and emit a clear 'flag X requires a value' message. Mirror whatever gitleaks.nu does for the same case so the two stay in conformance — PR #246 established that the three implementations agree, and a divergence here would be the start of the drift that PR spent five rounds eliminating.

AC: a flag given without its value produces a clear error naming the flag, exits nonzero, and never reports a scan result. Behaviour identical in gitleaks.nu and gitleaks.sh.

title: beads template beads:show is broken on bd 1.1.2 — three defects in one task
description:
Found by impl-264 during claude-skills-264, deliberately not fixed there — three distinct defects in one task is its own unit of work, not a ride-along in an unrelated PR.

plugins/tools/beads/skills/beads/templates/mise.toml, the beads:show task, against bd 1.1.2:

**1. Array-vs-record binding.** 'bd show --json' returns an ARRAY, so 'let task = (... | from json)' binds a table rather than a record. Every field then prints bracket-wrapped — observed output 'Task: [proj264b-niy]' instead of 'Task: proj264b-niy'.

**2. An unguarded dereference that aborts the task.** Line 17 dereferences $task.dependencies WITHOUT the '?' optional guard that the line immediately above it does use. On a task with no such column it raises nu::shell::column_not_found and the task dies rather than degrading. The inconsistency between adjacent lines is the tell — one was guarded and the next was not.

**3. The fields do not exist in 1.1.2 at all.** 'dependencies' and 'blocking' are not in bd 1.1.2's show output. The real fields are 'dependency_count' and 'dependent_count'. So even with the binding and the guard fixed, the task would report nothing useful.

Note defect 3 subsumes the others in a sense — you cannot fix 1 and 2 correctly without deciding what the task should show now that the field names changed. Decide that first, then the binding and guard follow.

This is the same class as claude-skills-262 (template drifted from the tool while the skill body was corrected), which is why it was found: the fake-HOME isolated run introduced by 264 exercises tasks that reading never did.

AC: beads:show produces correct unbracketed output against bd 1.1.2, using fields that actually exist; the unguarded deref given the same '?' treatment as its neighbour or removed; verified by running the task in an isolated project with a fake HOME against a real throwaway beads DB — not by reading, which is what let all three drift in. Add a dated note to sources.toml; do NOT touch last_full_check.

title: Root mise.toml nushell platform patterns are inert — platforms is a string and three keys are malformed
description:
Found by impl-264 while choosing a platform-pattern shape for the beads template, and independently verified by the lead before filing rather than taken on report.

/Users/vinnie/github/claude-skills/mise.toml's 'github:nushell/nushell' entry does not parse the way it reads. Verified with python tomllib:

  keys: ['version', 'exe', 'platforms', ' linux-x64 ', ' macos-arm64 ', ' macos-x64 ']
  platforms type: str
  platforms value: '{ linux-arm64 = { asset_pattern = "nu-*-aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz" }'

Two problems. 'platforms' is a STRING, truncated at the first closing brace, rather than a nested table. And ' linux-x64 ', ' macos-arm64 ', ' macos-x64 ' — note the leading and trailing spaces — are siblings of 'version', not entries under platforms. The quoting in the source line closes and reopens in the wrong places.

Consequence: every nushell asset pattern in this file is inert. Nushell still installs because mise auto-resolves platforms left undeclared, which is exactly why nobody noticed — the file looks configured and behaves as if it were not. That is the failure mode worth naming: not a broken build, a silently ignored configuration.

Scope note: only the nushell entry was checked. Other entries in the same file may share the pattern if they were written the same way — check them all rather than fixing this one line, since a single malformed quote style tends to have been copied.

The beads template written under claude-skills-264 deliberately did NOT copy this shape and uses a proper nested record instead; that one is verified parsing correctly and can serve as the reference form.

AC: nushell's platforms parse as a nested table with no space-padded sibling keys; every other tool entry in the file audited for the same defect; verified by tomllib or nushell 'open' showing platforms as a record and no stray sibling keys — not by reading the line, which is what hid it.

title: beads template drops the no-arg tree mode and never declares nushell in [tools]
description:
Two items from Gate 3 on PR #244 (claude-skills-262), both left out of that PR deliberately — one is a scope call, the other pre-existing.

**1. beads:tree lost its no-arg mode, and a one-line fallback exists.** templates/mise.toml:213-219. The original 'bd tree' with no argument printed the whole forest; the replacement 'bd children <id> --pretty' requires an id, so PR #244 changed the task arg from optional to required and the capability is gone.

Gate 3 verified a recoverable form live: 'bd list --pretty' with zero args prints exactly that — the full recursive tree of all issues. So the optional arg could be restored: no arg -> bd list --pretty, arg -> bd children <id> --pretty.

Also the task description now understates what it does. It reads 'List child tasks of a parent task', but --pretty prints the full recursive subtree including grandchildren — Gate 3 confirmed by building parent -> child -> grandchild. Worth correcting whether or not the no-arg mode returns.

**2. The template never declares nushell, so every scripted task fails as shipped.** templates/mise.toml:1-7 lists only github:gastownhall/beads in [tools], yet several tasks use a nu shebang. In a clean project every one of them fails with 'env: nu: No such file or directory'.

Verified pre-existing and not introduced by #244: in an isolated project with a fake HOME, the untouched beads:ready task fails identically to the tasks that PR changed. It only looks like it works on a machine where nushell happens to be on PATH from elsewhere — which is exactly the operator's machine, and exactly why nobody noticed.

This is the more consequential of the two: a template whose tasks cannot run as shipped is broken for every new installer, while the tree regression only costs a convenience. Fix is adding nushell to [tools] — but check the version pin against what the repo's own conventions use rather than picking one, and verify by running the tasks in a project with a fake HOME so the operator's global config cannot mask the result.

AC: nushell declared in the template's [tools] and every scripted task verified running in an isolated project with a fake HOME; beads:tree's no-arg mode restored or its removal justified in a comment; the description corrected to say it prints the recursive subtree. Verify by execution in an isolated project, not by reading — reading is what let the original drift in.
close_reason:
PR #245 merged 5f85531. nushell declared and pinned to 0.113.1 in the template's [tools], beads:tree no-arg mode restored, descriptions corrected.

Evidence for the main item: under 'env -i' with a fake HOME and minimal PATH, 13/13 scripted tasks failed 'env: nu: No such file or directory' before and 13/13 execute after — reproduced independently by Gate 3, and with tasks verified DOING their job against real Dolt data rather than merely exiting 0.

Pin reasoning, agreed independently by implementer and reviewer: this template SHIPS nu code, unlike the nushell skill's template which only INSTALLS nu. 'latest' now resolves to 0.114.1, a minor ahead of what CI runs, against a pre-1.0 tool. The deciding asymmetry, which is the reusable part: a stale pin fails LOUD at update time, 'latest' fails SILENT at install time.

Gate 3 REJECTED round one on a finding that only execution could produce. The platforms table the implementer added was NET-HARMFUL, not merely unverified: its linux-x64 '-gnu' asset_pattern OVERRODE mise's libc-aware auto-resolution and installed a binary that cannot start on musl — alpine x64 exit 133, missing glibc loader — where deleting the table makes it work. The implementer then reproduced it on arm64 too. Auto-resolution verified correct with no pattern on all five platform cells. The fix was a deletion; the smaller diff was the more correct one.

The beads:tree description took FOUR attempts to become true, and the sequence is the record worth keeping: (1) understated recursion; (2) undisclosed open/closed asymmetry between the two modes; (3) promised a 'FULL recursive subtree' the no-arg form does not deliver — bd list --pretty prunes closed at any depth and RE-ROOTS open descendants to top level, so a grandchild prints as a root and the printed hierarchy differs from the real one; (4) true. Every one of the first three read cleanly. Every author had run the command.

The implementer's own diagnosis is the sharpest artifact here: it had SEEN the grandchild printed as a root, reported it to the lead as 'slightly surprising', and filed it as a curiosity rather than as its own comment's first sentence being false in front of it. Its formulation: 'the gate that actually failed was not verification, it was willingness to be contradicted by my own terminal.' Executing is necessary and not sufficient.

A fifth false claim entered late and its provenance is instructive: 'bd is a static Go binary and libc-indifferent' originated as an explanatory aside in Gate 3's own REJECT, was relayed by the lead unmarked as established fact, and was written into a shipped comment. Both predicates false — file reports it dynamically linked with a glibc interpreter, and it exits 127 on alpine arm64. Caught only when the reviewer, on a verification pass, falsified its own earlier claim. The conclusion survived for a different reason: upstream publishes exactly one Linux asset per arch, so no pattern can override a choice that does not exist.

Three false gates also surfaced in this PR, all exit 0, none covering the artifact in question: an empty-stage gitleaks; a gitleaks whose flags were silently discarded by a shell wrapper (filed P2 as claude-skills-267); and a CI pass on content superseded by a later rewrite. The practice that fixed it: bind every result to the content it covers — the runner now names the shas and the implementer predicts the expected count BEFORE the run, which makes a mismatch impossible to rationalise afterwards.

sources.toml records the execution evidence, the four-round correction history, and the false claims explicitly AS false so they cannot be re-cited. last_full_check untouched at 2026-08-04 — this was a template check, not a full skill re-verification.

comments.text:
Correction to this bee's own premise, found by impl-264 while testing its fix — recording it here so the error does not get re-cited as established.

This bee states that Gate 3 on PR #244 'verified a recoverable form live: bd list --pretty with zero args prints exactly that — the full recursive tree of all issues.' That is wrong in one word. Measured on bd 1.1.2: it prints the full recursive tree of all **OPEN** issues. Closing a root removed it from the output, 4 issues down to 3.

Not a criticism of that review — recursion was the question it was asked and it answered that correctly. But the claim was written as unqualified and this bee inherited it unqualified, which is how a half-true finding becomes a premise.

The consequence is a real defect in the fix this bee produced: beads:tree's two modes apply DIFFERENT closed-issue filters. bd list --pretty (no-arg branch) hides closed; bd children <id> --pretty (arg branch) shows them, rendered with a check mark, and has no status filter at all — --pretty is its only flag. So the two modes of one task filter differently, undocumented, and the new description's 'every root' asserts a symmetry that does not exist.

bd list --all --pretty aligns them exactly, restoring the closed root to match the children form.

Open question at time of writing, deliberately not settled here: whether to align via --all or to keep the asymmetry and describe it accurately. Each mode is defensible on its own terms — open-only is the right default for a whole-tracker overview, closed descendants are useful context in a subtree — and since bd children cannot be filtered, the constraint forces one of them rather than forcing alignment. The lead leans documenting, the implementer leans aligning, and a third read was requested. Whichever lands, the description must state the actual filtering rather than implying symmetry.

Also confirmed while testing: 'mise run beads:tree ""' takes the whole-forest branch, because "" | is-empty is true on nu 0.113.1. Benign, arguably friendlier, but undocumented.

title: vantage_ex build.nu: generated_at claims Z but prints local time, and the artifact stamps the parent commit's sha
description:
Two nits from Gate 3 on vantage_ex PR #165 (claude-skills-261). Both pre-existing, neither introduced by that PR, both left unfixed there deliberately as out of scope.

**1. generated_at is a false UTC timestamp — this is the real bug.** docs/build.nu:76 formats local time and appends a literal 'Z', which asserts UTC. Verified by execution at a single instant: TZ=UTC produced '12:37:37Z' and TZ=Asia/Tokyo produced '21:37:37Z'. Anyone reading the committed artifact's timestamp gets a value that is wrong by the builder's UTC offset while explicitly claiming otherwise, and two builders in different timezones produce timestamps that cannot be compared.

Fix is a pipe through 'date to-timezone UTC' before formatting, or dropping the Z if local time is genuinely intended — but the former is almost certainly right for an artifact committed to a shared repo. Cheap, and it makes the field honest rather than merely volatile.

**2. The committed artifact stamps the PARENT commit's sha.** Verified: the committed index.html says 9b8f792 while the commit containing it is 82f82c3. This is inherent — at build time the commit that will carry the artifact does not exist yet, so the stamp is always one behind. PR #165 reduced the spurious regen diff from 788 lines to about 4 (2 sha stamps + 2 timestamps), but not to zero, so every regeneration commit still carries a small diff even with no content change.

There is no fix that keeps the current shape. Options, in rough order of cost: stamp at publish time rather than commit time; drop the sha from the artifact as PR #165 dropped the branch, accepting that the artifact self-identifies by content only; or document the off-by-one so nobody reads the stamp as the commit they are looking at. Decide deliberately rather than treating it as a defect to squash — the current behaviour is defensible if documented.

Fixing item 1 alone takes the regen diff from ~4 lines to ~2.

AC: generated_at emits real UTC or drops the false Z; the sha off-by-one either fixed or documented in build.nu with the reasoning. Verify the timestamp fix by building the same content under two different TZ values and confirming byte-identical output — that is the test that catches it, and it is the test that was missing.
close_reason:
vantage_ex PR #166 merged e91aeba.

Item 1 FIXED — generated_at now emits real UTC. docs/build.nu:76 was 'date now | format date "...Z"', where date now yields LOCAL time and the Z is a literal in the format string. Now pipes through 'date to-timezone UTC' first.

The bug was worse than the bee described. At one instant, TZ=UTC gave 2026-08-06T15:27:27Z and TZ=Asia/Tokyo gave 2026-08-07T00:27:27Z — a different DATE, both stamped Z. And it was live on main, provable from committed data alone: main's artifact claimed 08:30:42Z while the commit carrying it was stamped 08:38:19-04:00. A file cannot be built four hours before a commit made eight minutes after it. That internal contradiction is stronger evidence than any single test run.

Verification was the AC's named test, done properly. The implementer's first AFTER pair straddled a second boundary and differed by 1s; rather than explain that away it re-ran for a same-second pair and added a 5-sample paired control — 5 OLD pairs differing by 9h at the same second, 5 NEW pairs matching exactly. Structural, not drift. Byte-identical output under TZ=UTC and TZ=Asia/Tokyo, matching sha256.

Item 2 DECIDED, not squashed — document the sha off-by-one rather than drop or publish-time-stamp it, recorded in build.nu itself. The reasoning that settled it: restraint governs what you ADD and is not a licence to delete working provenance. The sha accurately names the source tree the page was built FROM, which is real information — unlike the branch name PR #165 dropped, which often did not exist on the remote. The implementer also tried to falsify its own conclusion by checking whether squash-merge leaves the stamped sha unreachable, which would have killed that argument; merge-base confirmed it reachable.

One judgement beyond the AC, approved: the rendered header now reads 'built from <sha> at <time>'. The AC asked for the reasoning in build.nu, but that only reaches people reading build.nu — the likely misreader is looking at the page. One word of template, fixed at the point of consumption.

Root-cause sweep found no other site using the same date idiom.

Process note worth keeping: this PR sat blocked ~11 hours across a GitHub-wide Actions outage (major_outage, incident 2026-08-06T15:22Z). After recovery its run was a ZOMBIE — status queued, conclusion null, last updated 6 hours prior, while 'gh run cancel' reported it completed and 'gh run rerun' reported it already running. Contradictory states, unrecoverable by rerun. Escape was closing and reopening the PR, which re-triggers the pull_request workflow with no empty commit and no history noise. Worth remembering: a run stuck queued for hours after an outage is dead, not waiting, and close/reopen is the clean way out.

title: beads templates/mise.toml teaches six commands that do not exist in bd 1.1.2
description:
Found by impl-beads during the 1.1.2 update (PR #243) and confirmed live by Gate 3 against bd 1.1.2 in a throwaway repo. Pre-existing, correctly kept out of that PR's scope.

plugins/tools/beads/skills/beads/templates/mise.toml defines mise tasks wrapping bd commands. Six of them fail outright on 1.1.2 — verified by execution, not inferred from docs:

- 'bd sync' -> Error: unknown command
- 'bd pull' -> Error: unknown command
- 'bd rebuild' -> Error: unknown command
- 'bd tree' -> Error: unknown command
- 'bd dep graph' -> not a subcommand; falls through to dep help
- line 199 uses 'bd label --add', a flag form that does not exist

One correction to the original report, which is why this bee reflects Gate 3's testing rather than the finder's list: **'bd status' WORKS** in 1.1.2 and prints 'Issue Database Status'. It is not deprecated. Two smaller wording problems near it, though: the task description 'Show beads sync status' mislabels what the command actually shows, and the beads:rebuild task description 'Rebuild SQLite cache from JSONL files' describes a backend that has been removed.

Severity: medium. Anyone who installs this template gets six tasks that error on first use. Blast radius is template installers only — SKILL.md itself no longer teaches these forms, since sources.toml already records the corrections. That is the sharp part: the skill body was corrected and its own template was not, so the template now contradicts the skill that ships it.

Note this template ALSO already uses the correct gastownhall/beads backend, so the slug is not the issue here — only the command forms.

AC: every bd command in that template verified against a live 1.1.2 install and either corrected to a working form or removed; the two mislabelled task descriptions fixed; a note in sources.toml recording that the template was checked, since it was demonstrably missed when the skill body was corrected. Verify by running each mise task against a throwaway beads repo under the scratchpad — never against a real tracker — rather than by reading the skill text, which is what let this drift in the first place.
close_reason:
PR #244 merged 6a4bf94. All six broken commands in templates/mise.toml corrected or removed, verified live against bd 1.1.2 in throwaway repos — never a real tracker.

bd sync -> bd dolt push; bd pull -> bd dolt pull; bd tree -> bd children <id> --pretty; bd dep graph -> bd dep tree <id>; bd label <id> --add <labels> -> a loop over bd label add; bd rebuild REMOVED (no cache to rebuild — Dolt is source of truth). bd status left alone: the original finder had reported it deprecated, Gate 3 tested it and it works; only its description was wrong.

The finding worth carrying: a substitution is a SEMANTIC claim, not an existence check. Replacing a loudly-broken command with one that merely runs is worse than leaving it broken, because it stops erroring and starts lying. Gate 3 attacked each substitution on that basis — the sharpest test was bd children --pretty, whose help text calls it 'a convenience alias for bd list --parent', implying one level. Built parent -> child -> GRANDCHILD: the grandchild printed. Semantics preserved, so the task keeps its name. bd dep tree's arg going optional->required is genuinely forced and no whole-graph command exists in 1.1.2, so that narrowing is disclosed in the description rather than hidden.

Two defects the implementer found by executing rather than reading, both of which would have shipped silently:
- bd label add takes exactly ONE label and does NOT split a comma-separated string: 'foo,bar' becomes one literal label. Fixing only the flag form would have produced a task that silently creates a wrong label instead of erroring. Fixed with split row plus a loop.
- That loop then aborted mid-apply on an empty element ('cc,,dd' applied cc, errored, never reached dd), leaving an issue half-labelled. Failing loudly on malformed input is fine; a partial mutation is not. Fixed with a where filter and verified against both 'cc,,dd' and a trailing comma.

Gate 3 caught one contradiction in the fix itself, which is the same defect class this bee existed to close: the removal comment asserted bd rebuild has 'no equivalent', while SKILL.md:449-451 and an earlier sources.toml note both name bd doctor as the successor. Sent back rather than merged — shipping a fresh template-vs-skill contradiction inside the fix for one would have been the ironic outcome.

The implementer then did the right thing with that correction: it verified bd doctor LIVE instead of trusting SKILL.md, and found it errors 'not yet supported in embedded mode' under the template's own default init mode. So it recorded the caveat rather than asserting bd doctor just works — trading one contradiction for a subtler one was the available mistake and it avoided it. Also declined to add a beads:doctor task on the grounds the command is non-functional in the template's default mode.

Filed separately as claude-skills-264: the no-arg forest mode dropped from beads:tree (bd list --pretty covers it), and the template's [tools] not declaring nushell, so every scripted task fails env: nu: No such file or directory in a clean project.

title: vantage_ex docs/build.nu stamps the wrong branch and embeds absolute builder paths; plus a duplicate adjunct doc on an unmerged branch
description:
Three items found by Gate 3 while reviewing vantage_ex PRs #162/#163/#164 (claude-skills-162 and 260). All are in vantage_ex, none blocked those PRs, and all are pre-existing rather than introduced by them.

**1. build.nu stamps the builder's local branch, not the PR's.** The committed docs/index.html header reads 'pr162 @ 66705b0' — 'pr162' is the throwaway branch name in the scratchpad clone the build happened to run in, and the sha is the parent commit. So the artifact on main advertises provenance that is misleading at best. Pre-existing class: the index before #163 was stamped 'docs/adr-native-binary-deployment @ 84395f8', another builder's local branch. Fix belongs in docs/build.nu — stamp the real branch, or drop the branch from the stamp entirely, since a generated artifact claiming a branch that does not exist on the remote is worse than no claim.

**2. build.nu embeds absolute builder paths in every entry.** The index carries the building machine's full filesystem path in roughly 200 entries — currently '/private/tmp/.../scratchpad/vx162/...'. Long-standing: the pre-#163 index carried a different builder's absolute path. Low severity because vantage_ex is private, but it makes the generated file's diff noisy and machine-dependent, so two people rebuilding the same content produce different bytes. Strip the prefix to a repo-relative path in build.nu.

Items 1 and 2 share a fix site and should land together.

**3. A duplicate adjunct-convention doc exists on an unmerged branch.** docs/conventions/vantage-ex-docs-adjunct.md (123 lines, commit 2dfdd56) lives on branch feature/featskills-epic-sizing-heuristics-dependency-ordering. It covers the SAME topic as the docs/vantageex-conventions.md just merged to main via #162 — the read-only vantage_ex docs-adjunct convention — but is different content, different structure, different hash. If that branch ever merges, main gets two overlapping docs on one convention with no indication which governs.

This is not a defect in either doc; it is a collision waiting to happen. Whoever lands that branch reconciles them — most likely keeping one and deleting the other rather than merging, since they are independent treatments rather than diverged copies. Note the branch also explains the provenance: docs/conventions/ was where that author put it, which is why the relocated doc listed docs/conventions/ as a notable subdirectory even though it has never existed on main.

AC: build.nu stamps a real branch or none, and emits repo-relative paths; the duplicate adjunct doc reconciled to one authority when that feature branch lands. Verify the build.nu changes by rebuilding twice from different directories and confirming byte-identical output apart from deliberately volatile fields.

comments.text:
2026-08-06: items 1 and 2 DONE — vantage_ex PR #165 merged a7c61a2. Item 3 (the duplicate adjunct doc) remains, blocked until its feature branch lands; leaving this bee OPEN for it.

Stamp: branch DROPPED from the committed artifact entirely (title, header meta, and the data JSON record), git_sha kept. Reasoning: a sha resolves from any clone, a builder's local branch name does not. Gate 3 confirmed zero consumers of docs.branch or __BRANCH__ repo-wide, and that the JS which DOES read .path still works since repo-relative paths still end .jsx.

Paths: made repo-relative. Root cause was not visible from reading build.nu — nushell's glob returns ABSOLUTE paths even for a relative pattern run from the target cwd, so every entry carried the builder's full path. Confirmed directly by both the implementer and Gate 3.

The evidence that matters, since reproducibility was the whole deliverable: BEFORE, two differently-named clones produced a 788-line diff, 394 of them path entries. AFTER, Gate 3 reproduced with two FRESH clones (not the implementer's cp -R, which could have shared state) and got a ZERO-line diff — both builds landed in the same second so even the timestamp matched. A later same-clone rebuild under LC_ALL=C plus a TZ override differed in exactly 2 lines, both generated_at. Also tested a symlinked repo path: clean.

Ordering was checked and is not filesystem-dependent — every glob is piped through sort before sort_alpha (build.nu:90,111,130,148), and the C-locale run produced identical ordering. That was the failure mode a same-machine test would never surface.

Two nits Gate 3 raised, neither blocking, both recorded as claude-skills-263 rather than fixed here:
- The committed artifact stamps the PARENT commit's sha (committed index says 9b8f792 while the head is 82f82c3), because the commit containing the artifact does not exist when the artifact is built. Inherent to committing a self-referential sha. Spurious regen diff is reduced from 788 lines to about 4, not to 0.
- generated_at prints LOCAL time with a literal Z suffix — verified TZ=UTC gives 12:37:37Z and TZ=Asia/Tokyo gives 21:37:37Z for the same instant. The Z is simply false.

title: vantage_ex conventions doc has four stale content claims, and docs/index.html needs a rebuild
description:
Follow-up to claude-skills-162 (vantage_ex PR #162, merged eb91de2). All four found by Gate 3 on that PR and deliberately left unfixed there: the PR's contract was a byte-identical relocation of content from claude-skills 4fc712f, so correcting the text in the same commit would have broken the provenance claim being verified. Fixing them now is clean.

All four live in vantage_ex's docs/vantageex-conventions.md. One small commit covers them.

**1. ADR 095 citation points at the wrong ADR — the interesting one.** Line 31 cites 'Multi-repo workspace conventions (ADR 043, ADR 095)'. Gate 3 traced the renumbering: at write time 095-cross-repo-epic-model.md existed, itself renumbered from a duplicate 086 on 2026-06-20 (commit 50dc3ca). It was renumbered AGAIN to 098-cross-repo-epic-model.md, and 095 is now 095-resource-pressure-telemetry-and-auto-throttle.md — an unrelated topic. So the citation resolves to a real ADR that says something else, which is worse than a dangling reference because nothing errors. Change 095 to 098.

Worth noting the doc already carries its own mitigation at line 58 — 'Always grep for relevant keywords rather than guessing numbers' — which is the right instinct and did not save it.

Gate 3 checked the other ten citations (008, 026, 029, 030, 035, 043, 045, 056, 071, 081): all exist on origin/main with titles matching their parentheticals. Only 095 rotted.

**2. Line 68 lists docs/conventions/ as a notable subdirectory. It does not exist** on origin/main — docs/audit/ and docs/research/ do. Verified via git ls-tree.

**3. Line 58's '95 ADRs exist (001 through 095)' is stale** — origin/main has 107 ADR files spanning 001-110. Self-qualified with 'As of the time this document was written', so honest rather than wrong, but stale on arrival and worth refreshing since the same line carries the grep-dont-guess advice.

**4. Line 14 conflates the two repos.** It gives 'Issues target files in the vantage_ex repo' as an indicator that an epic touches the VantageEx CODEBASE. The codebase is vantageex; vantage_ex is the docs repo. If issues genuinely target vantage_ex files then it is a write target, not the read-only adjunct the surrounding section describes — so the slip undercuts that section's own rule. This is the one place Gate 3 judged the wording could actually mislead a future agent.

**5. Separately: docs/index.html needs a rebuild.** It is a committed snapshot generated by docs/build.nu, and the new doc will not appear in that viewer until someone reruns the build. Measured before merge: the freshly-built index contains the doc, the committed one on main does not. Deliberately excluded from PR #162 — it is ~3.2MB of generated output that would have dominated an 89-line addition, and the WIP branch docs/loop-handoff-k3s-topology already carries its own modified index.html, so a competing regeneration was a near-certain conflict. Rebuild once that branch lands rather than now.

AC: the four content claims corrected in vantage_ex; index.html rebuilt after the WIP branch merges. Verify ADR citations by resolving each number against origin/main rather than trusting the text, since that is exactly how 095 rotted.
close_reason:
Both parts done. vantage_ex PR #163 (66705b0) rebuilt docs/index.html; PR #164 (9b8f792) corrected the four content claims, with its own index rebuild in-commit per the repo convention.

The four fixes, each verified against origin/main before editing rather than taken from the review:
- ADR 095 -> 098. Gate 3 traced the rename to commit f6e0673 ('normalize ADR numbering', #141) and confirmed 098's current title genuinely fits the 'multi-repo workspace conventions' grouping — so this was the successor, not another wrong hop.
- ADR count: 107 spanning 001-110 (missing 002, 003, 004), replacing '95 ADRs (001 through 095)'.
- docs/conventions/ bullet deleted — it has NEVER existed on main.
- Line 14's vantage_ex/vantageex slip corrected, with a parenthetical naming which repo is which.

Three of my own errors in this, worth recording because two were caught by review rather than by me:

1. I told the reviewer and the operator 'docs/ has no subdirectories at all'. WRONG — main has docs/audit, docs/research, docs/scripts. My check was 'git ls-tree --name-only origin/main docs/ | grep /$', and --name-only does not append trailing slashes, so the grep matched nothing and I read that as absence. Deleting the docs/conventions/ bullet was still right, but my stated reason was not. This is the never-verify-a-list-against-the-extraction-that-produced-it trap.

2. My rewrite of line 58 asserted 'ADRs are renumbered on collision' as a general convention, generalised from one instance — I flagged it to Gate 3 as the most likely place I had over-reached. It held: three independent renumber events in history (2b4a7db, 50dc3ca, f6e0673) plus commit 696b132 adding a duplicate-ADR-number CI check.

3. That same rewrite ended '095 above was renumbered to 098' — but after the fix no 095 remained above, so the antecedent was gone and the phrase referenced the doc's own edit history. Caught as a Gate 3 nit and fixed before merge to name the ADR by subject and give its full path (086 -> 095 -> 098).

Also: PR #162 was merged prematurely on an initial APPROVE while the indexing question I had commissioned was still open; the reviewer's follow-up reversed it, which cost a second PR (#163) rather than a second commit. Both of my objections to including the index were false — the delta is ~415 lines not 3.2MB, and generated-file conflicts here are routine and resolved by rerunning build.nu.

Two items surfaced by Gate 3 and filed separately as claude-skills-261 rather than fixed here.
