title: Optional userConfig option fields are unvalidated, and a typo'd self-test harness key is silently ignored
description:
Two residual items from PR #237 (claude-skills-256), both reported by Gate 3 and deliberately left out of that PR's scope.

**1. Optional option fields accept any type.** validate-user-config-option checks the three REQUIRED fields (type, title, description) and constrains type to the five-value enum. Upstream also documents optional fields with definite types: sensitive, required and multiple are booleans; min and max are numbers; default takes the option's own declared type.

Today a wrong-typed optional passes with 0 errors — 'sensitive: "yes"' and 'min: "3"' both validate clean. Confirmed by Gate 3, and note the PR does have a fixture proving a correctly-typed 'sensitive: true' is not false-rejected, so the accept direction is already pinned.

'default' is the interesting one and should be decided explicitly rather than swept in: its valid type DEPENDS on the sibling 'type' field, so checking it means a cross-field check within the option record. That may be worth doing or may be over-reach — decide and record the reasoning. The booleans and numbers are mechanical.

**2. A typo'd harness key is silently ignored.** The self-test runner reads assertion fields via 'get -o', so a fixture writing 'expect_errors_contains' instead of 'expect_error_contains' is not an error — the assertion simply never runs and the case passes on its remaining assertions. This is pre-existing (expect_success has the same property) and became more consequential in #237, which added expect_error_contains precisely because count-only assertions were masking fallthroughs. A typo there silently restores the masking the field exists to prevent.

Worth a guard: validate each fixture record's keys against the set of known assertion field names and fail the self-test on an unrecognized one. Cheap, and it protects every future fixture rather than one rule.

AC: optional option fields type-checked where the type is unambiguous, with the 'default' decision recorded either way; unknown-key guard on self-test fixtures. Reject fixture per rule differing from a valid manifest in exactly one dimension. Mutation-verify each: neuter, confirm the SPECIFIC case fails by clean stdout assertion rather than crash, restore.

Note the masking trap that motivated #237's harness field — when neutering a check, confirm the case fails for the RIGHT reason and not via a sibling branch producing the same error count with a different message. Assert on the message, not just the count.
close_reason:
PR #240 merged f51c31d. Optional userConfig option fields type-checked (sensitive/required/multiple as bool, min/max as number), and an unknown-fixture-key guard added across all 7 self-test case loops. Self-test 199 -> 205; mutation-probe now at 13 probes, all ok.

'default' deliberately NOT type-checked, with the reasoning recorded inline. Upstream's row reads 'Value used when the user provides nothing' and states no type constraint, unlike min/max's explicit 'Bounds for number type'. Enforcing that default mirrors its sibling 'type' field would need an undocumented type-to-nushell-shape mapping including guessed shapes for directory and file — schema-engine over-reach. Gate 3 fetched the live doc and confirmed the row wording.

The guard is the higher-value half: it protects every future fixture rather than one function. Its non-vacuity proof is the strongest form seen in this campaign — the same typo (expect_error_contains -> expect_errors_contains) applied to BOTH the branch and origin/main's pre-fix file: the branch failed naming the exact case, main passed silently at 199 cases / 0 failures. A differential proof, not an assertion.

The risk the guard introduced, and how it was closed: it validates fixture keys against a hardcoded list per loop, so it only works if those lists match the keys the runner ACTUALLY READS. A listed-but-never-read key would let a fixture pass the guard while its assertion silently never runs — the same bug wearing a guard's clothes. Gate 3 cross-checked all 7 lists against the consuming code in both directions with line numbers: zero dead keys, zero missing keys. expect_warning_contains, which appears in only one list and was the natural place for an aspirational key to hide, is genuinely read at 3215-3217.

Nushell trap found and fixed during the work: '$"...unknown fixture key(s)..."' parses '(s)' as a command call and crashed the whole self-test. Fixed at all 7 sites; Gate 3 then swept every interpolated string in both scripts for prose-like paren groups, using a planted '(s)' as a positive control to prove the scanner worked. Both files clean.

title: Empty strings pass every presence check in validate-plugin.nu
description:
Noted by Gate 3 during PR #236 (claude-skills-255), verified but deliberately left unfixed as out of scope.

Every presence check in validate-plugin.nu treats an empty string as present. Confirmed behaviours on main after #236:
- 'author: {name: ""}' prints the affirmative line '✓ author.name: ' with an empty value, 0 errors, 0 warnings. Worse than silent — it actively reports an empty value as correct.
- 'dependencies: [{name: "", version: "1.0.0"}]' exits 0.

The type checks added across #231, #232, #235, #236 all use is-string, and "" is a string, so none of them catch this. Note the nushell trap that makes the naive fix wrong: '42 | is-not-empty' returns TRUE, so is-not-empty is not a substitute for a type check and must be applied only after one.

Scope question to settle FIRST, before writing any check: is an empty string actually invalid for each field, or only for some? A required-ish identifier like a dependency's name is meaningless empty. An optional descriptive field may legitimately be empty in a work-in-progress manifest, and erroring there would be a false rejection — the exact class that has bitten this validator repeatedly. Upstream does not appear to address empty strings at all, so this is a judgement call about OUR validator's strictness, not a documented rule. Decide per field and record the reasoning, or decide the whole thing is not worth checking and close this with that conclusion.

Consider warning rather than error if the answer is unclear — but note #235 settled that wrong-typed values error, so a new warning-severity rule needs its own justification rather than inheriting that one.

AC: a per-field decision with recorded reasoning; checks only where empty is genuinely invalid; affirmative print gated so an empty value is never reported as correct. Reject fixture per change differing from a valid manifest in exactly one dimension. Mutation-verify each: neuter, confirm the specific case fails by clean stdout assertion rather than crash, restore. Closing this as 'not worth checking' with the per-field reasoning written down is an acceptable outcome.
close_reason:
PR #241 merged 13c5d76. The deliverable was the per-field decision, not the code: three checks added, six documented no-ops. Self-test 205 -> 210, mutation-probe 13 -> 17.

REJECT empty (identifier semantics — something else resolves against the value): dependencies[].name, dependencies[] bare-string entries, channels[].server.
ACCEPT empty, no change: description, license, $schema, displayName, homepage, repository — legitimately empty in a WIP manifest, and erroring would be the false-rejection class this file has been bitten by repeatedly. Also userConfig option title/description: upstream marks them required, but requiredness is satisfied by an empty string being PRESENT, and they are display text rather than identifiers.
ALREADY COVERED, verified by execution rather than assumed: top-level name via is-kebab-case's [a-z0-9]+ ('Invalid name format'), source.repo via a length gate ('Unsupported external source format'), top-level version via the semver warning, userConfig option type via the enum check.

The most valuable finding was a NON-change. dependencies[].version accepting empty is intentional — an empty semver range group means '*', with an existing code comment saying so. A sweep hunting silent passes would have added a check there and false-rejected documented behaviour. Gate 3 went further than our comment and verified against real node-semver: semver.satisfies('1.2.3','') returns true.

Separately, the affirmative print was fixed regardless of the strictness decision: '✓ author.name: ' on an empty value reported an empty value as correct, which is the #236 defect family (an affirmative not corresponding to what was verified). Empty still accepts with 0 errors; only the false checkmark is withheld.

Gate 3 rejected the first round on a real gap: dependencies: [""] — the bare-string form — still passed silently while {name: ""} errored. Upstream accepts both forms for that field, so it was the same empty identifier guarded in one syntactic form and not the other, and the decision table omitted the form entirely rather than recording it as a no-op. Fixed with a guard, fixture and probe, plus a table line.

Process note: the implementer wrote that fix and stalled before committing. A second agent took over the clone, independently mutation-verified the guard (neutered it and reproduced the original silent pass) rather than trusting the stalled work, and gated it. Gate 3 then ran the interaction check nobody had done across the handoff — a manifest with an empty bare dependency, an empty channels server and an empty author name produces exactly 2 errors with both messages present and no swallowing.

title: channels fixture tests a shape upstream does not document, and channels/userConfig subfield validation is still open
description:
Two related gaps left deliberately out of PR #236 (claude-skills-255), both confirmed by Gate 3 against the live upstream doc.

**1. The fixture tests nothing about channels entries.** validate-plugin.nu's pre-existing channels_array_of_objects_accepted fixture uses an entry of {type: "telegram"}. Upstream's Channels section states: 'The server field is required and must match a key in the plugin's mcpServers.' There is no documented 'type' field. That entry therefore has no valid server at all and passes only because entry content is unvalidated — what the fixture actually exercises is that an array-of-records clears the array type check, which channels_entry_server_string_accepted (added by #236, upstream-correct shape) now covers properly.

Severity today is low — no false-accept or false-reject risk — but it is a landmine: the moment a server-presence check lands, that fixture flips red and its entry needs correcting to server:. Fix the fixture in the same change as the presence check, not before.

**2. The validation that needs new machinery.** #236 took only the cheap subset — is-string on channels[].server when present. Still open, and each needs more than the existing idiom:
- channels[].server PRESENCE (upstream says required), which is what breaks the fixture above.
- The cross-field check that channels[].server matches a key in the plugin's mcpServers. This is the first validation here that spans two manifest fields.
- userConfig option records: upstream documents required 'type' (enum of exactly string/number/boolean/directory/file), required 'title', required 'description', and optional sensitive/required/default/multiple/min/max. Needs a reusable option-record validator with an enum check.
- channels[].userConfig reuses that same option schema, so the validator serves both.

AC: presence and cross-field checks for channels entries; an option-record validator covering userConfig and channels[].userConfig; the stale fixture entry corrected to the upstream shape in the same change as the presence check. Reject fixture per rule differing from a valid manifest in exactly one dimension. Mutation-verify each: neuter, confirm the specific case fails by clean stdout assertion rather than crash, restore. Prove any negative assertion is non-vacuous by first asserting absence of a string that IS present.

Watch the cross-field check specifically: a plugin with channels but mcpServers given as a STRING path (a documented shape) cannot have its server key resolved without reading that file. Decide what happens there — most likely skip the cross-check with no error rather than false-reject.
close_reason:
PR #237 merged e9bc04b. channels[].server presence + the mcpServers cross-field check, a reusable validate-user-config-option (required type/title/description, type constrained to the five-value enum) serving both top-level userConfig and channels[].userConfig, and the stale fixture corrected to the upstream server: shape. Self-test 181 -> 199.

The cross-field check skips rather than false-rejects wherever server keys are unknowable. Gate 3 built 13 manifests by hand and confirmed every branch: mcpServers absent, string, or array all skip silently; object-with-match passes; object-without-match errors. Also pushed past the enumerated shapes — array-of-records (which nushell describes as table<>, not list) skips without crashing, channels: [] passes, non-record channel entries skip, and multiple entries each report independently.

The finding worth carrying forward is a MASKING class that count-only assertions cannot detect. Neutering the server-presence branch does not change the error count — it falls through to the 'must be a string' sibling, because is-string(null) is false. Same for the type checks: 42 not-in [strings] evaluates TRUE at runtime, so the wrong-type and bad-enum branches mask each other. Six of the nine mutations kept count=1 while changing the message. Fixed by adding an expect_error_contains harness field and asserting exact messages; Gate 3 proved the new field non-vacuous in both directions — a string present nowhere fails, and a zero-error fixture does not trivially satisfy it.

Second finding, from the author mutation-testing its OWN first design: hoisting the mcp_server_keys computation above the channels check meant reverting the is-record gate crashed the in-process suite via two PRE-EXISTING unrelated fixtures (mcpServers set, no channels). That is the failure mode where one bad guard discards every queued case. Scoping the computation inside the channels-confirmed branch fixed it. A green run would never have surfaced this.

Judgement call recorded: mcpServers: {} with a channel server errors rather than skips — the strict reading of 'must match a key', since zero keys means nothing matches. Gate 3 flagged it as defensible with a clear message; revisit if a real manifest ever wants empty-inline-object to mean 'no cross-check'.

title: Two pre-existing verbose-mode validator defects: unconditional summary line and unvalidated author subfields
description:
Both found by Gate 3 on PR #235 (claude-skills-254) while enumerating the checkmark-ordering class. Both verified present on main and untouched by that PR's diff, so they are pre-existing rather than regressions.

**Defect 1 — validate-plugin.nu:420-422, unconditional success summary.** '✓ No invalid fields found' prints under --verbose even when the loop immediately above appended invalid-field errors. Reproduced: a manifest with 'category: "tools"' run with --verbose prints BOTH '✗ Invalid field category...' AND '✓ No invalid fields found', exit 1. Same contradiction symptom that #235 fixed for per-field checkmarks, but a different check — this is the summary line, so #235's per-field gating does not reach it. Gate the summary on the error list being empty.

**Defect 2 — validate-plugin.nu:611-618, author subfields entirely unvalidated.** 'author: {name: 42}' prints '✓ author.name: 42' and exits 0 with zero errors and zero warnings. Upstream documents author as an object with name, email and url; name and email are strings and url is a string URL. Nothing checks any of them.

This is the same family as claude-skills-250 and 253 — a documented field with no type validation — but one level down, on subfields of a field whose own object-ness is checked. Note the interaction with defect 1: the affirmative print fires on the unvalidated value, so a wrong-typed author.name is actively reported as correct rather than merely unreported.

AC: summary line gated on there being no invalid-field errors; author.name, author.email and author.url type-checked per upstream, with the affirmative print gated on the type check the way #235 did for description and license. Reject fixture per change differing from a valid manifest in exactly one dimension. Mutation-verify each: neuter, confirm the specific case fails by clean stdout assertion rather than crash, restore. Where a fixture asserts the ABSENCE of output, prove the negative assertion is not vacuous by first asserting absence of a string that IS present and confirming that fails — per #235's own verification of expect_output_not_contains.
close_reason:
PR #236 merged c957be2. Both defects fixed, and both FAMILIES swept rather than the two named instances — the sweep found three more.

Family 1 (affirmative checkmark printing alongside its own check's error) is closed with five sites fixed: the invalid-fields summary and author subfields (the two filed), plus SKILL.md's description-length checkmark, the marketplace-mode description checkmark, and the 'name' checkmark. Family 2 (checked object, unchecked subfields) fixed author.name/.email/.url, dependencies entry name, and channels[].server.

The methodological finding is the one worth keeping. The first sweep ran a grep over verbose print sites and still missed the 'name' checkmark, because that site HAD a gate — on a mismatch branch that is dead in direct-file mode, since plugin_name derives from plugin.name itself. A grep shaped around 'is a gate missing' cannot see 'gate present but on a branch that cannot fire'. The re-sweep reframed the question and found nothing further; Gate 3 then confirmed by a THIRD method — constructing a failing input per remaining checkmark site and asserting that checkmark suppresses while unrelated ones still print. Three independent methods, three different shapes of blindness.

Highest-risk item was dependencies, and it held: upstream documents entries as string OR object, and Gate 3 verified bare-string, mixed-array and object forms all accept while {name: 42} errors cleanly with no crash — bare strings take the string branch before any cell-path access. The marketplace-description restructure was the second risk (it merged two existing blocks rather than adding a gate); direct-file equivalence was verified, and nothing unrelated can land between the error snapshot and the gate comparison.

Self-test 163 -> 181. Every negative assertion proven non-vacuous by first asserting absence of a string that IS present.

title: version wrong-type is a warning while every sibling metadata field is an error
description:
Gate 3 nit on PR #232 (claude-skills-253). Severity inconsistency inside validate-plugin.nu, introduced by neither PR but now visible because the siblings landed.

After #232, a manifest with license set to 42 produces an ERROR (validate-plugin.nu ~562-575), while version set to 42 produces a WARNING (~494-499). Both fields are optional; both are documented string; upstream draws no distinction between them. The rule upstream states is flat: 'Fields with the wrong type still fail. For example, a keywords value that is a string instead of an array is a load error, and claude plugin validate reports it as one.'

The warning severity on version was a deliberate earlier choice (claude-skills-251) with its own justifying comment, on the reasoning that version is recommended rather than required. #232 correctly did not relitigate it. But required-ness governs whether a MISSING field is an error, not whether a WRONG-TYPED one is — those are separate questions, and the current code conflates them for version alone.

Two sub-items, and they can be decided independently:
- Align version wrong-type to ERROR, keeping missing-version as a warning. Requires updating the existing justifying comment so it stops asserting the conflated reasoning.
- Second Gate 3 nit, cosmetic and verbose-only (validate-plugin.nu:511, :544): a wrong-typed description or license prints a green check line before the type check errors, because the presence check prints first. Reorder so presence-ok only prints after the type check passes.

AC: version wrong-type severity decided and made consistent with its siblings either way, with the comment updated to match the actual reasoning; verbose-mode check-mark ordering fixed. Reject fixture per change differing from a valid manifest in exactly one dimension. Mutation-verify: neuter, confirm the specific case fails by clean stdout assertion rather than crash, restore.
close_reason:
PR #235 merged 6b6d045. version wrong-type is now an ERROR, matching all six sibling scalar fields; missing-version stays a warning. Both the inline justification and the loop exclusion note rewritten so no stale reasoning survives (grep for the old message text returns nothing). Verbose checkmark ordering fixed for description and license by gating the print on its own type check. Self-test 161 -> 163.

Gate 3 confirmed the severity reasoning empirically: all six siblings ($schema, displayName, description, homepage, repository, license) error at 582-587, so 'recommended not required' never distinguished version from them. Blast radius zero — every tracked manifest's version is already a string, and repo CI runs the script with --strict where warnings were fatal anyway, so this only tightens non-strict external use.

Two verifications worth recording. The new expect_output_not_contains machinery was proven non-vacuous by asserting absence of a string that IS present, which failed as it should — a negative assertion that never fires passes silently and pins nothing. And the severity fixture distinguishes error from warning by EXIT CODE, so reverting errors to warnings while keeping identical message text still fails it; a case asserting only '1 problem' would have passed under both.

Class closure confirmed rather than assumed: Gate 3 enumerated every verbose affirmative print in validate-plugin-content. displayName, $schema, homepage, repository and defaultEnabled have no affirmative print at all, so the two-field fix IS the complete class.

title: Seven scalar plugin.json metadata fields have no type validation
description:
Gate 3 on PR #231 (claude-skills-250) found this while verifying that PR's class-closure claim. That PR closed the component-path-fields class — all 13 rows of the upstream 'Component path fields' table are now type-checked. The scalar metadata fields are a separate, still-open subset.

In validate-plugin.nu the known-fields list at lines 433-437 also carries: $schema, displayName, homepage, repository, license, description, defaultEnabled. None has a type check. Verified by Gate 3: a manifest with displayName set to 42 passes silently — no error, no warning, exit 0.

Upstream documents all seven in the Metadata fields table: $schema, displayName, description, homepage, repository, license are string; defaultEnabled is boolean. Upstream also states plainly that wrong types are load errors — 'Fields with the wrong type still fail. For example, a keywords value that is a string instead of an array is a load error, and claude plugin validate reports it as one.' So rejecting these is upstream-faithful.

Lower severity than 250: these are scalars with no downstream typed access, so a wrong type is a silent no-op rather than a crash. Pure false-negative, no crash risk.

Two things any fix must handle, both learned the hard way on 250 and 230:
- author is an OBJECT per upstream, not a string. Do not sweep it in with the string fields.
- version is a string but already has semver validation elsewhere; check whether that path already type-guards it before adding a second check.

AC: add string type checks for $schema, displayName, description, homepage, repository, license and a bool check for defaultEnabled. Per-field reject fixture differing from a valid manifest in exactly one dimension. Mutation-verify per field: neuter, confirm that specific case fails by clean stdout assertion rather than crash, restore. These are non-crashing checks so in-process $cases is the right group — state that reasoning rather than defaulting to it.
close_reason:
PR #232 merged 3f8cd62. All seven scalar metadata fields type-checked: $schema, displayName, description, homepage, repository, license as string; defaultEnabled as boolean. author correctly excluded (object per upstream); version left alone (already guarded at 494-499). Self-test 151 -> 161.

Gate 3 tested the over-strictness lead and defeated it: $schema's 'Claude Code ignores this field at load time' describes its semantics, not its validation. Upstream's wrong-type rule sits immediately after the ignores-unrecognized-fields paragraph, and keywords is semantically unused too yet is explicitly named a load error. ERROR severity is upstream-faithful for all seven.

Gate 3 also mutation-tested the restraint argument that four fields needed no new accept fixture, in the FALSE-REJECT direction — injecting a mutant that rejects each field's own valid type. All four were genuinely covered: displayName and defaultEnabled by complete_manifest_all_documented_fields_recognized, description and license by 180 fixtures each. The reuse claim was real, not assumed.

Nushell trap recorded: a bare $schema as a record-literal key parses as variable_not_found, not a field name. Must be quoted.

title: setup-external-plugin crashes on wrong-typed fields inside a record source
description:
PR #229 added a guard rejecting a marketplace 'source' that is neither record nor string, fixing claude-skills-249. The guard admits any record, and setup-external-plugin then assumes its inner fields are strings.

Verified: source {"source":"github","repo":42} crashes uncaught with only_supports_this_input_type at a 'str length' call; repo as a list gives operator_unsupported_type. Pre-existing on main, confirmed by running main's validator against the same input.

Two related non-crash observations from the same function, worth handling in the same pass since they share a cause:
- get -o repo | default "" on a github record lacking 'repo' yields an empty repo path. No crash; the downstream is a network operation nobody has executed, so its behaviour requires analysis rather than assumption.
- The branch handling a "github:"-prefixed STRING is dead code: the function is only reachable when source is already a record.

Note the PR #229 body listed the missing-repo no-op among its known inconsistencies but did not catch that a wrong-TYPED repo actually crashes - the missing case and the mistyped case look adjacent and behave very differently.

AC: type-check the inner fields of a record source before use, per source kind (github, url, git-subdir, npm), rejecting wrong types with a clean error naming the field. Decide what an empty resolved repo path should do rather than leaving it to the network call. Remove the dead github-prefixed-string branch or make it reachable. Reject fixtures for a wrong-typed repo and a wrong-typed url, mutation-verified to fail by assertion rather than crash.
close_reason: PR #230 merged as part of the class sweep — wrong-typed fields inside a record source now type-checked. One claim in this bee was WRONG and is corrected on the record: an empty or missing repo does NOT reach an unexecuted network op; the 'str length > 0' check routes it to a clean 'Unsupported external source format' error. That claim originated in my own summary of an earlier requires-analysis flag and was upgraded into a statement of fact. The dead github-prefixed-string branch remains, noted but not removed

title: validate-plugin.nu: wrong-typed marketplace 'source' crashes at str replace
description:
On the marketplace path, a plugin entry whose name matches but whose 'source' is wrong-typed - for example source: 42 - crashes uncaught at ( | str replace --regex '^\./' ''), because str replace raises on a non-string input.

Pre-existing: the identical lines are on main, unchanged by PR #228. Found during that PR's Gate 3 class sweep rather than by the fix itself. A missing 'source' is already safe (get -o with a default).

This is the seventh distinct crash shape found in this file, and the pattern is the point: each was found by a different review round rather than by anyone sweeping the class. The earlier ones were unguarded 'open' calls; a sweep for that function name missed 'from yaml' one line later; guarding both parses missed the bare cell-path accesses; guarding the plugins list missed a record entry lacking the expected key; and this one is a string operation on unvalidated input, which is a different shape again.

AC: type-check 'source' before the str replace - it can legitimately be a string or a record per the marketplace schema, so accept both and reject other types with a clean error. Add reject fixtures for a number and a list, verified by mutation: neuter the check, confirm a case fails by clean stdout assertion rather than by crash.

Then do the sweep this file has never actually had: enumerate every operation that assumes well-formed OR well-typed input - opens, parses, cell-path accesses, string operations, list operations - and check each against a manifest crafted to violate that assumption. Searching by function name has now missed something four separate times.
close_reason: PR #229 merged — a guard now rejects any marketplace 'source' that is neither record nor string, placed before both the is_external branch and the source_dir derivation that raised on an int. Verified the guard rejects nothing legitimate: record sources still route to setup-external-plugin, strings still resolve. The fixture pins behaviour rather than exit code — neutering the guard fails one case on a stdout assertion, because nu crash output goes to stderr and cannot satisfy expect_output_contains. Residue one function downstream (wrong-typed fields INSIDE a record source) is tracked as claude-skills-252

title: validate-plugin.nu: null-check branches at 418/457/485 are unreachable dead code
description:
validate-plugin.nu guards its skills/commands/agents blocks with an outer 'if ( | get -o <field>) != null' test, then inside each block has a branch handling the case where the field's type is 'nothing'.

Those inner branches cannot fire for any file-loaded manifest. Probed during Gate 3 of PR #223: a JSON null loads through nushell's 'open' as 'nothing', and 'nothing == null' is true, so the outer guard skips the whole block before the inner branch is reached.

They surfaced because PR #223 (claude-skills-244) scoped them out as not among the eleven checks that bee named. That scoping was correct in effect - they are not a coverage gap - but wrong in kind: the right disposition is deletion, not adding fixtures for a branch that can never execute.

Adding coverage for unreachable code would be actively harmful. It would produce fixtures that pass for reasons unrelated to the branch they claim to test, which is the same wrong-reason-agreement failure this session has been removing everywhere else.

AC: confirm the unreachability independently (construct a manifest with an explicit null for each of skills, commands and agents, and verify the inner branch never executes), then delete the three branches. If any turns out to be reachable by some path - a programmatically constructed record rather than a file load, say - keep it and add a fixture exercising that actual path instead.
close_reason: PR #227 merged — all three null branches deleted after independent per-field verification. Unreachability confirmed analytically as well as empirically: in nushell 'nothing' IS null, so no value exists whose describe is 'nothing' while passing the outer '!= null' gate, including a programmatically constructed record. Deleting rather than fixturing was the right disposition — coverage for unreachable code produces tests that pass for reasons unrelated to what they claim to test

title: sources-validate-urls: a genuinely dead crate reports blocked instead of dead
description:
PR #220 added a crates.io API cross-check: a crates.io/crates/<name> URL that 404s on the website is re-checked against crates.io/api/v1/crates/<name> before being labelled. That correctly turned 13 false 'dead' entries into passes, and it cannot rescue a nonexistent crate to pass - verified by probe, and there is an additional gate requiring the API response's crate.name to equal the extracted name.

The remaining imprecision is in the other direction. When the API cross-check itself fails, the catch block discards why, so a genuine API 404 (affirmative evidence the crate does not exist) and a transient API failure both produce 'blocked - cannot confirm either way'. A genuinely dead crate therefore under-claims as blocked rather than dead.

Not dangerous: the harmful direction, a dead link silently passing, is structurally impossible here. And the note hands a reader the exact API URL to check by hand. But the API is proven reliable from this egress, so the information is available and being thrown away.

Roughly five lines: run classify-fetch-error on the caught API error text the same way check-url already does for the website call, and map no-releases to dead with a note recording that the API confirmed the 404. Anything else stays blocked.

AC: a nonexistent crate reports dead with an API-confirmed note; a transient API failure still reports blocked; both covered by self-test fixtures built from captured live error text rather than invented shapes.
close_reason: PR #222 merged — the API cross-check's own error now runs through classify-fetch-error, so a genuine API 404 reports dead with an API-confirmed note while a transient failure stays blocked. The safety property holds: a nonexistent crate never reaches pass. The tradeoff is recorded in the code — a transient API 404 for a live crate reads as affirmatively dead, with no retry, because the alternative reverts to the under-claim 242 exists to fix

title: sources:validate table truncates url and status columns in non-interactive runs
description:
mise sources:validate renders its results as a table whose url, status and notes columns truncate to '...' when run non-interactively. Setting COLUMNS to 500 or 600 has no effect - confirmed during PR #220.

Consequence: the summary line is readable ('274 checked - 270 pass | 0 dead | 1 blocked | 2 rate-limited | 1 private') but the per-row detail needed to act on it is not. Someone who sees a dead count cannot tell WHICH url is dead without working around the tool.

Both the author and the Gate 3 reviewer on PR #220 hit this and had to work around it independently - the author by scoping runs with --plugin and parsing ANSI-stripped output through python, the reviewer by being unable to extract the per-row dead list at all, which left a small discrepancy in their counts unresolved. That is the real cost: it makes the tool's own output unusable for diagnosis at exactly the moment diagnosis is needed.

Worth noting this sits under claude-skills-220's theme. An undifferentiated error bucket made a wrong attribution easy; a truncated table makes the corrected classification hard to read. Fixing the classification without fixing the display only half-solves the original problem.

AC: add a --format json or --wide flag (or emit one row per line when not a tty) so the per-row detail is retrievable without post-processing. Verify by running non-interactively and confirming a specific failing url can be identified from the output alone.
close_reason: PR #222 merged — sources-validate-urls gained --format line|json|table with line as the new default, so bare 'mise sources:validate' is grep-able with no flag to remember. Acceptance verified: a specific failing URL is identifiable from non-interactive output with no post-processing and without grep -a. Progress output routed to stderr so --format json actually parses under jq, which it did not when first submitted

title: beads: bd diff --help advertises HEAD~N refs that the implementation rejects
description:
Found while verifying beads command claims for claude-skills-223 (PR #219), against bd version 1.1.0 (8e4e59d39).

bd diff --help documents HEAD~1 and shows 'bd diff HEAD~5 HEAD' as an example. The implementation rejects that form:

    $ bd diff HEAD~1 HEAD
    Error: failed to get diff: invalid fromRef: invalid ref format: HEAD~1

Persists after explicit bd dolt commits, so it is not an empty-history artifact. Branch names and bare HEAD are accepted - 'bd diff main HEAD' returns 'No changes between main and HEAD'.

Why this is worth recording rather than just working around: a documentation author following the tool's own --help output produces a broken example and has no reason to doubt it. That is exactly what happened here - the skill's example was written from bd's help text and had to be corrected to 'bd diff main HEAD' after live testing caught it. Anyone else reading that help will hit the same thing.

This is an upstream beads defect (gastownhall/beads), not a claude-skills one. Filed here because the beads tracker is not in scope for this session. Note bd 1.1.2 is the current release and this was observed on 1.1.0 - worth re-checking against 1.1.2 before reporting upstream, in case it is already fixed.

AC: confirm against the current beads release, then either report upstream so help and implementation agree, or record here that HEAD~N is unsupported so future skill edits do not reintroduce it from the help text.
close_reason:
Closed as not-our-work per operator: we track with bees, not beads. beads is only something we PUBLISH a skill for (beads plugin v0.1.5 in the marketplace), not a tool this workspace uses.

Our side is already contained. plugins/tools/beads/skills/beads/SKILL.md:360 documents the real behaviour rather than the advertised one — 'bd diff main HEAD  # two required refs; despite --help advertising HEAD~N, that form errors live in bd 1.1.0' — corrected during the tier-1 verification pass (PR #219) and citing this bee. So no skill of ours repeats the false claim, which was the only part that was ever actionable here.

The remaining action would have been filing upstream in gastownhall/beads, which is a courtesy to a third party rather than work this workspace owes.

Two things recorded here rather than filed as new bees, since the operator has explicitly dropped this thread — they belong to whoever next touches the beads skill, not to a queue:

1. That SKILL.md line pins its claim to 'bd 1.1.0'. We are on 1.1.0; upstream released 1.1.2 on 2026-07-26, and its release notes give no changelog detail on this defect. The claim is correctly SCOPED to the version tested, so it is not false — but it is pinned to a version that is now behind, and nobody has verified whether 1.1.2 still errors. Re-check against current beads before that line is edited or the version pin moves.

2. Unrelated but adjacent, found while checking this: the beads install in ~/mise.toml pins 'github:steveyegge/beads', which resolves only because GitHub redirects that path to the renamed 'gastownhall/beads'. Works today; breaks the day anyone creates a new repo at the old path. Also note 'latest' in that pin resolved at install time — we sat at 1.1.0 while 1.1.2 shipped, so 'pinned to latest' is not self-updating. Three stale beads versions are also still installed (0.49.0, 0.63.3, 1.0.3).

title: No CI lint forbids symlinks under plugins/
description:
The skills-quality validator now reports unsafe references (broken, unreadable, external) instead of crashing on them, per claude-skills-222. Gate 3 on that PR found the external quarantine is bypassed when the SYMLINKED PATH IS AN ANCESTOR rather than the leaf - making plugins/core/skills/security/references itself a symlink to an outside directory caused the external content to be read and scanned into the corpus with no unsafe finding.

The in-PR fix canonicalizes every reference path, which closes that shape. A cheaper and broader guard is available: the repo currently contains ZERO symlinks under plugins/ (find plugins -type l returns nothing, verified twice), and nothing enforces that.

A CI lint asserting the count stays zero would make the whole class unreachable rather than handled, and would catch shapes nobody has thought of - a symlink to a device file, a symlink loop through a directory, a symlink introduced by a future contributor who has no idea the validator has opinions about them.

Weigh it against legitimate uses. AGENTS.md is a symlink to CLAUDE.md in some repos under this convention, so a blanket repo-wide ban would be wrong; scope any lint to plugins/ specifically, and decide whether templates/ needs an exception for shipped example trees.

AC: add a lint asserting no symlinks under plugins/ (or a documented allowlist), with a self-test that plants one and confirms it fires. Decide explicitly whether this replaces or complements the per-path canonicalization.
close_reason: PR #218 merged — test:no-symlinks lint added, detecting tracked symlinks under plugins/ via git ls-files mode 120000. AGENTS.md correctly out of scope. Residual documented: a local UNTRACKED symlink is invisible to the lint but self-corrects at git add, so the write-side guarantee holds for anything that ships

title: check-endoflife-status is not surfaced by sources:check, report or stale
description:
claude-skills-226 added check-endoflife-status to sources-lib.nu, returning {latest, eol, cycle} and correctly reporting eol true for a fully end-of-life product (verified live: centos gives eol true, nodejs gives eol false, parsed from the cycle's ISO eol date rather than truthiness).

It is not called by anything user-facing. Gate 3 confirmed zero callers outside sources-lib.nu apart from check-endoflife-date's internal delegation, which discards the eol field. sources-check.nu, sources-report.nu and sources-stale.nu are byte-untouched. So mise sources:check on an EOL-product source still prints the newest cycle's version with no sentinel - claude-skills-226's original symptom is unchanged in the reports.

This was accepted as legitimate scoping rather than a paper capability: 226's AC offered 'surface the cycle's eol field' as its first alternative and that is met at the library level, and the boundary is recorded explicitly in version-check-methods.md:274. The risk is that an uncalled function rots - nothing exercises it in the normal path, so a future refactor can break it without any report changing.

AC: wire the eol signal into at least one of sources:check / report / stale so an end-of-life pin is visible without calling the function by hand. Keep it distinguishable from 'behind latest', which is deliberately not a finding per claude-skills-174. Note claude-skills-176 asked for EOL detection originally, so this is the last mile of that request.
close_reason: PR #222 merged — sources-check now calls check-endoflife-status directly for endoflife-date sources and renders a separate eol column, distinct from stale. The claude-skills-174 policy is intact: in-support-but-not-latest is still not a finding, verified by classify-staleness being byte-untouched and eol feeding only the display column. Note the column is currently dormant — no real sources.toml entry uses endoflife-date yet, and adopting one artificially was deliberately declined

title: dependencies entries accept a malformed semver constraint silently
description:
validate-plugin.nu now validates the SHAPE of plugin.json dependencies entries (array of strings, or objects with a required name). It does not validate the version constraint. Verified during Gate 3 of PR #213: {"name":"x","version":"not-a-semver!!!"} is accepted with zero errors.

In scope by design for that PR — its body claimed only name-required-on-object-entries and never claimed constraint validation.

The reason it was not done matters for whoever picks this up: the repo's existing is-semver helper validates exact versions, and reusing it here would wrongly REJECT upstream's own documented example, which is a RANGE (~2.1.0). Constraint syntax is a different grammar from a version literal — it admits ~, ^, >=, and similar operators.

AC: validate the constraint as a range expression rather than an exact version. Establish the accepted operator set from upstream's own documentation rather than assuming npm or Elixir semantics, and add fixtures for each operator plus a genuinely malformed case. Do not reuse is-semver unchanged.
close_reason: PR #217 merged — dependency version constraints now validated as node-semver RANGES rather than exact versions, so upstream's own ~2.1.0 example passes. Verified against real node-semver 7.8.5 across 43 cases with zero disagreements. Note 7.8.1 and 7.8.5 differ on wildcard placement, so the pinned release is recorded in the code comment

title: Template mise.toml pins: the registered class has unregistered members
description:
PR #212 (claude-skills-230) registered the four template mise.toml pins that bee named. An independent sweep during Gate 3 found more of the same class still unregistered:

- tools/whamm/skills/whamm/templates/mise.toml: version = 0.1.0, with a comment citing the /claude-code:skill-update bump convention
- tools/sbx/skills/sbx/templates/elixir-tidewave/mise.toml: erlang 27.2, elixir 1.18.1-otp-27 — in the very template PR #212 touched for postgres:16
- tools/awman/skills/awman/templates/{0.9.1,0.10.0,0.11.0}/mise.toml and languages/zig/skills/zig/templates/{0.14.1,0.15.2,0.16.0}/mise.toml — versioned template directories, the exact class the runex intentional-pin entry now sets precedent for
- tools/slidev/skills/slidev/templates/mise.toml: node = 22

Not a defect in PR #212: bee 230 named exactly the four instances it registered, and the registry header honestly disclaims completeness. The scope was delivered as filed; the class was not closed.

Note the versioned-template directories are the interesting sub-case. A directory named after a version is plausibly a frozen snapshot, which is what runex got policy=intentional-pin for. Decide once whether that treatment generalises to awman and zig rather than case-by-case.

AC: register the remaining members or record documented exclusions. Verify each tag shape live before registering — the v-prefix is inconsistent across these upstreams (nushell has none, sbx and graphify have one).
close_reason: PR #218 merged — 10 template mise.toml pins registered (whamm, sbx erlang/elixir, awman x3, zig x3, slidev), every tag shape verified live with negative controls. Versioned-template directories get policy=intentional-pin uniformly, scoped to the tool's own version pin rather than co-located runtime pins

title: fenced-literal doc-agreement check passes when a stale second occurrence survives in the same file
description:
test/validate-fenced-literals.nu proves a registered literal exists SOMEWHERE in its file via a substring match. It does not prove the pin itself is intact.

Demonstrated during Gate 3 of PR #212: changing compose.yaml's real line to 'image: postgres:17' while a comment elsewhere in the file still mentioned postgres:16 produced a CLEAN result, exit 0. The pin drifted and the check did not notice.

Pre-existing in the mechanism, but PR #212 extends reliance on it from 21 to 27 entries across more files, including non-markdown ones where an incidental mention is likelier.

The check is deliberately format-agnostic (raw substring), which is what lets it cover Dockerfiles, compose.yaml and mise.toml with no per-format parsing. Any fix has to preserve that or accept per-format handling.

Options worth weighing: record the expected occurrence COUNT per entry and flag a change; add an optional line-anchor or surrounding-context field for entries where the literal plausibly appears more than once; or simply document the limitation in the registry header so nobody reads a clean run as proof the pin is intact.

AC: pick one and implement it, or document the limitation where a reader of the registry will see it.
close_reason: PR #218 merged — occurrences field added to fenced-literals with c2_occurrence_mismatch. The two generic literals were anchored to their keys ('node = "22"', 'erlang = "27.2"') after Gate 3 demonstrated a bare substring count is defeatable in both directions: an unrelated line containing the literal fails CI on an intact pin, and a count-preserving drift passes silently

title: Template mise.toml tool pins are outside the fenced-literal registry; nushell pin is already behind
description:
The fenced-literal registry from claude-skills-176 covers version literals inside code fences in markdown. It does not cover tool pins in template mise.toml files, which are a structurally similar staleness surface reached by a different route.

Known instances, found during Gate 3 of PR #211:
- core/skills/nushell/templates/mise.toml pins 0.111.0, while the nushell SKILL.md states current stable is 0.113.1. Already drifted, and nothing detects it.
- sbx template pins 0.30.0
- graphify template pins 0.8.36
- runex templates/0.0.7/mise.toml (versioned template directory - may be intentionally frozen, check before treating as drift)

This is a class-extension question, not a gap in what PR #211 delivered. Two things to decide:
1. Do template tool pins belong in fenced-literals.toml, or do they want their own mechanism? They are TOML values rather than fenced literals, so the registry's doc-agreement check (does the literal still appear in the file) would need a different extraction.
2. Versioned template directories like runex templates/0.0.7/ are plausibly meant to be frozen snapshots of a specific version. Freezing is legitimate and must be expressible, the same way intentional-pin is for fenced literals.

AC: decide whether to extend the registry or track these separately, and either way fix the nushell template pin, which is a live inconsistency against its own skill's stated version.
close_reason: PR #212 merged 61debb5 — extended fenced-literals.toml rather than adding a mechanism (its doc-agreement check is a format-agnostic substring match, so template mise.toml works as-is); nushell's stale 0.111.0 pin corrected to 0.113.1; sbx/graphify/runex registered with verified tag shapes. Class not closed — see the follow-up bee for unregistered members

title: postgres:16 in sbx templates is unregistered; fenced-literal registry attribution is per-file
description:
The fenced-literal registry created for claude-skills-176 registers one entry per literal per FILE - debian:13-slim correctly has two entries for its two files. postgres:16 appears in three places but is registered for only one:

- registered: core/skills/container/SKILL.md
- unregistered: tools/sbx/skills/sbx/templates/elixir-tidewave/README.md
- unregistered: tools/sbx/skills/sbx/templates/elixir-tidewave/compose.yaml

Low severity: the postgres:16 EOL date is already tracked via the container entry, so when that cycle rots the report WILL surface it. What is incomplete is per-file attribution - the report will not point a reader at the two sbx files that also need editing.

Found during Gate 3 of PR #211 by an independent fence-aware sweep run against the updated 21-entry registry.

AC: add the two sbx entries, or record why per-file attribution is not wanted for template files specifically. Note compose.yaml is not markdown, so confirm the registry's doc-agreement check handles a non-markdown file - templates/Dockerfile.claude-code is already registered, so the precedent exists.
close_reason: PR #212 merged 61debb5 — both sbx elixir-tidewave postgres:16 entries added; compose.yaml confirmed working with the raw-text doc-agreement check, proven by mutation

title: fence-freshness reports existence and EOL but not latest-vs-pinned; check-github-releases imported and unused
description:
The fence-freshness report added for claude-skills-176 classifies each registered literal as ok / eol / broken / intentional-pin / unknown. It answers 'does this target still exist, and is it end-of-life' but never shows how far behind a pin is.

Consequence: ARG MISE_VERSION=2026.5.0 badges as ok with no visible behind-ness while mise is at 2026.7.x. That is a milder echo of the complaint that motivated 176 in the first place - the bee asked for a tool that reports drift 'as a table'.

This is not a policy reversal. Not flagging in-support-but-not-latest is deliberate, carried forward from claude-skills-174 and endorsed on the bee. The gap is presentational: the fix list is correct, but the report gives the reader no way to see currency at all.

Noted during Gate 3 of PR #211: check-github-releases is already imported in fence-freshness.nu and never called, so for github-releases-backed entries the latest version is available at near-zero additional cost.

AC: add latest as an informational column for entries whose upstream can supply it, kept visually distinct from the fix list so it cannot be mistaken for a finding. Consider renaming the 'ok' badge to 'exists', which is what it actually asserts. Either use the dead import or remove it.
close_reason: PR #216 merged — informational latest= column added to fence-freshness (github-releases and docker-hub only), ok badge renamed exists. MISE_VERSION=2026.5.0 now shows latest=2026.8.1, visibly behind, still not a finding. Note the bee's dead-import premise was wrong: check-github-releases was never imported on main

title: Content-verification pass: remaining 31 of the 40 high-risk anti_fab skills
description:
Follow-up to claude-skills-204, which covered only the zig (7 skills) and wasm (wasmtime, wit) cluster of priority tier 1. This bee carries the remaining 31 skills so 204 can close without implying full coverage.

Remaining, by the priority order 204 established:

Tier 1 (rest): runex (this workspace's own product, fastest cadence), beads, bees. Note the beads INSTALL surface was corrected separately in PR #206 (claude-skills-214); its remaining API/flag claims are still unverified.

Tier 2: ansible (5 skills), slidev (8 skills).

Tier 3: design plugin (accessibility, material-design) - spec documents drift slower than CLI tools.

Method is the binding part, carried forward from 204's AC and from what the #209 review proved: not a mechanical sweep, and not a spot-check of the items a bee happens to name. The #209 reviewer sampled 21 zig claims and found 2 false ones, BOTH in the set the author had not checked - so an author-chosen sample is not evidence about the rest. Enumerate every checkable claim per skill, verify each against a live source, correct what is wrong, and add a verified-against citation only where the claim actually held.

Two failure modes from #209 to avoid explicitly:
- Never stamp verified on a code sample without establishing it compiles/type-checks at the pinned version. #209 certified a sample that passes a core linker to a function requiring a component linker.
- Check that a cited line actually supports the claim. #209 had a citation that resolved correctly to a line which refuted the sentence citing it.

AC: each of the 31 skills verified claim by claim with corrections or citations, and sources.toml/sources.md updated honestly - last_full_check means a full check, not a spot-check.
close_reason:
Complete. Final slice merged as PR #234 (d845922); slidev detail claims merged as PR #233 (e053b8f). All 40 high-risk anti_fab skills now verified claim-by-claim across four PRs (#219 tier 1, #225 ansible + slidev partial, #233 slidev detail, #234 ansible-inventory azure/gcp + tier 3).

The finding that matters most for future passes: EVERY ONE of the four slices produced corrections that were themselves wrong, caught only because Gate 3 verified the corrections rather than just the original claims.
- #219: 2 of its corrections wrong (ID format contradicted by the PR's own captured sample; bd export documented as writing a file when it streams to stdout).
- #233: 2 wrong. Declared slidev.highlighter a fabricated field — it is real, declared in SlidevThemeMeta (types.ts:82-86) and consumed in config.ts:66-77, merely undocumented in write-theme.md. And replaced a broken CSS fix with a no-op: #frame { border: none } removes a border that does not exist, since every deck loads @unocss/reset/tailwind.css zeroing border-width deck-wide.
- #234: an INVERTED WCAG claim — shipped 'every 2.1-conformant page also conforms to 2.2' where W3C states the exact reverse ('Content that conforms to WCAG 2.2 also conforms to WCAG 2.0 and WCAG 2.1'), self-refuting given the same text conceded 2.2 adds 9 new SC. Plus '13 tones' enumerated with 14 values, and '35 named patterns' where the APG index has 30 — fabricated precision inside a sentence claiming index verification.
- #225 was the exception on corrections but produced the self-contradiction pattern instead: a correct fix that left a references/ file teaching the old schema while SKILL.md linked it uncaveated.

Two method rules earned across the campaign, worth applying to any future verification work:
1. A correction carries the same evidentiary burden as the claim it replaces. Verify BOTH directions — is the original actually wrong, and is the replacement actually right.
2. The author's own cross-file grep is not reliable. It missed 3 live sites on #233 and undercounted 2-vs-5 on #234's WCAG sweep. Independent re-grep at a wider scope caught both.

Bookkeeping honesty held throughout: ansible last_full_check deliberately NOT bumped (molecule-scenarios.md still unverified); design bumped, both skills genuinely covered. Two upstream defects filed separately as claude-skills-239 (runex) and claude-skills-240 (beads).

comments.text:
PR #219 merged — runex, beads and bees verified claim-by-claim, completing priority tier 1. Beads needed 11 corrections (commands, flags and JSON schemas that did not exist); runex needed 2 (driver list was 8 of 14, workflow resolution was 3 roots of 4); bees needed none. Gate 3 then found TWO of the corrections were themselves wrong (the ID format claimed 4 hex chars where live output is 3-char base36, contradicted by the PR's own captured sample; and bd export was documented as writing a file when it streams to stdout) — both fixed. A third, bd diff HEAD~N, was written from the tool's own --help and errors live; that is upstream, filed as claude-skills-240, along with claude-skills-239 for a runex execution_class/1 guard mismatch.

Still open under this bee: tier 2 (ansible x5, slidev x8) and tier 3 (accessibility, material-design) — 31 of the 40 skills.

One constraint for whoever takes the next slice: beads/SKILL.md is now at exactly 500/500 lines, so the next edit to it fails CI without a references/ split first. Candidates identified during this pass: the Task Hierarchies section (~35 lines) or Skills-Aware Task Creation (~35 lines), both following the externalization pattern already used for workflow-examples.md and ide-integration.md in that same file.

Method note worth carrying forward: bees held on all six re-sampled behaviours while beads collapsed on 11 — the reviewer's read is that this reflects prior verification depth (bees got a dedicated 12-behaviour pass in PR #151, beads only a storage-level one) rather than intrinsic documentation quality.

PR #225 merged — tier 2 delivered as a FULL pass on ansible (all 5 skills) and a PARTIAL pass on slidev.

Ansible was verified against a live-installed toolchain (ansible-core 2.21.2, molecule 26.6.0, ansible-lint 26.6.0, pytest-testinfra 10.2.2, amazon.aws 11.4.0, community.hashi_vault 7.1.0) rather than against docs. Nine corrections, several of which were inverted rather than merely imprecise: default('x') and default('x', boolean=true) had their semantics exactly backwards; flatten's default flattens ALL levels, not one; path_join rejects the documented positional form entirely; molecule lint does not exist as a command; --driver-name does not exist; and molecule.yml's top-level schema is entirely different from what was documented. Gate 3 re-ran every one against the same toolchain and confirmed all nine in both directions, plus nine samples from the confirmed-correct list. No falsification found — unlike tier 1, where two corrections were themselves wrong.

Slidev got five corrections verified against slidevjs/slidev source (exportFilename default, mdc deprecated in favour of comark, clicks auto-calculated rather than defaulting to 0, colorSchema missing 'all', routerMode missing 'memory'), plus an alias-direction swap. Its last_full_check was deliberately NOT bumped, since the pass covered headmatter/frontmatter schema, layout and component names, and the CLI surface — not the per-skill detail claims in code/export/interactive/presentations/styles/troubleshooting.

Gate 3's one finding is worth recording as a pattern: the correction was right and left the skill self-contradicting. references/molecule-scenarios.md still taught the old schema and the non-existent --driver-name flag, while SKILL.md linked it uncaveated as the complete annotated reference. Fixed with a schema-drift caveat citing the live errors, a softened References line, and the file added to the sources.toml unverified list.

REMAINING under this bee: tier 2's slidev detail claims (six skills), ansible-inventory's Azure RM and GCP Compute sections, and all of tier 3 (accessibility, material-design).

title: beads: bare 'go install' command shape is unsupported upstream; mise backend and docs URL are stale
description:
Three findings from the Gate 3 review of PR #191, all pre-existing and left out of that PR's scope.

1. installation.md ships a bare 'go install github.com/steveyegge/beads/cmd/bd@latest'. Upstream documents exactly two supported go-install modes, both requiring an env prefix: CGO_ENABLED=0 (server-mode only, no embedded Dolt, needs an external sql-server and a --server init) and CGO_ENABLED=1 with GOFLAGS=-tags=gms_pure_go (embedded-capable). The shipped form is neither. Upstream also advises preferring Homebrew, npm, or the install script unless go install is specifically needed. The MODULE PATH is correct and should stay — released modules still declare the steveyegge path for compatibility, stated verbatim in upstream's installation doc.

title: hex-pm and crates-io fetch errors fall through to a bare catch; 429 undistinguished
description:
PR #197 added classify-fetch-error to distinguish a dead feed (404) from rate limiting (403) for github-releases, matching on nushell's parenthesised status rendering. Verified against real nu 0.113.1: 403 renders 'Access forbidden (403)' and 404 renders 'Requested file not found (404)', while 401/429/500 take a generic form with no parens — so the heuristic is precisely aligned, and the failure direction is safe (unknown shapes degrade to generic 'error' rather than a confident misclassification).

Two gaps remain: hex-pm and crates-io still use a bare catch { "error" } with no classification, and GitHub's 429 secondary rate limit lands in generic error rather than rate-limited.

Live evidence: a transient crates.io throttle during review surfaced as '1 check error', confirming non-GitHub fetch failures are currently indistinguishable from any other failure.

AC: classify hex-pm and crates-io errors on the same axes; distinguish 429 from generic error.

title: Boundary test needs a fourth stays-prescriptive category: quoted source material
description:
The boundary test in claude-code/skills/claude-skills/references/context-engineering-claude-5.md names three reasons a prescription stays prescriptive: removing it would break a check, permit a fabrication, or rely on an agent recognising a need it does not yet have.

claude-skills-146's rule-by-rule pass found a fourth that the test does not name. twelve-factor SKILL.md:252 is a verbatim blockquote from 12factor.net. It is not eligible for softening at all — altering a direct quotation is a fabrication risk in the opposite direction, regardless of how the three existing clauses score it.

Found by applying the standard, which is the best evidence it is a real gap rather than a hypothetical one.

title: Settle CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT notation repo-wide — bare vs angle-bracket is split
description:
Two notations are now in use for the same variable with no single documented convention. The claude-code plugin uses CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT bare and documents that choice twice (claude-hooks/SKILL.md:37, claude-plugins/SKILL.md:71). agent-sandboxing uses the angle-bracket form after PR #190. Angle brackets ARE house style — but for CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR, a different variable.

Both are safe (neither expands at load time). This is consistency, not correctness.

AC: pick one form for CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT in bodies, document it in the claude-skills skill alongside the existing CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR guidance, and apply it repo-wide.
close_reason: PR #210 merged 7fe2a66. The bee's premise overstated the drift: the repo already followed a coherent implicit convention (bare backtick-name when NAMING the variable, angle-bracket when showing it embedded in runnable syntax), matching the CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR precedent — independently confirmed with zero counter-examples across all 6 bare and 13 angle-bracket CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR references. Of 9 bare CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT occurrences, 8 were definitional and already correct; converting them would have CREATED an inconsistency. Exactly one genuine conflict existed (claude-plugins/SKILL.md:83, bare inside a runnable JSON hooks example) and was fixed. The convention is now documented explicitly as a three-tier rule in claude-skills/SKILL.md, and CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT was added as a fourth CLAUDE_* substitution variable — its load-time expansion empirically confirmed. The claude-hooks:37 and claude-plugins:90 sites the bee cited as evidence of a split are definitional mentions consistent with the settled rule and correctly needed no change. One edit IS the repo-wide application.

title: Content-verification pass for the 40 high-risk anti_fab skills
description:

The remaining 40 document an external or internal tool's flags, versions, API surface, or config keys and need a claim-by-claim verification pass against upstream — not a pointer. title: Commit the relocated vantageex-conventions.md in the vantage_ex repo
description:
PR #153 removed docs/vantageex-conventions.md from claude-skills after relocating it to ~/github/vantage_ex/docs/vantageex-conventions.md (byte-identical, shasum ba62b2642901efef1d8f3083951015bfa3419ceb on both). It was left UNTRACKED there because vantage_ex had work in progress on branch docs/loop-handoff-k3s-topology — committing would have mixed an unrelated doc into that branch.

So the only COMMITTED copy is now claude-skills git history (commit 4fc712f, and the deletion in #153). That is recoverable indefinitely since #153 was a plain deletion with no history rewrite, but the working copy in vantage_ex is one 'git clean' away from loss.

Do: once that branch's WIP clears, commit docs/vantageex-conventions.md in vantage_ex. Consider whether it belongs as its own file or merged into the existing docs/bundle-authoring-conventions.md, which is its sibling pattern — both are project conventions for that codebase.

Context on why it moved: the file states in its own opening that its conventions 'apply to agents working on VantageEx epics and are not part of the universal /linear:plan-epic or /linear:audit-epics skills'. It arrived in claude-skills by riding along in PR #110 (epic-sizing heuristics for the linear skill), was never touched again, and nothing referenced it.
close_reason:
vantage_ex PR #162 merged eb91de2. docs/vantageex-conventions.md is now tracked in vantage_ex; the only committed copy is no longer claude-skills git history.

The blocker was the shared working tree, not the doc — vantage_ex is STILL on docs/loop-handoff-k3s-topology with 12 dirty entries. Built the commit with git plumbing against origin/main instead of waiting: hash-object for the blob, read-tree into a TEMP index via GIT_INDEX_FILE, update-index, write-tree, commit-tree, then push the object to a new branch. No checkout, no staging, no HEAD move. Verified after that the branch and all 12 dirty entries were untouched. That is the general answer for committing to a repo whose tree is busy, and it is worth reusing.

Three gates: local CI exit 0 (run in a FRESH CLONE of the PR branch — running it in the shared tree would have tested the WIP branch's code, not the PR, and a green there would have been meaningless), remote CI green, Gate 3 fable APPROVE WITH NITS.

Gate 3 verified the byte-identity claim independently — both blobs shasum ba62b264..., including the trailing newline — and confirmed the plumbing produced a tree of main plus exactly ONE added path with nothing silently dropped, checking the tree-level diff rather than just the file list.

Kept as its own file rather than merged into docs/bundle-authoring-conventions.md. Gate 3 confirmed no overlap: zero other hits for the adjunct pattern anywhere in the repo, and the two docs cover different subjects.

The doc's own 'never edit, commit, or push inside vantage_ex' rule is NOT contradicted by this. Gate 3 argued both sides and found the constraint properly scoped to the read-only ADJUNCT usage — agents referencing this repo while working other epics — with line 23 explicitly routing needed changes to a separate issue, which is the path this PR took.

Content nits found but deliberately NOT fixed here, because fixing them would have broken the byte-identity provenance that was this PR's whole contract. Filed as claude-skills-260.

title: pm agents still imply bees prime returns issue data
description:
Left as a follow-up by Gate 3 on PR #151 rather than widening a 12-file PR to 14.

plugins/pm/agents/pm-discovery.md:40 and plugins/pm/agents/pm-lead.md:94 list 'bees prime' in the bees-map command surface with wording that implies it contributes issue data — 'List each issue's id, title, status ... as returned by these commands'. PR #151 established and verified that prime returns NO issue data at all: 58 lines of static agent-workflow cheatsheet, zero issue-id mentions in a repo holding four issues. The bees-to-spec.md reference these agents defer to was corrected in #151 and now says so; the agent files were not.

Harmless in practice — prime is read-only and the other commands in the same list (bees list --json, bees show --json) do supply the data, so the shard still gets what it needs. But the wording tells an agent to expect issue data from a command that never returns any, which is the same false-expectation class #151 removed everywhere else.

Fix: drop 'bees prime' from the 'as returned by these commands' enumeration in both files, or move it to a separate line noting it returns workflow context rather than issues. Two one-line edits plus a pm version bump.
